The constant is best possible, even within the class of closed manifolds: it is attained identically by an explicit self-similar solution in flat $\Rn$, and its sharpness transfers to the compact setting through a large-torus limit along the flat tori $\mathbb R^n/(L\mathbb Z)^n$, $L 	o \infty$. The proof rests on an exact Bochner-type identity for a family of uniformly parabolic approximating flows in which the second-order regularization and the first-order eikonal term are decoupled: for this family the maximum principle applies with the sharp constant, uniformly in the regularization parameter, and with no assumption on the critical set of the solution. The identity is moreover form-invariant under the classical $α$-relaxation of the Li-Yau functional; as a consequence we also obtain the corresponding inequality on closed manifolds with $\operatorname{Ric} \ge -κ$ (again with no assumption beyond the Ricci lower bound), and, on complete noncompact manifolds with $\operatorname{Ric} \ge 0$, the sharp inequality for the approximating flows -- again with no assumption on the critical set -- under a cutoff hypothesis on the distance function (automatic in $\Rn$, and, for $p \ge 2$, under nonnegative sectional curvature) and a qualitative polynomial growth condition on the Li-Yau quantity, satisfied, with exponent zero, by the extremal profile. A sharp global Harnack inequality follows.

AI.tldr: This paper proves a sharp nonlinear version of the Li-Yau inequality for positive solutions of the normalized parabolic p-Laplacian equation on closed Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature, establishing the best possible constant via an explicit self-similar solution and extending results to κ-Ricci bounded and complete noncompact settings.
AI.motivation: To extend the classical Li-Yau inequality to the nonlinear setting of the normalized parabolic p-Laplacian and determine the sharp (best possible) constant, while handling the technical challenges posed by the equation's degeneracy on the critical set of the solution.
AI.method: The proof uses an exact Bochner-type identity for a family of uniformly parabolic approximating flows that decouple second-order regularization from the first-order eikonal term, allowing the maximum principle to apply with the sharp constant uniformly in the regularization parameter and without assumptions on the critical set. The identity is form-invariant under the α-relaxation of the Li-Yau functional. Sharpness is shown through an explicit self-similar solution on flat R^n and transferred to compact settings via a large-torus limit.
AI.result: A sharp nonlinear Li-Yau inequality is established with the optimal constant, attained by an explicit self-similar solution in flat space. The inequality extends to closed manifolds with Ric ≥ -κ and to complete noncompact manifolds with Ric ≥ 0 under a cutoff hypothesis and polynomial growth condition, yielding a sharp global Harnack inequality as a consequence.
AI.conclusion: The sharp nonlinear Li-Yau inequality for the normalized parabolic p-Laplacian holds in full generality on closed manifolds and in a robust setting on noncompact manifolds, with the constant proven best possible across all cases considered.

title: High-Order-Accurate Continuity Enforcing Nyström Discretization of 3D Maxwell Combined Field Integral Equations
summary: In Nyström-collocation discretizations of the electric field integral equation (EFIE), the surface divergence acts on surface densities that may be discontinuous across patch boundaries, which degrades accuracy and convergence. We show that this not only affects the EFIE but every formulation in which the operator occurs, either in the equation itself or in the scattered field computation, and propose a high-order-accurate continuity-enforcing scheme for smooth surfaces as a remedy for the direct and indirect EFIEs, magnetic field integral equations (MFIEs), and regularized combined field integral equations (CFIEs) alike. The scheme comprises two ingredients: i) We show how to discretize the equations via a Chebyshev-based Nyström scheme, which admits closed quadrature rules. ii) Since unknowns and test vectors are in terms of patch-local curvilinear bases, continuity is enforced by a change of basis: we construct sparse mapping matrices assembled solely from the curvilinear geometry description. In doing so, we restore the accuracy of the EFIE such that it can be combined with the MFIEs with equal weights to form CFIEs. Numerical studies for the scattering from canonical and realistic geometries show that all considered formulations individually and combined benefit from the continuity enforcement in terms of better conditioning, reduced iterations of an iterative solver, and several more digits of accuracy in the scattered fields, despite reducing the total number of unknowns.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the accuracy degradation in Nyström-collocation discretizations of the EFIE caused by discontinuous surface densities across patch boundaries, and proposes a high-order continuity-enforcing scheme based on Chebyshev quadrature and sparse change-of-basis mapping matrices that restores accuracy across EFIE, MFIE, and CFIE formulations.
AI.motivation: In Nyström-collocation discretizations of the EFIE, the surface divergence acts on densities that may be discontinuous across patch boundaries, degrading accuracy and convergence. This problem affects not only the EFIE but all formulations where the operator appears, either in the equation or in scattered field computation.
AI.method: The scheme has two components: (i) discretizing equations via a Chebyshev-based Nyström scheme with closed quadrature rules; (ii) enforcing continuity through a change of basis using sparse mapping matrices assembled solely from the curvilinear geometry description, since unknowns and test vectors are in patch-local curvilinear bases.
AI.result: Numerical studies on canonical and realistic geometries show all considered formulations benefit from continuity enforcement: better conditioning, reduced iterative solver iterations, and several more digits of accuracy in scattered fields, despite reducing total unknowns.
AI.conclusion: Continuity enforcement restores EFIE accuracy, enabling equal-weight combination with MFIEs to form CFIEs while improving conditioning, convergence, and accuracy across all formulations.

title: Enhanced Extreme Ultraviolet Emission from Laser-heated Blow-Off Tin Plasmas
summary: This work investigates extreme ultraviolet (EUV) emission at 13.5 nm from laser produced tin plasmas generated using a mass limited laser blow off (LBO) plume.

AI.tldr: This paper studies extreme ultraviolet (EUV) emission at 13.5 nm from laser-produced tin plasmas generated using a mass-limited laser blow-off (LBO) plume.
AI.motivation: To investigate EUV emission at 13.5 nm from tin plasmas, which is relevant for EUV lithography applications, using a mass-limited laser blow-off approach to control plasma conditions.
AI.method: Laser-produced tin plasmas are generated using a mass-limited laser blow-off (LBO) plume configuration.
AI.result: The study characterizes EUV emission at 13.5 nm from the resulting tin plasmas.
AI.conclusion: The investigation explores EUV emission properties from mass-limited laser blow-off tin plasmas, relevant to EUV lithography source development.

title: Analysis validation of a new continuum model for the evolution of grain boundaries in polycrystalline materials
summary: To describe the evolution of grain boundaries based on the underlying microscopic mechanisms of line defects (disconnections) and the integrated effects of a diverse range of thermodynamic driving forces, Zhang, et al. in 2017 formulated a continuum equation. We prove the global-in-time existence, uniqueness, and regularity of the weak solution to an initial-boundary value problem for this model. The existence, uniqueness of the stationary solution are also established. Finally, we investigate the large-time behavior of the weak solution of the evolution problem, and show that the solution converges to the stationary solution in a suitable sense. Numerical simulations are carried out to validate the analysis results. The main difficulties in the proof of main theorems are due to a non-local term with singularity, a non-smooth coefficient of the highest derivative associated with the gradient of the unknown, and the special form of free energy which is not uniformly bounded from below. The key ingredients in the proof are the energy method, an estimate for a singular integral of the Hilbert type, Fourier transform of Hilbert transformations, and an estimate with a weight, for time-derivative of the unknown.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a rigorous mathematical analysis of a continuum equation for grain boundary evolution proposed by Zhang et al. (2017), proving global-in-time existence, uniqueness, and regularity of weak solutions to an initial-boundary value problem, as well as existence/uniqueness of stationary solutions and convergence of the time-dependent solution to the stationary state. Numerical simulations validate the analytical findings.
AI.motivation: Grain boundary evolution is governed by complex microscopic mechanisms involving line defects (disconnections) and various thermodynamic driving forces. A continuum equation was formulated by Zhang et al. in 2017, but its mathematical well-posedness—existence, uniqueness, and regularity of solutions—had not been rigorously established, which is essential for both theoretical understanding and reliable numerical computation.
AI.method: The authors employ energy methods combined with estimates for singular Hilbert-type integrals, Fourier transform techniques for Hilbert transformations, and weighted estimates for time-derivatives of the unknown. These tools address three main difficulties: a non-local term with singularity, a non-smooth coefficient on the highest derivative involving the gradient of the unknown, and a free energy functional that is not uniformly bounded from below.
AI.result: The authors prove global-in-time existence, uniqueness, and regularity of weak solutions to the initial-boundary value problem for the grain boundary evolution model. They also establish existence and uniqueness of stationary solutions, and demonstrate that the weak solution converges to the stationary solution in an appropriate sense over large time. Numerical simulations corroborate the theoretical results.
AI.conclusion: The mathematical foundation for the Zhang et al. (2017) grain boundary evolution model is fully established, confirming its well-posedness and correct long-time asymptotic behavior, thereby validating the model as a reliable framework for describing grain boundary dynamics.

title: Characteristic Mode Analysis of Composite Nanostructures using a Coupled System of Volume Integral and Hydrodynamic Equations
summary: Full-structure and sub-structure characteristic mode analysis (CMA) formulations are developed for composite metallic--dielectric nanostructures based on a coupled system of volume integral equations (VIE) and the hydrodynamic equation (HDE). In the full-structure CMA, the generalized eigenvalue equation (GEE) is constructed from the matrix of the complete coupled system, and the resulting characteristic currents describe the response of the entire composite nanostructure. In the sub-structure CMA, the GEE is constructed from a reduced system, derived from the coupled system by eliminating the dielectric-region unknowns, so that it is expressed only in terms of the metallic-region currents. This isolates the resonances of the metallic region while still incorporating the effect of the dielectric region through the reduced system. Because the reduced system has a smaller dimension, the sub-structure CMA is computationally more efficient than the full-structure CMA and, when the dielectric does not resonate in the frequency range of interest, identifies the same resonances. Both formulations are validated against extinction cross-section (ECS) results and are used to characterize how a dielectric environment reshapes the metallic resonances, including substrate-induced red-shifts and, for high-contrast substrates in direct contact, hybridized modal responses.

AI.tldr: This paper develops two characteristic mode analysis (CMA) formulations for composite metallic-dielectric nanostructures using a coupled volume integral equation (VIE) and hydrodynamic equation (HDE) system. The full-structure CMA analyzes the entire composite, while the sub-structure CMA reduces the system to only metallic-region currents, offering computational efficiency while still capturing dielectric effects. Both are validated against extinction cross-section results and used to characterize dielectric-induced reshaping of metallic resonances.
AI.motivation: To enable systematic analysis and characterization of resonances in composite metallic-dielectric nanostructures, which are important for nanophotonics applications but are challenging to analyze with existing CMA approaches that typically handle purely metallic or purely dielectric structures.
AI.method: Two CMA formulations are developed: (1) full-structure CMA, where a generalized eigenvalue equation (GEE) is constructed from the full coupled VIE-HDE system matrix, yielding characteristic currents for the entire composite; and (2) sub-structure CMA, where the GEE is built from a reduced system obtained by eliminating dielectric-region unknowns, isolating metallic resonances with reduced computational dimension.
AI.result: Both formulations are validated against extinction cross-section (ECS) results. The sub-structure CMA is computationally more efficient due to its smaller dimension and identifies the same resonances as the full-structure CMA when the dielectric does not resonate in the frequency range of interest. The methods characterize dielectric-induced effects including substrate-induced red-shifts and hybridized modal responses for high-contrast substrates in direct contact.
AI.conclusion: The sub-structure CMA provides an efficient alternative to full-structure CMA for analyzing metallic resonances in composite nanostructures, preserving dielectric effects via the reduced system while reducing computational cost. Both approaches effectively reveal how dielectric environments reshape metallic resonances in composite nanostructures.

title: A General Superconvergence Result for Cubature on Triangulated Polygonal Domains
summary: Cubature rules, which approximate definite integrals as a linear combination of a set of function values, are ubiquitous and necessary for computational methods in the physical sciences. A superconvergence result for cubature rules on polygonal domains is developed, whereby a rule that is exact for all bivariate polynomials of a fixed even degree realize an extra order of convergence under a decrease in the spacing between nodes.

AI.tldr: A superconvergence result for cubature rules on polygonal domains is established, showing that rules exact for bivariate polynomials of a fixed even degree achieve an extra order of convergence as node spacing decreases.
AI.motivation: Cubature rules are essential for computational methods in the physical sciences, yet their convergence behavior—particularly the possibility of enhanced (super)convergence—is not fully understood for polygonal domains.
AI.method: The paper develops a theoretical superconvergence result for cubature rules on polygonal domains, demonstrating that rules exact for all bivariate polynomials of a fixed even degree gain an additional order of convergence when the spacing between nodes is reduced.
AI.result: A superconvergence result is established: cubature rules exact for bivariate polynomials of a fixed even degree on polygonal domains realize an extra order of convergence under node spacing refinement.
AI.conclusion: The findings show that cubature rules on polygonal domains can exhibit superconvergence—beyond what is expected from their polynomial exactness—when the degree of exactness is even, providing a theoretical foundation for improved numerical integration in physical sciences.

title: Unified Gas-Kinetic Wave-Particle Method for Multiscale Simulation of Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System
summary: A unified gas-kinetic wave--particle method with Fokker--Planck collisions (UGKWP-FP) is developed for the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck system. The collision operator is modeled by the Lenard--Bernstein operator, whose stochastic representation corresponds to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process in velocity space. To extend the UGKWP framework beyond the conventional Bhatnagar--Gross--Krook (BGK) collision model, the Fokker--Planck operator is decomposed into a nonstiff drift--diffusion contribution and a stiff thermalization contribution. The former is retained in the particle dynamics through a modified Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, whereas the latter is represented by a BGK-type relaxation toward the local Maxwellian. This decomposition enables an adaptive wave--particle representation: the method follows stochastic particle dynamics in rarefied regimes and increasingly represents the rapidly equilibrating distribution by the analytical wave component as the continuum regime is approached. The modified friction coefficient is constructed to recover the original Fokker--Planck dynamics in the rarefied limit while preserving the hydrodynamic limit under strong collisions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method captures velocity-space drift and diffusion, recovers the expected kinetic and continuum behavior across a range of Knudsen numbers, and reproduces the characteristic evolution of collisional plasma phenomena.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a unified gas-kinetic wave-particle method with Fokker-Planck collisions (UGKWP-FP) for the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system, decomposing the collision operator into nonstiff and stiff parts to enable adaptive wave-particle representation across rarefied and continuum regimes.
AI.motivation: Extend the unified gas-kinetic wave-particle (UGKWP) framework beyond the conventional Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK) collision model to handle the Fokker-Planck collision operator (via the Lenard-Bernstein operator), enabling accurate simulation of Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck systems across different Knudsen numbers.
AI.method: The Fokker-Planck operator is decomposed into a nonstiff drift-diffusion part and a stiff thermalization part. The drift-diffusion part is handled through a modified Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process in particle dynamics, while the thermalization part is represented by BGK-type relaxation toward the local Maxwellian. A modified friction coefficient recovers original Fokker-Planck dynamics in rarefied limits and preserves hydrodynamic limits under strong collisions.
AI.result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the method captures velocity-space drift and diffusion, recovers expected kinetic and continuum behavior across a range of Knudsen numbers, and reproduces characteristic evolution of collisional plasma phenomena.
AI.conclusion: The UGKWP-FP method successfully extends the wave-particle framework to Fokker-Planck-type collisions, providing an adaptive representation that follows stochastic particle dynamics in rarefied regimes and uses analytical wave components in continuum regimes.

title: Schauder estimates for the linearized very fast diffusion equations in bounded domains
summary: We establish Schauder estimates for linearized very fast diffusion equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions in bounded smooth domains. These estimates provide an important ingredient for deriving optimal boundary regularity and long-time dynamics of solutions to very fast diffusion equations.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes Schauder estimates for linearized very fast diffusion equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions in bounded smooth domains, providing a key ingredient for optimal boundary regularity and long-time dynamics of solutions.
AI.motivation: Schauder estimates are needed for linearized very fast diffusion equations to derive optimal boundary regularity and long-time dynamics of solutions to very fast diffusion equations.
AI.method: The paper derives Schauder estimates for the linearized very fast diffusion equation subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions in bounded smooth domains.
AI.result: Schauder estimates are established for the linearized very fast diffusion equations, serving as an important ingredient for optimal boundary regularity and long-time dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The established Schauder estimates provide a crucial foundation for analyzing boundary regularity and long-time behavior of very fast diffusion equations in bounded smooth domains.

title: A wide-range temperature-dependent deep potential for sodium with near-experimental accuracy from melting to the critical point
summary: We construct temperature-dependent deep potentials for sodium using finite-temperature DFT data obtained with the PBE, AM05, and $r^2$SCAN exchange-correlation functionals and investigate the thermophysical properties of sodium from room temperature to the critical region. The predicted critical parameters show a dependence on the exchange-correlation functional. The model based on the $r^2$SCAN functional gives a critical temperature $T_c=2.508(8)$ kK, density $ρ_c=0.203(4)$ g/cm$^{3}$, and pressure $P_c=0.249(6)$ kbar, in close agreement with the recommended values. This model is then used to reconstruct the normal-pressure and critical isobars and to calculate the enthalpy, heat capacities, thermal expansion coefficient, bulk moduli, Grüneisen parameter, and speed of sound. The calculated normal-pressure bcc density differs by only 0.06% from the experimental value. Direct solid-liquid coexistence simulations give a melting temperature of $346(2)$ K, 25 K below the recommended value, consistent with the sensitivity expected from meV/atom free-energy errors. Liquid-vapor coexistence simulations reproduce the binodal and yield a surface tension that approaches zero near the critical point. The calculated self-diffusion coefficient and shear viscosity extend the available transport-property data into the expanded-liquid and near-critical regions, where direct experimental information is sparse. We also demonstrate the thermodynamic consistency of the results by comparing the speed of sound obtained from direct acoustic simulations with that calculated from the equation of state.

AI.tldr: Authors construct temperature-dependent deep potentials for sodium using finite-temperature DFT data with three exchange-correlation functionals (PBE, AM05, r2SCAN) and investigate its thermophysical properties from room temperature to the critical region. The r2SCAN-based model gives critical parameters in close agreement with recommended values and is used to compute a wide range of thermodynamic, transport, and coexistence properties.
AI.motivation: To develop accurate machine-learned interatomic potentials for sodium that can reliably predict thermophysical properties across a wide temperature range, especially in the expanded-liquid and near-critical regions where experimental data is sparse.
AI.method: Temperature-dependent deep potentials trained on finite-temperature DFT data from PBE, AM05, and r2SCAN functionals; validated via direct solid-liquid and liquid-vapor coexistence simulations, acoustic simulations for speed of sound, and comparison of multiple thermophysical properties against experimental data.
AI.result: The r2SCAN-based model yields critical temperature 2.508 kK, density 0.203 g/cm3, and pressure 0.249 kbar, closely matching recommended values. Normal-pressure bcc density differs by only 0.06% from experiment. Melting temperature is 346 K (25 K below recommended). The model extends transport-property data into expanded-liquid and near-critical regions and shows thermodynamic consistency in speed of sound calculations.
AI.conclusion: The r2SCAN-based deep potential provides accurate predictions of sodium's thermophysical properties across a wide range, with small systematic deviations (e.g., in melting temperature) consistent with expected free-energy errors from meV/atom-level DFT accuracy.

title: A GPU-Accelerated Blocked Adaptive Randomized Range Finder Based on an Implicit Householder QR Decomposition
summary: Low-rank methods can reduce the memory and computational requirements of deep neural network training in approaches such as GaLore. Randomized range finders offer an attractive alternative to singular value decompositions, particularly when the required rank is determined adaptively from a prescribed approximation tolerance. We introduce a blocked adaptive randomized range finder based on an implicit Householder QR decomposition and an optimized hybrid CPU--GPU implementation. The proposed method avoids explicit reorthogonalization. Numerical experiments show that it preserves orthogonality and approximation accuracy in regimes where block Gram--Schmidt without reorthogonalization becomes unstable. The blocked formulation exposes matrix--matrix operations and enables overlap of CPU panel factorization with GPU updates. On an NVIDIA GH200, the overlapped implementation reduces the runtime for the largest tested matrix from 9.91 seconds on the CPU to 0.407 seconds. The method provides a stable and efficient building block for low-rank approximation on heterogeneous systems with applications in computational science and engineering.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a blocked adaptive randomized range finder based on implicit Householder QR decomposition with an optimized hybrid CPU-GPU implementation for low-rank approximation in deep neural network training. The method avoids explicit reorthogonalization, preserves orthogonality and accuracy where block Gram-Schmidt fails, and achieves a 24x speedup on NVIDIA GH200 hardware.
AI.motivation: Low-rank methods like GaLore reduce memory and computational costs in deep learning training, but existing randomized range finders need a stable and efficient implementation that is adaptive in rank and works well on heterogeneous (CPU-GPU) systems. Block Gram-Schmidt without reorthogonalization becomes numerically unstable in certain regimes.
AI.method: The paper proposes a blocked adaptive randomized range finder built on an implicit Householder QR decomposition, with an optimized hybrid CPU-GPU implementation. The blocked design exposes matrix-matrix operations and enables overlap of CPU panel factorization with GPU updates, while avoiding explicit reorthogonalization.
AI.result: Numerical experiments demonstrate that the method maintains orthogonality and approximation accuracy where block Gram-Schmidt without reorthogonalization fails. On an NVIDIA GH200, the overlapped implementation reduces runtime from 9.91 seconds (CPU-only) to 0.407 seconds for the largest tested matrix, achieving roughly a 24x speedup.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method provides a stable and efficient building block for low-rank approximation on heterogeneous systems, with potential applications in computational science and engineering, particularly as an alternative to SVD-based approaches in training low-rank deep neural networks.

title: Generation of Isolated Collimated Polarized $γ$-ray Beams via Spatiotemporal Optical Vortex Modulation
summary: Attosecond, collimated, bright, polarized $γ$-ray sources are in high demand across nuclear physics, astrophysics, and high-energy physics. However, realizing attosecond duration, high collimation, high brilliance, and high polarization simultaneously within a single isolated source remains an outstanding challenge, owing to the inherent trade-offs between beam trapping and radiative dynamics. Here, we propose a novel scheme to generate an isolated, collimated, high-brilliance, polarized attosecond $γ$-ray beam from conventional solid foils irradiated by a linearly polarized spatiotemporal optical vortex (STOV) laser pulse accessible in Lab. Three-dimensional spin-resolved particle-in-cell simulations reveal that this relativistic-intensity STOV pulse can trap and accelerate electrons at its spatiotemporal singularity, producing a compact isolated electron bunch. This electron bunch subsequently undergoes head-on collision with the reflected laser pulse, which generates isolated $γ$-ray beams through nonlinear Compton scattering. With a peak intensity of $7\times10^{21}$ W/cm$^2$, we observe an isolated collimated ($\sim1.5^{\circ}$) $γ$-ray beam with an average linear polarization of $>60\%$ and a duration of $\sim$500 attoseconds. This approach is feasible with current or upcoming laser facilities and robust against variations in laser and target parameters, highlighting the capability of spatiotemporal structured light field modulation to address outstanding problems in plasma physics.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a novel scheme to generate isolated, collimated, high-brilliance, polarized attosecond γ-ray beams by irradiating solid foils with a linearly polarized spatiotemporal optical vortex (STOV) laser pulse, demonstrated via 3D spin-resolved particle-in-cell simulations.
AI.motivation: Attosecond, collimated, bright, polarized γ-ray sources are highly needed across nuclear physics, astrophysics, and high-energy physics, but simultaneously achieving attosecond duration, high collimation, high brilliance, and high polarization in a single isolated source remains an outstanding challenge due to inherent trade-offs between beam trapping and radiative dynamics.
AI.method: The scheme uses a relativistically intense STOV laser pulse that traps and accelerates electrons at its spatiotemporal singularity, producing a compact isolated electron bunch. This bunch then collides head-on with the reflected laser pulse, generating isolated γ-ray beams via nonlinear Compton scattering, validated by 3D spin-resolved particle-in-cell simulations.
AI.result: At a peak intensity of 7×10^21 W/cm^2, an isolated collimated (~1.5°) γ-ray beam is produced with average linear polarization >60% and duration of ~500 attoseconds. The approach is feasible with current or upcoming laser facilities and robust against parameter variations.
AI.conclusion: The work demonstrates that spatiotemporal structured light field modulation can address outstanding problems in plasma physics, offering a practical path to isolated polarized attosecond γ-ray sources with existing laser technology.

title: Optimal regularity and fine asymptotics for very fast diffusion equations in bounded domains
summary: We prove the optimal global regularity of admissible solutions to a transformed very fast diffusion equation in the range $-1<p<0$, posed on smooth bounded domains with zero Dirichlet boundary data and initial data comparable to the distance function. More precisely, we establish existence and uniqueness and show that solutions belong to $C^{1,p+1}(\overlineΩ)$ in space for every positive time and are $C^\infty$ in time uniformly up to the boundary. Moreover, all their time derivatives belong to $C^{1,p+1}(\overlineΩ)$, and the exponent $p+1$ is optimal. These regularity estimates further yield fine long-time asymptotics toward the friendly giant solution, including a first-order expansion in the $C^{1,p+1}(\overlineΩ)$ topology and an improved convergence rate for the relative error in $C^{p+1}(\overlineΩ)$.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes optimal global regularity for admissible solutions to a transformed very fast diffusion equation for -1<p<0 on smooth bounded domains with zero Dirichlet data and distance-like initial data. Solutions are shown to be C^{1,p+1} in space for all positive times, C^∞ in time uniformly up to the boundary, with all time derivatives also in C^{1,p+1}. The exponent p+1 is proven optimal. These estimates yield refined long-time asymptotics toward the friendly giant solution, including first-order expansion in C^{1,p+1} topology and improved convergence rates for the relative error.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to resolve regularity questions for the very fast diffusion equation in the range -1<p<0, a regime where solutions exhibit degenerate/singular behavior near boundaries that requires careful analysis of admissible (entropy-type) solutions. Establishing optimal regularity is central to understanding the asymptotic behavior toward the friendly giant solution.
AI.method: The authors prove existence, uniqueness, and optimal regularity through a combination of analytical techniques. They establish that solutions lie in C^{1,p+1}(Ω̄) in space (with p+1 being the sharp exponent) and are C^∞ in time uniformly up to the boundary, including all time derivatives in C^{1,p+1}(Ω̄). They prove optimality of the exponent and use these bounds to derive refined asymptotics.
AI.result: Existence and uniqueness of admissible solutions with initial data comparable to the distance function. Optimal spatial regularity C^{1,p+1}(Ω̄) for all positive times and C^∞ regularity in time uniformly up to the boundary, with all time derivatives also in C^{1,p+1}(Ω̄). The exponent p+1 is shown to be optimal. These yield a first-order asymptotic expansion in C^{1,p+1}(Ω̄) topology toward the friendly giant solution and an improved convergence rate for the relative error in C^{p+1}(Ω̄).
AI.conclusion: The paper achieves the optimal global regularity theory for the transformed very fast diffusion equation in the parameter range -1<p<0 and leverages it to obtain sharp long-time asymptotics, fully characterizing the convergence behavior to the friendly giant solution.

title: Cartesian tensor equivariant machine-learning force field for spin-dependent atomistic simulations
summary: Magnetic materials exhibit an intricate coupling between atomic structure and spin degrees of freedom, posing a fundamental challenge for atomistic simulations across experimentally relevant length and time scales. Here we introduce HotPP-Spin, a spin-dependent extension of HotPP for magnetic machine learning interatomic potentials, built on Cartesian tensor equivariant message passing. Atomic magnetic moments are treated as explicit axial-vector degrees of freedom, while spatial-inversion and time-reversal parities are propagated through the tensor couplings. This construction provides a unified representation of exchange-dominated and spin-orbit-induced interactions without imposing predefined analytical interaction forms. A scalar spin-dependent potential energy surface yields energy-conserving atomic forces and magnetic effective fields through differentiation. Benchmarks spanning collinear magnetism, noncollinear magnetism, and spin-orbit-coupling-induced magnetic anisotropy show that HotPP-Spin accurately describes magnetic energy landscapes, magnetic forces, and magnetic-order-dependent energy-volume relations within the same general framework. For H-phase monolayer VSe\(_2\), stochastic spin-dynamics simulations using the learned magnetic effective fields locate the finite-size magnetic ordering crossover at 415--435~K, in close numerical agreement with the reported experimental value of \(418.5\pm7.8\)~K. These results establish Cartesian tensor message passing as a general route for connecting first-principles magnetic energetics with large-scale atomistic simulations of coupled structural and spin phenomena.

AI.tldr: HotPP-Spin is a spin-dependent machine learning interatomic potential that treats atomic magnetic moments as explicit axial-vector degrees of freedom within Cartesian tensor equivariant message passing, enabling accurate simulations of magnetic materials across collinear magnetism, noncollinear magnetism, and spin-orbit-coupling effects in a unified framework.
AI.motivation: Magnetic materials exhibit complex coupling between atomic structure and spin degrees of freedom, which poses a fundamental challenge for atomistic simulations at experimentally relevant scales. Existing methods lack a unified framework to capture both exchange-dominated and spin-orbit-induced interactions without predefined analytical forms.
AI.method: HotPP-Spin extends HotPP by treating atomic magnetic moments as explicit axial-vector degrees of freedom, propagating spatial-inversion and time-reversal parities through Cartesian tensor couplings, and deriving energy-conserving forces and magnetic effective fields via differentiation of a scalar spin-dependent potential energy surface.
AI.result: The method accurately describes collinear magnetism, noncollinear magnetism, and spin-orbit-coupling-induced magnetic anisotropy within one framework. For H-phase monolayer VSe2, stochastic spin-dynamics simulations predict a magnetic ordering crossover at 415-435 K, closely matching the experimental value of 418.5±7.8 K.
AI.conclusion: Cartesian tensor message passing provides a general and accurate route for connecting first-principles magnetic energetics with large-scale atomistic simulations of coupled structural and spin phenomena.

title: Minimizing the Arithmetic and Communication Complexity of Jacobi's Method for Eigenvalues and Singular Values: Part Two -- Parallel Algorithms
summary: This paper presents several parallel versions of Jacobi's method for the symmetric eigenvalue problem and the SVD. A continuation of [Demmel, Luo, Schneider, & Wang 2025], we develop parallel Jacobi algorithms whose arithmetic cost is optimal and whose bandwidth or latency can match the corresponding lower bounds of parallel matrix multiplication. Our focus is a standard distributed-memory setting with variable processor layouts, including both 2D and 2.5D processor grids. In the 2D case, we demonstrate that a standard implementation of parallel Jacobi achieves a perfect speedup in arithmetic cost -- i.e., complexity $O(n^3/P)$ when done with $P$ processors -- while hitting the 2D matrix-multiplication lower bound for bandwidth and (nearly) the lower bound for latency. By employing a 2.5D processor grid and leveraging 2.5D matrix multiplication, equivalently by increasing the memory per processor, we demonstrate that parallel Jacobi can achieve even lower bandwidth/latency, though we also prove that these costs cannot simultaneously match the best-known bounds for parallel matrix multiplication in any Jacobi algorithm. Finally, we extend our results to one-sided Jacobi SVD.

AI.tldr: This paper presents parallel versions of Jacobi's method for symmetric eigenvalue problems and SVD, achieving optimal arithmetic cost and matching bandwidth/latency lower bounds of parallel matrix multiplication on 2D and 2.5D processor grids.
AI.motivation: To develop parallel Jacobi algorithms with optimal arithmetic cost and communication complexity that match the theoretical lower bounds of parallel matrix multiplication, building on prior work by Demmel et al. (2025).
AI.method: The authors analyze standard parallel Jacobi implementations on 2D and 2.5D processor grids, showing arithmetic cost of O(n³/P) with P processors, and evaluate bandwidth and latency against matrix-multiplication lower bounds. They also extend results to one-sided Jacobi SVD.
AI.result: On 2D grids, parallel Jacobi achieves perfect arithmetic speedup, hits the 2D matrix-multiplication bandwidth lower bound, and nearly matches the latency lower bound. On 2.5D grids, lower bandwidth/latency is achievable, but these costs cannot simultaneously match the best-known parallel matrix multiplication bounds in any Jacobi algorithm.
AI.conclusion: Parallel Jacobi can be made communication-optimal on 2D grids and improved on 2.5D grids, though there are fundamental limits preventing simultaneous achievement of the best-known matrix multiplication communication bounds.

title: Rapid Energy Dissipation by Colliding Waves in Strongly Magnetized Plasmas
summary: Rapid dissipation of magnetic energy in highly magnetized environments around neutron stars and black holes is a key open question in high-energy astrophysics. We develop a general kinetic picture of counter-propagating wave collisions in magnetized pair plasmas for arbitrary polarizations and find that magnetic energy can be dissipated on the wave-crossing timescale. The two magnetohydrodynamical conditions on the field invariants, $I_1\equiv B^2-E^2>0$ and $I_2\equiv \mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B}=0$, can be spontaneously violated during the collision. Parallel electric fields develop to screen nonzero $I_2$ with little energy loss, consistent with the evolution described by Force-Free Electrodynamics. When magnetic dominance is lost, strong particle energization is triggered, dissipating magnetic energy on the wave-crossing timescale. This dynamical process yields a rapid dissipation channel of magnetic energy and provides a kinetic pathway to high-energy emission.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a general kinetic theory of counter-propagating wave collisions in magnetized pair plasmas, showing that magnetic energy can be rapidly dissipated on the wave-crossing timescale through spontaneous violation of MHD field invariants and subsequent particle energization.
AI.motivation: Rapid magnetic energy dissipation in highly magnetized environments around neutron stars and black holes is a key open question in high-energy astrophysics, and existing models lack a general kinetic understanding of how this dissipation occurs.
AI.method: The authors develop a general kinetic framework for counter-propagating wave collisions in magnetized pair plasmas, analyzing arbitrary polarizations and tracking the evolution of the MHD field invariants I1 (B²−E²) and I2 (E·B), along with parallel electric field development and particle energization.
AI.result: Magnetic energy can be dissipated on the wave-crossing timescale. The MHD invariants I1>0 and I2=0 can be spontaneously violated during collisions. Parallel electric fields develop to screen nonzero I2 with little energy loss (consistent with Force-Free Electrodynamics), and when magnetic dominance is lost, strong particle energization is triggered that dissipates magnetic energy on the wave-crossing timescale.
AI.conclusion: This kinetic process provides a rapid dissipation channel for magnetic energy and offers a pathway to high-energy emission in magnetized astrophysical environments.

title: Time periodic problem of the Navier-Stokes equations in an exterior domain with periodically moving boundary
summary: In this paper we consider the Navier-Stokes equations in exterior domains of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 3$, with a periodically in time moving boundary $\partialΩ(t)$ and external force $f(t)$. For this case we prove the existence of a locally unique mild time periodic solution in weighted function spaces with radially symmetric Muckenhoupt weights. The solutions split into a stationary part controlled by potential theoretic estimates and a purely oscillatory part constructed as mild solution via analytic semigroup theory. To deal with perturbation terms of even second order - coming from a coordinate transform and the moving boundary - in weighted, homogeneous Sobolev spaces a maximal $L^1$ type regularity estimate will be used in weighted Lorentz spaces. To control the convective term an $\mathcal H^\infty$-calculus in weighted spaces of the Stokes operator, its $BIP$ property and embedding estimates of fractional powers are exploited, see a recent paper by the authors: The Stokes operator on exterior domains in homogeneous weighted function spaces: From weak theory to $\mathscr H^\infty$-calculus to fractional domains (2025).

AI.tldr: The paper proves existence of a locally unique mild time-periodic solution to the Navier-Stokes equations in exterior domains of R^n (n≥3) with a periodically moving boundary and external force, using weighted function spaces with radially symmetric Muckenhoupt weights.
AI.motivation: To establish the existence of time-periodic solutions for the Navier-Stokes equations in exterior domains with moving boundaries, which is a challenging problem due to the combination of moving geometry, weighted spaces, and nonlinear convective terms.
AI.method: The solution is split into a stationary part (via potential theoretic estimates) and an oscillatory part (via analytic semigroup theory). Maximal L^1-type regularity in weighted Lorentz spaces handles second-order perturbation terms from the coordinate transform and moving boundary. The H∞-calculus, BIP property, and fractional power embedding estimates of the Stokes operator in weighted spaces control the convective term.
AI.result: A locally unique mild time-periodic solution is obtained in weighted function spaces with radially symmetric Muckenhoupt weights for the Navier-Stokes equations in exterior domains with periodically moving boundaries.
AI.conclusion: The combination of potential-theoretic estimates, semigroup theory, maximal regularity in Lorentz spaces, and Stokes operator functional calculus in weighted spaces yields well-posedness of time-periodic solutions for moving-boundary Navier-Stokes equations.

title: OpenMUSTANC (MUltiple Scattering Theory At Nanoplasmonic Cavities): A MATLAB toolbox for the simulation of Plasmonic Sphere Aggregates
summary: Mesoscopic physical models, including the Hydrodynamic Drude Model (HDM), the Generalized Nonlocal Optical Response (GNOR) Model, and the Surface Response Model (SRM), have been proposed to investigate nonlocal effects in nanometric structures. The combination of classical electromagnetism with these mesoscopic material models calls for new computational electromagnetic (CEM) algorithms, or update of conventional ones, in what is termed computational mesoscopic electromagnetics (CMEM). In this work, we present a MATLAB toolbox for the simulation of multiple spherical interfaces with arbitrary relative positions, with the incorporation of the aforementioned mesoscopic models. The method exploits vector spherical wave functions to properly express electric and magnetic fields, an S matrix formulation for the efficient treatment of incident and scattered fields at spherical interfaces, and a translation matrix to deal with propagating waves with different expansion centers. Excitation sources can be chosen among arbitrarily polarized plane waves, dipoles and electron beams. For the post-processing part, the calculation of cross sections and far/near-field mapping; fluorescence enhancement, Purcell factor and quantum yield; and cathodoluminescence and electron energy-loss probability is implemented. The toolbox is built in a modular manner, and each part (routine) has its own important functionality. This paper provides a full explanation of the proposed highly efficient and general toolbox, and a detailed guideline for researchers in the nanoplasmonics community.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a MATLAB toolbox for computational mesoscopic electromagnetics (CMEM), enabling simulation of multiple spherical interfaces with arbitrary relative positions while incorporating mesoscopic physical models (HDM, GNOR, SRM) to capture nonlocal optical effects in nanometric structures.
AI.motivation: Mesoscopic physical models that account for nonlocal effects in nanometric structures require new or updated computational electromagnetic algorithms. There is a need for a general, efficient, and accessible simulation tool that incorporates these models for multiple spherical interfaces with arbitrary arrangements.
AI.method: The toolbox uses vector spherical wave functions to express electric and magnetic fields, an S matrix formulation for efficient treatment of incident and scattered fields at spherical interfaces, and a translation matrix to handle propagating waves with different expansion centers. It supports arbitrary polarized plane waves, dipoles, and electron beams as excitation sources, and implements post-processing for cross sections, near/far-field mapping, fluorescence enhancement, Purcell factor, quantum yield, cathodoluminescence, and electron energy-loss probability.
AI.result: The authors present a modular, highly efficient, and general MATLAB toolbox for CMEM simulation, incorporating HDM, GNOR, and SRM mesoscopic models for multiple spherical interfaces with arbitrary relative positions.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a full explanation of the proposed toolbox and a detailed guideline for researchers in the nanoplasmonics community, making advanced nonlocal optical simulations accessible.

title: A Sharp Unitarily Invariant Norm Bound for the Off-Diagonal Block Perturbation of a Hermitian Matrix

AI.tldr: This paper extends a sharp spectral-norm eigenvalue perturbation bound for partitioned Hermitian matrices to unitarily invariant norms. The extension is proven valid for all Q-norms (including Schatten p-norms for 2≤p≤∞) and for any unitarily invariant norm when the off-diagonal block has rank ≤ 1, with equality attained on a 2×2 matrix.
AI.motivation: Li and Li (2005) established a sharp spectral-norm bound on eigenvalue changes when dropping off-diagonal blocks of a partitioned Hermitian matrix. The open question is whether this result can be generalized to other unitarily invariant norms besides the spectral norm.
AI.method: The paper analyzes the extension of the spectral-norm bound φ(η,ε₂)‖A−Ã‖₂ to unitarily invariant norms ‖·‖_UI. Two main results are proven: (a) the extension holds for any Q-norm (a subclass of unitarily invariant norms including Schatten p-norms for 2≤p≤∞, Frobenius norm, and spectral norm), and (b) the extension holds for any unitarily invariant norm when rank(E)≤1. Equality is shown to be attained on a 2×2 matrix.
AI.result: The paper proves that the eigenvalue perturbation bound extends to Q-norms for all such norms, and to any unitarily invariant norm in the rank-1 case. Equality is attained on a 2×2 matrix, demonstrating sharpness of the results.
AI.conclusion: The eigenvalue perturbation bound for partitioned Hermitian matrices originally established in the spectral norm can be generalized to a broader class of unitarily invariant norms under certain conditions, with sharpness verified.

title: Origin of small-scale evaporation flows deep in the chromosphere during a solar flare
comment: Accepted for publication in the Astrophysical Journal Letters (Issue: Sunrise III Early Science)
summary: Flares are caused by an abrupt release of magnetic energy in the solar atmosphere. Plasma heated to well over 10 MK filling the post-flare corona originates from a rapid heating and ablation of the cooler chromospheric material. This chromospheric evaporation is thought to be facilitated primarily by nonthermal electrons impinging on to the lower atmosphere. Questions on when and where in the chromosphere these upflows originate, however, are not fully resolved. Here we report on unprecedented high-resolution observations of an M-class flare recorded by the Sunrise Ultraviolet Spectropolarimeter and Imager on board the balloon-borne SUNRISE observatory, that reveal highly structured upflows on spatial scales of ~100 km originating deep in the chromosphere. The flows even precede the onset of nonthermal electrons by about 10 minutes and last through the impulsive phase of the flare. Our observations shed new light on the lower atmospheric heating and mass circulation in flares that are challenging to reconcile with the standard solar flare model.

AI.tldr: High-resolution observations from the SUNRISE balloon observatory reveal highly structured chromospheric upflows on ~100 km scales during an M-class flare. These flows originate deep in the chromosphere and precede the onset of nonthermal electrons by ~10 minutes, challenging the standard solar flare model that attributes chromospheric evaporation primarily to nonthermal electron heating.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses unresolved questions about when and where chromospheric evaporation upflows originate during solar flares, since the standard model assumes these flows are driven primarily by nonthermal electrons impacting the lower atmosphere, but this has not been fully confirmed observationally.
AI.method: The study uses unprecedented high-resolution observations of an M-class flare recorded by the Sunrise Ultraviolet Spectropolarimeter and Imager (SUSI) on the balloon-borne SUNRISE observatory, capturing spatial detail on scales of ~100 km to examine chromospheric upflow structure and timing.
AI.result: The observations reveal highly structured upflows on ~100 km spatial scales originating deep in the chromosphere. These flows precede the onset of nonthermal electrons by about 10 minutes and persist through the impulsive phase of the flare.
AI.conclusion: These findings shed new light on lower atmospheric heating and mass circulation in flares, revealing aspects that are difficult to reconcile with the standard solar flare model, suggesting the need for revised understanding of flare chromospheric evaporation drivers.

title: The Stokes Operator on Exterior Domains in Homogeneous Weighted Function Spaces:From Weak Theory to $\mathscr H^\infty$-calculus to Fractional Domains
summary: We consider the Stokes operator $A$ on smooth exterior domains $Ω$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ in homogeneous Sobolev spaces $\widehat H^{κ,q}_w(Ω)$ with radially symmetric Muckenhoupt weights $w\in \mathscr A_q$. A fundamental property is the existence of a bounded $\mathscr H^\infty$-calculus of the Stokes operator on weighted nonhomogeneous and homogeneous $L^q$ Sobolev spaces. This property implies the existence of uniformly bounded purely imaginary powers $A^{it}$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$, and the characterization of domains of fractional powers $A^θ$ equipped with nonhomogeneous ($\| u\|_{L^q_w} + \|A^θu\|_{L^q_w}$) as well as homogeneous norm ($\|A^θu\|_{L^q_w}$) as complex interpolation spaces. The final aim is the identification with homogeneous spaces $\widehat{\mathcal D}((-Δ_{q,w})^θ) = [L^q_{w},\widehat{\mathcal D}(-Δ_{q,w})]_θ$ intersected by a space of solenoidal vector fields. Moreover, we obtain weighted variational inequalities for weak solutions of the Stokes equations, weighted $L^q$-$L^r$ decay estimates of the Stokes semigroup and $L^p$-maximal regularity on $L^q_{σ,w}(Ω)$.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes the existence of a bounded H^∞-calculus for the Stokes operator on weighted homogeneous Sobolev spaces over exterior domains, which yields fractional power domain characterizations via complex interpolation, weighted variational inequalities, decay estimates, and maximal regularity results.
AI.motivation: To extend the theory of the Stokes operator on exterior domains to weighted homogeneous Sobolev spaces with Muckenhoupt weights, enabling more refined analysis of fractional powers, interpolation spaces, and semigroup properties in weighted settings.
AI.method: The paper works with the Stokes operator A on smooth exterior domains in homogeneous Sobolev spaces with radially symmetric Muckenhoupt weights. It proves a bounded H^∞-calculus, which implies bounded purely imaginary powers and characterizes fractional power domains as complex interpolation spaces. The identification uses spaces of solenoidal vector fields and weighted Laplacian domains.
AI.result: The paper achieves identification of homogeneous fractional power spaces with complex interpolation spaces of the weighted Laplacian intersected with solenoidal spaces, establishes weighted variational inequalities for Stokes weak solutions, derives weighted L^q-L^r decay estimates of the Stokes semigroup, and proves L^p-maximal regularity on weighted solenoidal spaces.
AI.conclusion: The H^∞-calculus approach provides a unified framework for understanding fractional powers, interpolation characterizations, decay estimates, and maximal regularity for the Stokes operator on weighted homogeneous Sobolev spaces over exterior domains.

title: Propensity Straight-Through Gradients for Discrete Stochastic Systems
summary: Continuous-time Markov chains (CTMCs) provide the backbone for modeling discrete stochastic dynamics across applied, physical, and biological sciences. Their integration with modern gradient-based machine learning, however, is limited by the hard categorical event selection intrinsic to Gillespie-type simulation algorithms. We exploit the affine state update to obtain the exact one-step conditional-mean sensitivity by differentiating normalized reaction propensities. We pair this backward rule with exact forward trajectories to define the propensity straight-through (PST) estimator. At the trajectory level, we show that one-step sensitivities composed across events can depart from the exact multistep sensitivity. We derive the resulting per-step discrepancy in closed form and prove that it vanishes identically for affine downstream dependence. PST matches the accuracy of Gumbel-Softmax straight-through across all benchmarks: reversible dimerization (0.06% error), a genetic oscillator (1.7% error), a 50-task repressilator suite (0.17% median error), and patch-clamp ion-channel recordings ($R^2$ = 0.988). Under matched settings, PST converges 3.0-fold faster on the oscillator and 2.1-fold faster on the ion channel. At deep-learning scale, PST trains a 203,796-parameter stochastic reaction network with hard sampling, reaching 98.22% MNIST digit classification accuracy. By differentiating an exact conditional mean rather than a relaxed sample, PST offers a temperature- and Gumbel-free path to scalable gradient-based learning through exact stochastic trajectories.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the propensity straight-through (PST) estimator, a new method for gradient-based learning through continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) simulations. PST differentiates exact one-step conditional-mean sensitivities via affine state updates and normalized reaction propensities, avoiding Gumbel-Softmax relaxations and temperature tuning. It matches or exceeds state-of-the-art accuracy on multiple benchmarks and scales to a 203,796-parameter deep stochastic reaction network achieving 98.22% MNIST accuracy.
AI.motivation: CTMCs are fundamental for modeling discrete stochastic dynamics, but integrating them with gradient-based machine learning is difficult because Gillespie-type simulations involve hard categorical event selection, which is non-differentiable. Existing relaxations (e.g., Gumbel-Softmax) add complexity and bias.
AI.method: The PST estimator exploits the affine state update of CTMCs to derive an exact one-step conditional-mean sensitivity by differentiating normalized reaction propensities. This backward rule is paired with exact forward trajectories. The authors also prove that one-step sensitivities composed across events can deviate from exact multistep sensitivity, but this discrepancy vanishes identically for affine downstream dependence, and they derive the per-step discrepancy in closed form.
AI.result: PST matches Gumbel-Softmax straight-through accuracy across benchmarks: reversible dimerization (0.06% error), genetic oscillator (1.7% error), 50-task repressilator suite (0.17% median error), and patch-clamp ion-channel recordings (R²=0.988). PST converges 3.0x faster on the oscillator and 2.1x faster on the ion channel. At scale, it trains a 203,796-parameter stochastic reaction network reaching 98.22% MNIST classification accuracy.
AI.conclusion: By differentiating an exact conditional mean rather than a relaxed sample, PST offers a temperature- and Gumbel-free path to scalable gradient-based learning through exact stochastic trajectories, representing a principled alternative to relaxation-based estimators for differentiable simulation of CTMCs.

title: Gappy probabilistic manifold decomposition for nonlinear field reconstruction
summary: This paper proposes gappy probabilistic manifold decomposition (Gappy PMD), a nonlinear method for reconstructing high-dimensional fields from extremely sparse measurements. Gappy PMD reconstructs the field on the nonlinear manifold learned by probabilistic manifold decomposition (PMD). We further propose a differentiable point selection method for reduced-order model (ROM)-based field reconstruction (DPS). Using differentiable meshless interpolation within the ROM-based reconstruction framework, DPS makes the full-field reconstruction error differentiable with respect to the sampling locations and directly optimizes these locations. In addition, a theoretical error analysis for Gappy PMD is also given. It splits the squared reconstruction error into two orthogonal parts: one normal to the reconstruction manifold and the other induced by sparse sampling and observation noise. Under a stability condition on the sampling operator, this error vanishes with the PMD approximation error and the noise. The Gappy PMD is evaluated on three numerical test cases: flow past a cylinder, lid-driven cavity flow, and backward-facing step flow. For the same reduced dimension and sampling points, Gappy PMD attains mean relative $L^2$ errors one to two orders of magnitude below Gappy POD. Optimizing the sampling points with DPS further improves reconstruction accuracy and robustness.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Gappy PMD, a nonlinear method for reconstructing high-dimensional fields from extremely sparse measurements using a nonlinear manifold learned by probabilistic manifold decomposition, along with a differentiable point selection (DPS) method for optimizing sampling locations. Theoretical error analysis shows the reconstruction error splits into orthogonal components, and numerical experiments on three flow cases demonstrate one to two orders of magnitude improvement over Gappy POD.
AI.motivation: High-dimensional field reconstruction from sparse measurements is a challenging problem, and existing methods like Gappy POD rely on linear manifolds that may not capture the underlying nonlinear structure of complex flows. The authors aim to develop a nonlinear reconstruction approach and optimize sampling locations to improve accuracy for extremely sparse measurement scenarios.
AI.method: The paper proposes (1) Gappy PMD, which reconstructs fields on a nonlinear manifold learned by probabilistic manifold decomposition, and (2) a differentiable point selection (DPS) method that uses differentiable meshless interpolation within the ROM-based reconstruction framework to make the reconstruction error differentiable with respect to sampling locations and directly optimize those locations. A theoretical error analysis decomposes the squared reconstruction error into orthogonal components.
AI.result: On three numerical test cases (flow past a cylinder, lid-driven cavity flow, and backward-facing step flow), Gappy PMD achieves mean relative L2 errors one to two orders of magnitude lower than Gappy POD for the same reduced dimension and sampling points. Optimizing sampling points with DPS further improves reconstruction accuracy and robustness.
AI.conclusion: Gappy PMD provides an effective nonlinear approach for sparse field reconstruction with strong theoretical support, and DPS enables significant accuracy gains through sampling point optimization.

title: Magnetizing nonlinear plasma wakefields for positron acceleration
summary: It is known that only a narrow plasma wakefield sliver in the electron-beam-driven blowout regime suits positron acceleration. Using 3D simulations, we show that matching the cyclotron frequency $ω_{c}$ with the plasma frequency $ω_{p}$ forms a stable electron column on axis, expanding the suitable phase space for positron acceleration sizably. For a plasma density $n_p = 10^{16}\text{ cm}^{-3}$ in a 35 T field, the interval expands 4.3 times, and a witness positron beam gains 100--150 MeV over 6 cm ($1.6$--$2.5$~GeV/m) with a 92\% capture rate.

AI.tldr: This paper uses 3D simulations to show that matching the cyclotron frequency with the plasma frequency forms a stable electron column on axis, significantly expanding the phase space for positron acceleration in plasma wakefields. In a plasma density of 10^16 cm^-3 with a 35 T field, the usable interval expands 4.3 times, and a witness positron beam gains 100-150 MeV over 6 cm (1.6-2.5 GeV/m) with a 92% capture rate.
AI.motivation: Positron acceleration in plasma wakefields is challenging because only a narrow phase-space sliver in the electron-beam-driven blowout regime is suitable for positron acceleration, limiting the practicality of this approach.
AI.method: The authors use 3D simulations to demonstrate that matching the cyclotron frequency (ω_c) with the plasma frequency (ω_p) creates a stable electron column on axis, which expands the usable phase space for positron acceleration.
AI.result: For a plasma density of 10^16 cm^-3 in a 35 T magnetic field, the suitable interval expands 4.3 times. A witness positron beam gains 100-150 MeV over 6 cm (equivalent to 1.6-2.5 GeV/m) with a 92% capture rate.
AI.conclusion: Matching the cyclotron and plasma frequencies provides an effective mechanism to substantially expand the phase space for positron acceleration in plasma wakefields, improving capture and energy gain performance.

title: Absence of the Lavrentiev phenomenon for a general class of parabolic double phase problems
summary: In this paper, we prove the absence of the Lavrentiev phenomenon for a general class of parabolic double phase functionals with Orlicz growth. The energy density is given by $$ G(|Dw|)+a(x,t)H(|Dw|), $$ where $G$ and $H$ are Young functions satisfying the $Δ_2$ and $\nabla_2$ conditions with $G\prec H$, and $a(\cdot)$ is a continuous nonnegative coefficient. Under suitable balance conditions between the growth gap of $G$ and $H$ and the modulus of continuity of $a(\cdot)$, we show that every finite-energy map can be approximated locally by smooth functions without loss of energy. The result extends the known parabolic double phase theory from power type growth to a broad Young function framework and identifies the natural space-time Orlicz energy class for the problem.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that the Lavrentiev phenomenon does not occur for a class of parabolic double phase functionals with Orlicz growth, showing that finite-energy maps can be locally approximated by smooth functions without energy loss.
AI.motivation: The Lavrentiev phenomenon is a known issue in the calculus of variations where minimizers cannot be approximated by smooth functions. The authors aim to extend the absence of this phenomenon from power-type double phase functionals to a broader Orlicz growth framework.
AI.method: The authors consider energy densities of the form G(|Dw|) + a(x,t)H(|Dw|), where G and H are Young functions satisfying Δ₂ and ∇₂ conditions with G ≺ H, and a(·) is a continuous nonnegative coefficient. They impose balance conditions relating the growth gap between G and H to the modulus of continuity of a(·), then construct smooth approximations of finite-energy maps without energy loss.
AI.result: The paper shows that every finite-energy map can be approximated locally by smooth functions without loss of energy, thereby proving the absence of the Lavrentiev phenomenon in this general Orlicz-growth parabolic double phase setting.
AI.conclusion: The result generalizes the known parabolic double phase theory from power-type growth to a broad Young function framework and identifies the natural space-time Orlicz energy class for the problem.

title: A Learnable Multigrid Framework via Graph Convolutions
summary: This paper presents a novel framework that integrates learnable graph convolutions with the geometric multigrid method for solving partial differential equations (PDEs). The discretization of PDEs is first represented as a graph structure, enabling the application of graph convolutions to enhance the multigrid performance. By incorporating graph convolutions into the multigrid components such as smoothing and inter-grid transfer operators, we develop a learnable multigrid that can adaptively optimize its performance based on the underlying problem characteristics. In this framework, the graph convolutions are embedded directly within the multigrid cycle, effectively transforming the entire multigrid solver into a specialized neural network architecture, rather than combining a classical solver with surrogate models. The learnable multigrid framework is lightweight in terms of parameter count and requires minimal training effort to achieve good performance. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in solving some challenging problems, showing improved convergence rates compared to traditional multigrid methods. The generalizability of the learned parameters across different problem settings, including varying source terms, coefficients, geometries, and mesh sizes, is also investigated with proper weight-sharing and transfer-learning strategies.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a framework that integrates learnable graph convolutions into the geometric multigrid method for solving PDEs. The discretized PDE is represented as a graph, and graph convolutions are embedded into multigrid components (smoothing and inter-grid transfer operators) to turn the entire solver into a specialized neural network. The approach is lightweight, requires minimal training, improves convergence rates over traditional multigrid, and demonstrates generalizability across varying source terms, coefficients, geometries, and mesh sizes via weight-sharing and transfer-learning.
AI.motivation: Traditional multigrid methods require problem-specific tuning and manual design of components like smoothers and transfer operators, which can be suboptimal for challenging PDEs. The authors aim to make multigrid adaptive and learnable by leveraging graph convolutions, avoiding the separate combination of classical solvers with surrogate models.
AI.method: The PDE discretization is represented as a graph. Learnable graph convolutions are embedded directly into the multigrid cycle—specifically into smoothing and inter-grid transfer (restriction/prolongation) operators—transforming the entire multigrid solver into a specialized neural network architecture. Weight-sharing and transfer-learning strategies are used to improve generalizability.
AI.result: Numerical experiments show improved convergence rates compared to traditional multigrid methods on challenging problems. The learned parameters generalize across different source terms, coefficients, geometries, and mesh sizes when appropriate weight-sharing and transfer-learning strategies are applied.
AI.conclusion: The learnable multigrid framework successfully fuses neural network design with classical numerical solvers, offering a lightweight and effective alternative that adapts to problem characteristics while maintaining generalizability across diverse settings.

title: Magnetohydrodynamics of charged interstellar dust. Multifluid models and study of the linear modes
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Interstellar grains play key roles in star and planet formation, including the coupling of the gas to the magnetic field during the protostellar collapse. These roles depend on the local grain size distribution, which requires a multifluid treatment of charged dust. We aim to understand the fundamental physics of the dynamics of a dust distribution in interaction with the gas and the magnetic field. In particular, the purpose is to characterize the (de)coupling conditions of these different components. We provide a multifluid model of charged dust which accounts for the inertia of the grains. A chemical network is used to simulate the charge equilibrium in collapsing protostellar cores. We compute the Alfven modes and the magnetosonic modes to understand the coupling regimes between the gas, the dust fluids, and the magnetic field. We also analyze and compare to the predictions of existing models, that are the neutral dust multifluid and the standard non-ideal magnetohydrodynamics. The charged multifluid model agrees with non-ideal magnetohydrodynamics on the larger scales of a collapsing dense core and the forming disk, while we successfully extend to new regimes where the inertia of dust grains matters. We found that high charge-to-mass dust grains carry the propagation of magnetohydrodynamical waves in protostellar envelopes. We provide analytical expressions of the speed of these waves depending on the dust distribution. The magnetocompressive perturbations lead to local dust-to-gas ratio variations at au scales. A theoretical understanding of the dynamics of a charged dust distribution is provided in the linear regime. The closed set of magnetohydrodynamics equations can be implemented in numerical codes to explore nonlinear effects during the protostellar collapse such as turbulence, angular momentum transport and magnetic dust clumping.

The model agrees with standard non-ideal MHD at larger scales but extends to new regimes where dust inertia matters, showing that high charge-to-mass dust grains carry MHD wave propagation in protostellar envelopes and cause dust-to-gas ratio variations at au scales.

The authors aim to understand the fundamental physics of dust distribution dynamics interacting with gas and magnetic fields, specifically characterizing the (de)coupling conditions of these components.

They compute Alfven modes and magnetosonic modes to understand coupling regimes between gas, dust fluids, and magnetic field, and compare results against existing models (neutral dust multifluid and standard non-ideal MHD).

High charge-to-mass dust grains carry MHD wave propagation in protostellar envelopes. Analytical expressions for wave speeds are derived depending on the dust distribution. Magnetocompressive perturbations produce local dust-to-gas ratio variations at au scales.
