In this work, we intend to develop hybrid schemes which maintain the non-oscillatory feature of characteristic-wise WENO while being less costly. We propose three hybrid schemes, namely the H1-WENO, H2-WENO, and H3-WENO schemes, based on a new troubled-cell indicator constructed from the smoothness indicators of the WENO scheme. The proposed troubled-cell indicator effectively distinguishes smooth and discontinuous regions, allowing the hybrid schemes to employ inexpensive reconstructions in smooth regions and the characteristic-wise WENO reconstruction only near discontinuities. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed schemes retain the accuracy and robustness of characteristic-wise WENO methods while significantly reducing the computational cost. In particular, the H1-WENO scheme achieves an approximately 30--40% improvement in computational efficiency compared to the standard WENO scheme in 2D test cases.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes three hybrid WENO schemes (H1, H2, H3-WENO) for Special Relativistic Hydrodynamics that use a new troubled-cell indicator based on WENO smoothness indicators to apply inexpensive reconstructions in smooth regions and characteristic-wise WENO only near discontinuities, achieving 30-40% computational speedup in 2D tests while maintaining accuracy and robustness.
AI.motivation: Characteristic-wise WENO reconstruction for SRHD equations is accurate and non-oscillatory but computationally expensive due to eigenvector computations in every cell, while cheaper component-wise WENO can produce spurious oscillations near discontinuities. A hybrid approach is needed to balance cost and accuracy.
AI.method: Three hybrid schemes (H1, H2, H3-WENO) are developed using a new troubled-cell indicator derived from the smoothness indicators of the WENO scheme. This indicator distinguishes smooth from discontinuous regions, enabling inexpensive reconstructions in smooth regions and reserving characteristic-wise WENO reconstruction only for cells near discontinuities.
AI.result: Numerical experiments show the hybrid schemes retain the accuracy and robustness of characteristic-wise WENO while significantly reducing computational cost. The H1-WENO scheme achieves approximately 30-40% computational efficiency improvement over standard WENO in 2D test cases.
AI.conclusion: The proposed hybrid WENO schemes successfully balance computational efficiency and numerical accuracy for SRHD simulations, offering a practical alternative to the expensive characteristic-wise WENO approach without sacrificing solution quality.

title: Global solutions to the Boussinesq equations and the planetary geostrophic approximation
comment: 20 pages, to be submitted to SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis, accepted in SIAM TXLA 2026
summary: We investigate the three dimensional Boussinesq equations in the planetary geostrophic scale, where the buoyancy/gravity driven flow is near geostrophic balance in the large horizontal spatial scale. By establishing the uniform (with respect to the characteristic number) estimates, we are able to obtain the global weak solutions and the unique global strong solutions to the Boussinesq equations without restriction on the initial data. Furthermore, sending the characteristic number to zero with the established compactness rigorously justifies the planetary geostrophic approximation of the Boussinesq equations. We employ the novel buoyancy flow-free flow decomposition to overcome the singularity caused by the buoyancy/gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper proves the existence of global weak and unique global strong solutions to the three-dimensional Boussinesq equations in the planetary geostrophic scale without restrictions on initial data, and rigorously justifies the planetary geostrophic approximation by sending the characteristic number to zero using a novel buoyancy flow-free flow decomposition.
AI.motivation: The Boussinesq equations in the planetary geostrophic scale present mathematical challenges due to buoyancy/gravity-driven flows near geostrophic balance, and the singularity caused by buoyancy/gravity makes it difficult to obtain global solutions and justify the planetary geostrophic approximation rigorously.
AI.method: The authors establish uniform estimates with respect to the characteristic number, and employ a novel buoyancy flow-free flow decomposition to overcome the singularity caused by buoyancy/gravity. Compactness arguments are used to rigorously justify the limit as the characteristic number approaches zero.
AI.result: Global weak solutions and unique global strong solutions to the Boussinesq equations are obtained without restrictions on the initial data, and the planetary geostrophic approximation is rigorously justified via compactness as the characteristic number tends to zero.
AI.conclusion: The paper successfully resolves the mathematical challenges of the Boussinesq equations in the planetary geostrophic scale, providing both existence of global solutions and a rigorous derivation of the planetary geostrophic approximation.

title: Solute dispersion in magnetically influenced multiphase flow through a porous tube: axial transport and microrotational effects
summary: This study presents a theoretical investigation of generalized solute dispersion in magnetohydrodynamic multiphase tube flow with porous layers. A two-fluid analytical model is developed for applications in biofluid and environmental fluid dynamics. The model comprises a micropolar (non-Newtonian) fluid core representing the rotational behaviour of red blood cells and a Newtonian plasma periphery embedded with Brinkman and Darcy porous structures, corresponding to the glycocalyx and endothelial layers with distinct permeability characteristics. A transverse magnetic field is incorporated to investigate how magnetic-field-induced modifications of the carrier flow influence solute localisation, with potential relevance to magnetic nanoparticle-mediated drug delivery. Using the generalised dispersion framework of Sankarasubramanian & Gill, analytical solutions are derived to investigate how the coupled axial velocity field and associated microrotational dynamics influence solute transport. The analytical predictions are independently validated through Brownian dynamics simulations, demonstrating excellent agreement for the temporal evolution of the zeroth and first transport moments. The results reveal the previously unexplored influence of microrotational dynamics on solute concentration, convection coefficients and effective dispersion, providing new insights into the coupled roles of translational and rotational fluid motion in biofluid transport. This work bridges an important gap in the literature and establishes a generalized theoretical framework linking magnetic fields, micropolar fluids and porous arterial structures for biofluid transport, targeted drug delivery and clinical engineering applications.

AI.tldr: A theoretical study of generalized solute dispersion in magnetohydrodynamic multiphase tube flow with porous layers, using a two-fluid model (micropolar core + Newtonian periphery with porous structures) validated by Brownian dynamics simulations.
AI.motivation: To bridge a gap in the literature by investigating the coupled roles of microrotational dynamics, magnetic fields, and porous arterial structures in solute transport within biofluid flows, with relevance to targeted drug delivery.
AI.method: A two-fluid analytical model is developed comprising a micropolar (non-Newtonian) fluid core mimicking red blood cell rotation and a Newtonian plasma periphery with Brinkman and Darcy porous layers (glycocalyx/endothelial). A transverse magnetic field is included. Analytical solutions are derived using the Sankarasubramanian & Gill generalized dispersion framework and validated with Brownian dynamics simulations.
AI.result: Analytical predictions show excellent agreement with Brownian dynamics simulations for the zeroth and first transport moments. The study reveals the previously unexplored influence of microrotational dynamics on solute concentration, convection coefficients, and effective dispersion.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes a generalized theoretical framework linking magnetic fields, micropolar fluids, and porous arterial structures, providing new insights for biofluid transport, targeted drug delivery, and clinical engineering applications.

title: Optimal error estimates of sequential finite element method for nonlinear thermo-poroelasticity problems
summary: This study introduces and analyzes a three-step sequential decoupling algorithm designed to address nonlinear, fully coupled quasi-static thermo-poroelasticity systems incorporating convective transport. The finite element method is employed for spatial discretization and the backward Euler method for temporal discretization. The proposed sequential method has a higher computing efficiency than the fully implicit nonlinear numerical scheme, since it does not require any internal iterations. The well-posedness of the numerical solution is discussed by introducing a cut-off operator and the stability analysis of the algorithm is performed. Rigorous analysis yields optimal convergence order estimates for both spatial and temporal discretizations. In order to confirm the theoretical results and the effectiveness of the suggested approach, numerical experiments are finally carried out.

AI.tldr: This paper presents and analyzes a three-step sequential decoupling algorithm for nonlinear fully coupled quasi-static thermo-poroelasticity systems with convective transport, using FEM for space and backward Euler for time discretization. The method requires no internal iterations, offering higher efficiency than fully implicit schemes, with rigorous stability and optimal convergence analyses confirmed by numerical experiments.
AI.motivation: Fully coupled nonlinear thermo-poroelasticity systems with convective transport are computationally expensive to solve using fully implicit schemes due to the need for internal (Newton-type) iterations. There is a need for a more computationally efficient sequential decoupling algorithm that avoids these iterations while maintaining accuracy and stability.
AI.method: A three-step sequential decoupling algorithm is introduced for nonlinear fully coupled quasi-static thermo-poroelasticity with convective transport. Spatial discretization uses the finite element method, and temporal discretization uses the backward Euler method. A cut-off operator is introduced to ensure well-posedness of the numerical solution.
AI.result: The algorithm is shown to be stable and yields optimal convergence order estimates for both spatial and temporal discretizations. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach.
AI.conclusion: The proposed three-step sequential decoupling method provides an efficient alternative to fully implicit schemes for nonlinear thermo-poroelasticity problems, achieving optimal convergence rates without requiring internal iterations, as validated both theoretically and numerically.

title: A Riemannian Extension of a Quadrature Surface Free Boundary Problem: Stability and Optimality
summary:
We study a quadrature surface free boundary problem on a smooth compact finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$. The problem is formulated as a shape optimization problem involving a Dirichlet problem for the Laplace--Beltrami operator, with a geometric condition on the free boundary.
  Under suitable uniform geometric assumptions on the admissible class, we establish its compactness and prove the stability of the corresponding Dirichlet problems, including strong convergence of the associated states in $H_0^1(M)$. We derive the first-order optimality condition for the associated shape functional. Finally, we establish a Riemannian comparison principle for the second fundamental forms and the mean curvatures of tangent boundaries at a contact point. These results provide a rigorous extension of the quadrature surface free boundary framework from the Euclidean setting to compact Riemannian manifolds.

AI.tldr: The paper extends the quadrature surface free boundary problem from Euclidean space to compact Riemannian manifolds, establishing compactness of admissible shapes, stability of Dirichlet problems, first-order optimality conditions, and Riemannian comparison principles for mean curvatures.
AI.motivation: The quadrature surface free boundary problem has been well-studied in Euclidean settings, but a rigorous extension to curved spaces requires addressing geometric complications arising from the manifold structure. The authors aim to generalize this framework to compact Riemannian manifolds.
AI.method: The problem is formulated as a shape optimization problem for a Dirichlet problem of the Laplace-Beltrami operator with a free boundary geometric condition. Under uniform geometric assumptions on the admissible class, the authors prove compactness, stability of Dirichlet problems with strong H0^1(M) convergence of states, derive the first-order optimality condition, and establish a Riemannian comparison principle for second fundamental forms and mean curvatures.
AI.result: Compactness of the admissible class is established, Dirichlet problems are shown to be stable with strong H0^1(M) convergence, the first-order optimality condition for the shape functional is derived, and a Riemannian comparison principle for second fundamental forms and mean curvatures at tangent boundary contact points is proven.
AI.conclusion: The paper rigorously extends the quadrature surface free boundary framework from Euclidean space to compact Riemannian manifolds, providing theoretical foundations for shape optimization problems on curved spaces.

title: Chemical potentials from structure factors: II. Charged multi-component mixtures
summary: The chemical potentials of charged multi-component mixtures are central to electrolyte thermo- dynamics, but remain difficult to compute from atomistic simulations. The S0 method enables computing chemical potentials of mixtures from equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations. Here we extend the S0 method to charged mixtures by combining the composition-space framework developed in Part I: Neutral Multi-component Mixtures with a Coulombic treatment of the small- wavenumber limits of static structure factors. This approach separates thermodynamically relevant neutral composition fluctuations from forbidden macroscopic charge fluctuations, and further ac- counts for charge-neutrality constraints. We use the method to compute the chemical potentials of multiple-halide aqueous salt solutions, elucidating the ion-specific thermodynamic effects. We also calculate the mixing free energies of molten salt mixtures, demonstrating the importance of correctly describing long-wavelength electrostatic correlations.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the S0 method, originally for computing chemical potentials of neutral mixtures from equilibrium MD simulations, to charged multi-component mixtures by combining a composition-space framework with a Coulombic treatment of small-wavenumber static structure factor limits. The method separates neutral composition fluctuations from forbidden macroscopic charge fluctuations and accounts for charge-neutrality constraints, demonstrated on halide salt solutions and molten salt mixtures.
AI.motivation: Chemical potentials of charged multi-component mixtures are central to electrolyte thermodynamics but remain difficult to compute from atomistic simulations, motivating an extension of the S0 method to handle charged systems.
AI.method: The authors extend the S0 method to charged mixtures by integrating the composition-space framework from Part I (neutral mixtures) with a Coulombic treatment of small-wavenumber limits of static structure factors. This separates thermodynamically relevant neutral composition fluctuations from forbidden macroscopic charge fluctuations while accounting for charge-neutrality constraints.
AI.result: The method computes chemical potentials of multiple-halide aqueous salt solutions, revealing ion-specific thermodynamic effects, and calculates mixing free energies of molten salt mixtures, demonstrating the importance of correctly describing long-wavelength electrostatic correlations.
AI.conclusion: The extended S0 method effectively handles charged mixtures, correctly treating long-wavelength electrostatic correlations and charge-neutrality, enabling accurate chemical potential and mixing free energy calculations for electrolytes and molten salts.

title: Interior $C^{2,α}$ Regularity for the Quadratic Hessian Equation
summary: We establish interior $C^{2,α}$ regularity for admissible solutions of the quadratic Hessian equation with positive $C^α$ right-hand side on the full positive branch. The main ingredients are a quantitative large-trace propagation argument and an adaptive Dirichlet comparison method.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes interior C^{2,α} regularity for admissible solutions of the quadratic Hessian equation with positive C^α right-hand side on the full positive branch, using a quantitative large-trace propagation argument and an adaptive Dirichlet comparison method.
AI.motivation: The quadratic Hessian equation σ₂(D²u) = f is a fundamental fully nonlinear PDE, and understanding interior regularity for admissible solutions on the full positive branch is a key open problem, especially when the right-hand side is only C^α rather than smooth.
AI.method: Two main ingredients: (1) a quantitative large-trace propagation argument, and (2) an adaptive Dirichlet comparison method, which together yield the desired C^{2,α} interior regularity.
AI.result: Interior C^{2,α} regularity is established for admissible solutions of the quadratic Hessian equation with positive C^α right-hand side on the full positive branch.
AI.conclusion: The result provides optimal (up to the regularity of f) interior regularity for this Hessian equation under minimal regularity assumptions on the data.

title: Dark exciton signatures in the infrared transient absorption of MoS$_2$ monolayer
summary: Dark excitons play a central role in the nonequilibrium dynamics of two-dimensional semiconductors, but remain difficult to characterize. In this work we show that transient-absorption experiments, with probe pulses tuned in the exciton-exciton transitions energy range (exc-tr-abs), can be used to detect excitations from any populated dark excitonic state, including symmetry-forbidden, spin-forbidden, and finite momentum ones. We develop a fully ab initio scheme, on top of $GW$+BSE, for computing exc-tr-abs spectra from arbitrary populated exciton distributions. The different classes of dark excitons are included on an equal footing, by evaluating exciton-exciton dipole matrix elements in a locally smooth gauge, which accounts for both intra-band and inter-band contributions. As a test case, we consider monolayer MoS$_2$, for which experimental data are available. The exc-tr-abs signal emerges from a sum of contributions from four different valleys in the exciton dispersion, namely $Γ$, $K$, $M$, and $Q$ valleys. The interpretation of the final signal is substantially different from the one based on transitions at $\mathbf{q}=Γ$ alone. The exciton-exciton dipoles show similar intensity among these valleys, while their relative weight is mostly dictated by the initial excitonic population. State- and spin-resolved analyses show that the main peaks can be described as $1s \rightarrow 2p$ and $1s \rightarrow 3p$ transitions from A and B excitons, but with a superposition of transitions from both spin-flip and spin-conserving excitons across the valleys, and with contributions averaged over different momenta within the individual valleys.

AI.tldr: The authors develop a fully ab initio scheme based on GW+BSE to compute transient-absorption spectra from exciton-exciton transitions (exc-tr-abs), enabling detection of dark excitons—including symmetry-forbidden, spin-forbidden, and finite-momentum ones—in 2D semiconductors. Applied to monolayer MoS2, they show contributions from four valleys (Γ, K, M, Q) and reveal that the signal interpretation differs significantly from considering only q=Γ transitions.
AI.motivation: Dark excitons are central to nonequilibrium dynamics in 2D semiconductors but are difficult to characterize experimentally. The authors aim to show that transient-absorption experiments with probes in the exciton-exciton transition energy range can detect excitations from any populated dark excitonic state, and to develop a computational framework for predicting these spectra.
AI.method: The authors build on GW+BSE and compute exciton-exciton dipole matrix elements in a locally smooth gauge, accounting for both intra-band and inter-band contributions. This allows all classes of dark excitons (symmetry-forbidden, spin-forbidden, finite-momentum) to be treated on equal footing. The scheme is applied to monolayer MoS2, where experimental data exist.
AI.result: In monolayer MoS2, the exc-tr-abs signal arises from contributions of four valleys (Γ, K, M, and Q) in the exciton dispersion. Exciton-exciton dipoles have similar intensity across these valleys, with relative weights dictated mainly by the initial excitonic population. The main peaks correspond to 1s→2p and 1s→3p transitions involving both spin-flip and spin-conserving excitons across valleys, with momentum averaging within individual valleys.
AI.conclusion: Transient-absorption in the exciton-exciton transition range can detect any populated dark exciton state, and the interpretation of such signals must account for contributions from multiple valleys and both spin-flip and spin-conserving transitions, rather than considering only q=Γ transitions.

title: High-order energy-stable BGN parametric finite element methods for geometric flows
summary: We construct high-order Runge--Kutta extensions of Barrett--Garcke--Nürnberg (BGN) parametric finite element methods for curve-shortening flow and curve diffusion of planar curves and for mean curvature flow and surface diffusion of closed genus-$0$ surfaces. On each time slab $I_m=(t_m,t_{m+1}]$, the continuous equations are posed on the left-endpoint surface $Γ^m=Γ^{t_m}$ through the map $\X^{m,t}:Γ^m\toΓ^t$, whose target is the evolving surface at time $t$. For curves, this formulation follows by harmonic pullback from $Γ^0$ to $Γ^m$. For surfaces, an orientation-preserving harmonic diffeomorphism is posed separately on each time slab, and conformality yields the weight $\frac12|\nabla_{Γ^m}\X^{m,t}|^2$. Evaluating the time-slab equations at the Runge--Kutta internal times and applying mass-lumped parametric finite elements yields systems on the common domain $Γ^m$, with $Γ^{t_m+c_iτ_m}$ as the intermediate target geometry. This internal-time discretization constructs high-order BGN-structured extensions for the four flows. For an algebraically stable tableau with nonnegative weights, every exact stage solution with nondegenerate intermediate configurations satisfies monotone decay of the discrete curve length or surface area for every positive time step for which that solution exists. Radau IIA experiments exhibit energy decay for all four flows and BGN-type mesh redistribution in the curve tests. The Hausdorff self-convergence results exhibit high-order behavior consistent with the corresponding design orders.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs high-order Runge-Kutta (RK) extensions of Barrett-Garcke-Nürnberg (BGN) parametric finite element methods for four geometric flows: curve-shortening, curve diffusion, mean curvature flow, and surface diffusion. The approach reformulates continuous equations on each time slab using the left-endpoint surface as a common domain, evaluates at RK internal times, and applies mass-lumped parametric finite elements. The resulting methods achieve high-order accuracy, preserve energy decay (curve length/area monotonicity) under algebraically stable tableaus, and demonstrate high-order convergence in experiments with Radau IIA.
AI.motivation: BGN parametric finite element methods are popular for geometric flows due to their favorable mesh properties, but they are limited to low (first/second) order accuracy in time. This paper aims to construct high-order temporal extensions of BGN methods while preserving their structure-preserving properties such as energy decay and mesh redistribution.
AI.method: The authors formulate the continuous geometric flow equations on each time slab using the left-endpoint surface Γ^m as a common reference domain, via a map X^{m,t} whose target is the evolving surface. For curves, this is achieved by harmonic pullback; for surfaces, an orientation-preserving harmonic diffeomorphism with conformality yields a weight of 1/2|∇_{Γ^m} X^{m,t}|². Evaluating these time-slab equations at RK internal times and applying mass-lumped parametric finite elements gives systems on the common domain Γ^m, with intermediate target geometries Γ^{t_m+c_iτ_m}. This constructs high-order BGN-structured extensions for all four flows.
AI.result: For algebraically stable RK tableaus with nonnegative weights, every exact stage solution with nondegenerate intermediate configurations achieves monotone decay of discrete curve length or surface area for any positive time step for which the solution exists. Numerical experiments with Radau IIA tableaus demonstrate energy decay for all four flows, BGN-type mesh redistribution for curve tests, and Hausdorff self-convergence rates consistent with the designed high-order accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The paper successfully extends BGN parametric finite element methods to arbitrary high order via RK time stepping, while preserving key structural properties (energy monotonicity and mesh redistribution). The method is validated across curves and surfaces for four distinct geometric flows.

title: Non-time-decaying global classical solutions to nonlinear wave equations in 3D under the null condition
summary: We present an alternative proof of the global well-posedness of nonlinear wave equations in three spatial dimensions under the null condition, in the regularity regime of the classical local existence theory, assuming smallness of the angular derivatives. Unlike previous methods, which rely on decay in time, our approach is based solely on spatial decay. This provides a new perspective on the problem and offers potential applications to the study of Einstein's equations, which we intend to explore in future work.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a new proof of global well-posedness for nonlinear wave equations in 3D under the null condition, using spatial decay instead of time decay, requiring only smallness of angular derivatives in the classical local existence regularity regime.
AI.motivation: Previous methods for proving global well-posedness of nonlinear wave equations under the null condition rely on decay in time. The authors seek a new perspective based solely on spatial decay, which could offer new insights and potential applications to Einstein's equations.
AI.method: The proof employs solely spatial decay rather than time decay, working in the regularity regime of classical local existence theory, while only requiring smallness of angular derivatives.
AI.result: Global well-posedness is established for nonlinear wave equations in three spatial dimensions under the null condition within the classical local existence regularity regime.
AI.conclusion: The alternative proof provides a new perspective on the problem and has potential applications to the study of Einstein's equations, which the authors intend to explore in future work.

title: Efficient primal--dual splitting methods for a Poisson-constrained JKO scheme for Poisson-Nernst-Planck models
summary: The Poisson--Nernst--Planck (PNP) equations strongly couple ionic transport and electrostatic interactions through the Poisson equation, posing substantial numerical challenges under small permittivity and complex potential boundary conditions. Underlying these equations is a natural Wasserstein gradient-flow structure, in which the Poisson equation serves as a local realization of the nonlocal electrostatic interaction energy. Exploiting this structure, we formulate each time step as a constrained convex minimization problem where the ionic continuity equations and the Poisson equation are incorporated as linear constraints, allowing the concentrations, fluxes, and electrostatic potential to be updated simultaneously. The variational structure of the scheme intrinsically guarantees the dissipation of the original free energy, mass conservation, and nonnegativity of ionic concentrations under general electrostatic boundary conditions. Moreover, the framework is structurally modular: extending from classical to modified PNP models with steric interactions and concentration-gradient corrections requires only modifying the energy functional, while all structure-preserving properties are automatically retained. To efficiently solve the resulting large-scale constrained problems, we develop preconditioned and transformed primal--dual algorithms equipped with tailored fast dual solvers, namely DCT-based direct and Schur-complement iterative methods, that exploit the coupled block structure of the PDE constraints. Numerical experiments on classical and modified PNP systems demonstrate the accuracy and structure-preserving properties of the scheme, and show that the proposed algorithms converge reliably in strongly coupled small-permittivity regimes without significant growth in computational cost.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a structure-preserving numerical scheme for Poisson-Nernst-Planck (PNP) equations, formulated as a constrained convex minimization problem at each time step, exploiting the Wasserstein gradient-flow structure. The scheme guarantees free-energy dissipation, mass conservation, and nonnegativity, and extends modularly to modified PNP models. Efficient primal-dual algorithms with DCT-based and Schur-complement solvers handle large-scale problems, including challenging small-permittivity regimes.
AI.motivation: PNP equations couple ionic transport and electrostatics, posing severe numerical challenges under small permittivity and complex boundary conditions. Existing approaches struggle with these strongly coupled regimes, motivating a structure-preserving framework that respects the underlying variational (gradient-flow) structure.
AI.method: The authors reformulate each time step as a constrained convex minimization problem, where continuity equations and the Poisson equation serve as linear constraints, enabling simultaneous updates of concentrations, fluxes, and potential. They develop preconditioned and transformed primal-dual algorithms with fast dual solvers (DCT-based direct and Schur-complement iterative methods) exploiting the coupled block structure.
AI.result: Numerical experiments demonstrate accuracy and structure-preserving properties on both classical and modified PNP systems. The algorithms converge reliably in strongly coupled small-permittivity regimes without significant growth in computational cost.
AI.conclusion: The variational, modular framework provides a robust and efficient approach for PNP simulations, automatically retaining structure-preserving properties across model extensions (e.g., steric interactions), with scalable solvers suitable for challenging regimes.

title: Advancements in Spectral Collocation Methods for High-Order Eigenvalue Problems
summary: This paper focuses on computing spectral solutions for high-order eigenvalue problems using an efficient discretization method based on Chebfun spectral discretization algorithms and domain truncation. We solve several numerical eigenvalue problems, demonstrating both the accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed approach.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an efficient spectral discretization method for solving high-order eigenvalue problems, combining Chebfun-based algorithms with domain truncation, and demonstrates accuracy and computational efficiency through numerical examples.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of computing accurate spectral solutions for high-order eigenvalue problems and to provide a numerically efficient alternative to existing discretization approaches.
AI.method: The approach uses Chebfun spectral discretization algorithms combined with domain truncation to discretize and solve high-order eigenvalue problems.
AI.result: The method is validated through several numerical eigenvalue problems, showing both high accuracy and computational efficiency.
AI.conclusion: The proposed discretization strategy offers a reliable and efficient means of solving high-order eigenvalue problems numerically.

title: Infinite time blow-up of solutions to the classical Keller-Segel model of chemotaxis in higher dimensions
summary: We study the simplest parabolic-elliptic model of chemotaxis in ${\bf R^N}$, and show the optimal criteria for the existence of infinite time blow-up of solutions with the initial data below the Chandrasekhar singular solution when $N \geq 10$. In particular, we exhibit the differences of the criteria between the cases $N \geq 11$ and $N = 10$. Our argument is based on the study of the Cauchy problem for the transformed equation involving the averaged mass of the solution and the asymptotic expansions of solutions to the Liouville equation.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes optimal criteria for infinite-time blow-up in the parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model in R^N, showing a critical distinction between N ≥ 11 and N = 10 for initial data below the Chandrasekhar singular solution.
AI.motivation: To determine the sharp conditions under which solutions to the chemotaxis equation with subcritical initial data exhibit infinite-time blow-up, and to reveal how the criteria differ between spatial dimensions N ≥ 11 and N = 10.
AI.method: The analysis transforms the chemotaxis system into a Cauchy problem involving the averaged mass of the solution, combined with asymptotic expansions of solutions to the Liouville equation.
AI.result: Optimal criteria for infinite-time blow-up are identified when N ≥ 10, with demonstrated differences between the N ≥ 11 case and the critical N = 10 case.
AI.conclusion: The paper completes the picture of blow-up criteria for the parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis system in high dimensions, highlighting the exceptional behavior at N = 10 as a critical threshold.

title: Particle-Mediated Tuning of Defect Stability in Lamellar Block Copolymer Systems
summary: We study how colloidal inclusions modify the formation energy of dislocation pairs in lamellar block copolymer systems. Using a hybrid particle/Ginzburg--Landau model, we calculate defect formation energies by comparing defect-free and defect-containing states with and without embedded colloids. Finite-size scaling is used to obtain formation energies in the thermodynamic limit. The effect of colloid insertion depends strongly on particle sizes and surface patterning. Homogeneous particles increasingly stabilize dislocation pairs with increasing particle sizes. Particles larger than one lamellar domain preferentially occupy the dislocation cores, where they replace strained polymer rather than deforming defect-free lamellae. The magnitude of this stabilization depends on surface affinity. Balanced Janus particles instead increase the formation energy, because their competing surface preferences cannot be satisfied simultaneously near the curved core. Varying the patch ratio interpolates between these limits. Surface patterning has little effect for particles smaller than one lamellar domain but changes the formation energy by several tens of $k_BT$ for larger particles. These results provide quantitative guidelines for controlling topological defect stability in lamellar block copolymer systems.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how colloidal inclusions affect dislocation pair formation energy in lamellar block copolymers using a hybrid particle/Ginzburg-Landau model, finding that particle size and surface patterning critically determine whether colloids stabilize or destabilize defects.
AI.motivation: To understand and quantitatively control how embedded colloidal particles modify topological defect stability in lamellar block copolymer systems, which is important for designing self-assembled materials with tunable defect behavior.
AI.method: The authors use a hybrid particle/Ginzburg-Landau model to compute defect formation energies by comparing defect-free and defect-containing states, both with and without embedded colloids. Finite-size scaling is employed to extract formation energies in the thermodynamic limit, and particle size, surface affinity, and patch ratio are systematically varied.
AI.result: Homogeneous particles increasingly stabilize dislocation pairs with growing particle size, with large particles preferentially occupying defect cores. Balanced Janus particles increase formation energy due to competing surface preferences near curved cores. Surface patterning has negligible effect on small particles but changes formation energy by tens of k_BT for large particles.
AI.conclusion: The stabilization magnitude depends on surface affinity, and patch ratio interpolates between stabilizing and destabilizing limits, providing quantitative guidelines for controlling topological defect stability in lamellar block copolymer systems.

title: A variant of the block preconditioner for indefinite complex symmetric linear systems
summary: In this paper, we propose an efficient preconditioner for solving indefinite complex symmetric linear systems within a block preconditioning framework. We analyze the convergence of the corresponding iterative method and investigate several spectral properties of the preconditioned matrix, including eigenvalue distributions and eigenvector structures. The new preconditioner is used to accelerate the convergence of the flexible version of GMRES. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed preconditioner, and comparisons with existing block preconditioners demonstrate its superior performance.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an efficient preconditioner for indefinite complex symmetric linear systems within a block preconditioning framework, analyzing convergence and spectral properties, and demonstrates superior performance over existing block preconditioners through numerical experiments.
AI.motivation: Solving indefinite complex symmetric linear systems efficiently is challenging, and existing block preconditioners have limitations in performance. There is a need for a more effective preconditioner to accelerate iterative methods for such systems.
AI.method: The paper develops a new preconditioner within a block preconditioning framework, analyzes its convergence and spectral properties (eigenvalue distributions and eigenvector structures), and applies it to accelerate the flexible GMRES method.
AI.result: Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed preconditioner, and comparisons show it outperforms existing block preconditioners in terms of convergence and performance.
AI.conclusion: The proposed block preconditioner is an efficient and superior alternative for solving indefinite complex symmetric linear systems, supported by both theoretical spectral analysis and numerical validation.

title: Remarks on the two-dimensional Cahn-Hilliard equation forced by divergence of space-time white noise
summary: We consider the two-dimensional Cahn-Hilliard equation forced by divergence of space-time white noise that represents Kawasaki dynamics in conservative form. The standard heuristic argument shows that the solution is a distribution and thus the product within the nonlinear term is ill-defined. We prove the global-in-time unique solution theory. Besides a minimum amount of the standard renormalization procedure to deal with ill-defined products, our proof consists of applications of deterministic analysis tools and taking advantage of the unique structure of the equation, which is crucial.

AI.tldr: The paper proves global-in-time existence and uniqueness of solutions to the two-dimensional Cahn-Hilliard equation forced by divergence of space-time white noise, addressing the issue that the nonlinear product term is ill-defined by using minimal renormalization combined with deterministic analysis techniques tailored to the equation's structure.
AI.motivation: The two-dimensional Cahn-Hilliard equation forced by divergence of space-time white noise (representing Kawasaki dynamics in conservative form) leads to solutions that are distributions, making the product in the nonlinear term ill-defined. The paper aims to establish a rigorous global-in-time solution theory for this equation.
AI.method: The proof combines a minimal renormalization procedure (required to handle the ill-defined products) with deterministic analysis tools and leverages the unique structural properties of the Cahn-Hilliard equation.
AI.result: The authors prove global-in-time existence and uniqueness of solutions to the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equation in two dimensions under conservative (Kawasaki) noise.
AI.conclusion: A rigorous global-in-time solution theory exists for this equation, achievable through minimal renormalization and deterministic analytical techniques that exploit the equation's special structure.

title: Second-Order Accuracy from Large Local Errors in Interface Problems: A Discrete Green's Function Analysis
summary:
Finite difference methods for interface problems often exhibit large local truncation errors near the interface, particularly when discontinuities in coefficients or solution derivatives are present. Nevertheless, many such schemes achieve second-order accuracy, a phenomenon not fully explained by standard pointwise consistency arguments.
  In this work, we provide a precise explanation of this behavior through the structure of the discrete Green's function associated with the underlying conservative difference operator. An explicit representation of the Green's function reveals a two-plateau structure in its weighted increments. By expressing the numerical error in terms of this Green kernel, we show that the dominant interface truncation errors, although individually of order \(O(1)\), possess a cancellation structure that reduces their effective contribution to the global error.
  The exact Green's-function analysis leads to a class of conservative interface flux--balance schemes for which the cancellation mechanism yields second-order accuracy in the maximum norm. The weighted harmonic discretization is included as a particular member, and its cancellation property is established directly. For Cartesian grids with a flat interface parallel to a coordinate direction, the same conservative cancellation mechanism persists along grid lines crossing the interface. Numerical experiments in one and two dimensions directly illustrate the predicted cancellation behavior and the resulting second-order accuracy.
  These results demonstrate that second-order accuracy in interface problems can arise from the interaction between localized truncation errors and the global structure of the discrete operator, rather than from pointwise consistency alone.

AI.tldr: The paper explains why finite difference methods for interface problems achieve second-order accuracy despite having O(1) local truncation errors near interfaces. Through an explicit representation of the discrete Green's function, they show that interface truncation errors cancel each other out via a two-plateau structure, leading to a class of conservative interface flux-balance schemes with second-order accuracy in the maximum norm.
AI.motivation: Finite difference methods for interface problems with discontinuous coefficients/derivatives exhibit large local truncation errors (O(1)) near interfaces yet still achieve second-order accuracy, which standard pointwise consistency arguments cannot explain. The authors aim to provide a precise theoretical explanation for this phenomenon.
AI.method: The authors derive an explicit representation of the discrete Green's function for the underlying conservative difference operator, revealing a two-plateau structure in its weighted increments. They express the numerical error as a convolution with this Green kernel and demonstrate that the dominant O(1) interface truncation errors possess a cancellation structure. This analysis leads to a general class of conservative interface flux-balance schemes where cancellation yields second-order accuracy in the maximum norm.
AI.result: The analysis shows that the cancellation mechanism through the discrete Green's function structure yields second-order maximum-norm accuracy for a class of conservative interface flux-balance schemes. The weighted harmonic discretization is identified as a specific member with directly established cancellation properties. Numerical experiments in 1D and 2D confirm the predicted cancellation behavior and second-order accuracy, including for flat interfaces parallel to coordinate directions on Cartesian grids.
AI.conclusion: Second-order accuracy in interface problems can arise from the interaction between localized truncation errors and the global structure of the discrete operator (via Green's function cancellation), rather than from pointwise consistency alone. This provides a deeper theoretical foundation for why many practical interface schemes outperform their local accuracy would suggest.

title: Time-modulated refocusing in inhomogeneous medium
summary: In an inhomogeneous dissipative medium, different rays experience different round-trip attenuation, so an instantaneous time mirror may retrace rays without producing a balanced point focus. We solve this problem for a microlocally selected back-propagating transverse-magnetic component generated by a short pulsating modulation of a thin shell surrounding an inhomogeneous Debye medium with Ohmic conductivity. An exact decomposition of the Maxwell--Debye field isolates the pulse-generated return, and a semiclassical mode reduction yields a scalar returned operator whose principal symbol separates the temporal pulse response, shell modulation, and accumulated material loss. Our analysis shows that geometric distortion and amplitude attenuation are both involved in wave propagation, but the geometric distortion cancels between the outgoing and returning branches, whereas physical attenuation remains. A normalized directional energy, computed from pre-modulation measurements using the known lossless backward propagator, contains the same leading attenuation factor as the returned symbol. Its reciprocal defines a smooth, nonnegative, physically admissible modulation that equalizes the selected source-side gain up to a relative $O(h)$ error without requiring a complete attenuation model. With such a modulation, the field generated by a point source has a focal-scale leading profile independent of directional attenuation, with a unique maximum at the source and coherent return time. In every fixed focal window, the maximum is displaced by at most $O(h^2)$ in space and time, and the spatial half-amplitude area is $O(h^2)$.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the problem of time reversal in inhomogeneous dissipative media, where different rays suffer different round-trip attenuation, preventing balanced point focusing. The authors solve this using a microlocally selected back-propagating TM component generated by a pulsating thin-shell modulation around an inhomogeneous Debye medium with Ohmic conductivity. They derive an exact decomposition and a semiclassical scalar returned operator whose symbol separates temporal, modulation, and loss effects. Geometric distortion cancels between outgoing and returning branches, but physical attenuation persists. A normalized directional energy from pre-modulation measurements yields a smooth, admissible modulation that equalizes source-side gain up to O(h) error without a full attenuation model, producing a focal-scale profile with O(h²) spatial/temporal focusing accuracy.
AI.motivation: Conventional time reversal (time mirror) in homogeneous lossless media produces balanced point focusing. However, in inhomogeneous dissipative media, different ray paths experience different round-trip attenuation, breaking the symmetry between forward and backward propagation and destroying the point focus. The authors aim to restore coherent focusing despite unknown direction-dependent attenuation.
AI.method: The method involves: (1) an exact decomposition of the Maxwell–Debye field that isolates the pulse-generated return via a short pulsating modulation of a thin shell; (2) a semiclassical mode reduction yielding a scalar returned operator whose principal symbol separates temporal pulse response, shell modulation, and accumulated material loss; (3) construction of a normalized directional energy from pre-modulation measurements using the known lossless backward propagator; (4) using its reciprocal as a smooth, nonnegative, physically admissible modulation that equalizes source-side gain up to relative O(h) error.
AI.result: The analysis shows geometric distortion and amplitude attenuation are both present, but geometric distortion cancels between outgoing and returning branches while physical attenuation persists. The constructed modulation equalizes directional attenuation without requiring a complete attenuation model. With this modulation, a point-source-generated field has a focal-scale leading profile independent of directional attenuation, with a unique maximum at the source and coherent return time. In every fixed focal window, the spatial and temporal maximum displacement is at most O(h²), and the spatial half-amplitude area is O(h²).
AI.conclusion: The paper demonstrates that coherent time-reversal focusing can be restored in inhomogeneous dissipative media by using data-driven measurements (from the lossless propagator) to construct an admissible modulation that compensates for direction-dependent attenuation. The resulting focal quality is near-optimal, with O(h²) accuracy in space and time.

title: Fortin operators for DPG advection discretizations
summary: We construct Fortin operators for discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin (DPG) discretizations of the advection equation with a piecewise constant divergence-free advection vector $β$, on simplicial meshes of any spatial dimension $N$ and for any polynomial degree $k \ge 1$ of the trial space. A minimal test space is built on each element from facet and interior bubbles and later augmented. The Fortin operator is shown to be bounded, uniformly over shape-regular mesh families, in the natural $β$-weighted broken test graph norm built on $L_q$ for every $1 < q < \infty$, where $q$ is the exponent conjugate to the trial exponent $p$. A non-characteristic facet condition is assumed when $k \ge 2$, while the lowest-order case requires no such condition and admits characteristic facets. As applications we prove that the practical fully discrete residual minimization method is quasioptimal in the DPG energy norm for every $1 < p < \infty$, with a quasioptimality constant governed solely by the Fortin operator, that its computable residual is a globally reliable and efficient a posteriori error estimator, and that augmenting the test space and changing the test norm improves the results in the lowest-order case.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs Fortin operators for DPG discretizations of the advection equation with piecewise constant divergence-free advection vectors, on simplicial meshes of any dimension, proving uniform boundedness in β-weighted broken test graph norms for all 1<q<∞, and using these to establish quasioptimality of residual minimization, reliability/efficiency of a posteriori error estimators, and improvements from test space augmentation.
AI.motivation: The DPG method's well-posedness and quasioptimality rely on the existence of Fortin operators with uniform bounds. Constructing such operators for advection problems is challenging, particularly for general polynomial degrees, spatial dimensions, and Lp spaces. The authors aim to provide a complete construction and rigorous analysis that guarantees optimal convergence properties of the DPG method for advection equations.
AI.method: The authors construct minimal test spaces from facet and interior bubbles on each element, which are later augmented. A Fortin operator is explicitly built and shown to be uniformly bounded in the natural β-weighted broken test graph norm over Lq (for all 1<q<∞, where q is conjugate to trial exponent p). A non-characteristic facet condition is imposed for k≥2, while the lowest-order case (k=1) requires no such condition and admits characteristic facets.
AI.result: The paper proves: (1) practical fully discrete residual minimization is quasioptimal in the DPG energy norm for all 1<p<∞ with a constant governed by the Fortin operator; (2) the computable residual serves as a globally reliable and efficient a posteriori error estimator; (3) augmenting the test space and changing the test norm improves results in the lowest-order case. Results hold in any spatial dimension N for any polynomial degree k≥1 on simplicial meshes.
AI.conclusion: The construction of uniformly bounded Fortin operators enables rigorous quasioptimality and a posteriori error estimation guarantees for DPG discretizations of the advection equation across all spatial dimensions, polynomial degrees, and Lp/Lq settings, with the lowest-order case enjoying the additional flexibility of characteristic facets and improved results via test space augmentation.

title: Critical Morrey Rigidity and Removable Singularities for Five-Dimensional Stationary Navier-Stokes Flows
summary:
We prove a critical Morrey rigidity theorem for the five-dimensional stationary Navier--Stokes equations. More precisely, every smooth solution on $\mathbb R^5\setminus\{0\}$ satisfying \[ \sup_{R>0}R^{-2}\int_{B_R}|u|^3\,dx<\infty \] is identically zero, up to an additive constant in the pressure. This replaces the pointwise Type-I control in the known higher-dimensional rigidity theory by a velocity-only, scale-invariant averaged condition that allows spatial concentration. The proof develops a weak head-pressure mechanism that does not rely on pointwise pressure estimates or classical normal traces. We reconstruct a canonical pressure from the velocity, derive a renormalized inequality for the positive head pressure, and introduce two monotone radial fluxes. Annular energy estimates, suitable-weak compactness, and blow-up and blow-down limits are then used to identify the endpoint fluxes and force rigidity.
  As an application, we obtain a removable-singularity criterion in dimension five: if a suitable weak solution is smooth away from one point and either its scale-invariant Dirichlet energy or its cubic velocity Morrey quantity remains bounded near that point, then the singularity is removable. Thus, within the isolated-singularity class, the smallness assumption in the classical stationary regularity criterion is replaced by boundedness. We also prove the corresponding velocity-only cubic Morrey rigidity theorem in dimension four by a different finite-energy argument.

AI.tldr: This paper proves a critical Morrey rigidity theorem for 5D stationary Navier-Stokes equations: any smooth solution on R^5\{0} with bounded cubic velocity Morrey norm must be zero (up to pressure constant). This replaces pointwise Type-I control with a velocity-only scale-invariant averaged condition. Applications include a removable-singularity criterion in dimension five and a similar velocity-only rigidity theorem in dimension four.
AI.motivation: To extend the higher-dimensional rigidity theory for stationary Navier-Stokes equations by removing the dependence on pointwise Type-I control of the velocity, replacing it with a weaker, scale-invariant averaged (Morrey) condition that permits spatial concentration of the solution.
AI.method: The authors develop a weak head-pressure mechanism that avoids pointwise pressure estimates and classical normal traces. They reconstruct a canonical pressure from the velocity, derive a renormalized inequality for the positive head pressure, and introduce two monotone radial fluxes. Proof techniques include annular energy estimates, suitable-weak compactness, and blow-up/blow-down limits to identify endpoint fluxes and force rigidity.
AI.result: They prove the critical Morrey rigidity theorem in dimension five, yielding a removable-singularity criterion: if a suitable weak solution is smooth away from one point and either its scale-invariant Dirichlet energy or cubic velocity Morrey quantity is bounded near that point, the singularity is removable. They also prove a corresponding velocity-only cubic Morrey rigidity theorem in dimension four via a finite-energy argument.
AI.conclusion: Within the isolated-singularity class, the smallness assumption in the classical stationary regularity criterion can be replaced by boundedness. The result provides a cleaner, velocity-only formulation of rigidity for higher-dimensional stationary Navier-Stokes equations.

title: An Immersed Interface Method for Parabolic Interface Problems with Nonlinear Jump Conditions
summary: We develop an immersed interface finite difference method for a one-dimensional nonlinear parabolic interface problem with jump condition \[ [u]_α=λu^+u^-. \] The method combines a Crank--Nicolson immersed interface discretization with an \(s\)-parameter reduction of the nonlinear interface condition, thereby reducing the nonlinear coupling to a scalar quadratic equation. We also discuss two different viewpoints for combining Newton iteration with immersed interface discretization, namely the IIM--Newton and Newton--IIM formulations. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the behavior and accuracy of the method.

AI.tldr: This paper develops an immersed interface finite difference method for solving a one-dimensional nonlinear parabolic interface problem with a jump condition involving a nonlinear coupling term. The method combines Crank-Nicolson discretization with an s-parameter reduction technique that transforms the nonlinear interface condition into a scalar quadratic equation. Two Newton-type formulations (IIM-Newton and Newton-IIM) are discussed, and numerical experiments demonstrate the method's accuracy and behavior.
AI.motivation: Nonlinear parabolic interface problems with jump conditions arise in various applications, and existing immersed interface methods primarily handle linear jump conditions. There is a need for efficient and accurate numerical methods that can handle nonlinear interface conditions, particularly the product-type jump condition [u]_α = λu^+u^-.
AI.method: The method combines a Crank-Nicolson time discretization with an immersed interface finite difference spatial discretization. The key innovation is an s-parameter reduction that converts the nonlinear interface condition into a scalar quadratic equation, simplifying the coupling. Two Newton iteration strategies are also discussed: IIM-Newton (immersed interface method with Newton for the nonlinearity) and Newton-IIM (Newton iteration applied to the full system with IIM discretization).
AI.result: The method successfully handles the nonlinear interface problem, and numerical experiments illustrate the behavior and accuracy of the proposed approach, demonstrating the effectiveness of the s-parameter reduction strategy alongside the Crank-Nicolson immersed interface discretization.
AI.conclusion: The proposed immersed interface method provides an efficient and accurate approach for solving one-dimensional nonlinear parabolic interface problems with product-type jump conditions, with the s-parameter reduction offering a tractable way to handle the nonlinear coupling and multiple Newton formulations providing flexibility in implementation.

title: Plasmon poles for the linearized Coulomb--Hartree--Fock equation
summary: We study the time-dependent Hartree--Fock equation in $\R^3$ with physical Coulomb interactions in both direct and exchange channels, with exchange coupling $η$, linearized about homogeneous equilibria $γ_f=g(-i\nabla)$ having compact momentum support. Nguyen and You showed that, without exchange, two purely imaginary plasmon poles $\pm iτ_0(|k|)$ exist below a survival threshold $κ_0>0$. Existing nonlinear Hartree--Fock theory requires a short-range direct interaction and a smooth small exchange kernel, excluding the present Coulomb setting. On every compact band $0<k_-\le|k|\le k_+<κ_0$, we prove unconditionally for Coulomb exchange that, for small $|η|$, the poles persist, remain simple and purely imaginary, and depend real-analytically on $η$. Their first-order shift $τ_X$ splits into explicit static self-energy and dynamic vertex corrections. Each pole yields an exact undamped mode with a closed-form unit-density eigenfunction, embedded in the fiber generator's essential spectrum. The causal density Green function splits into an explicit undamped sine wave and a remainder whose Laplace transform is holomorphic near the poles, while the plasmon channel satisfies uniform $t^{-3/2}$ dispersive decay and endpoint Strichartz estimates. A first-order Ward-type cancellation gives $|τ_X(r)|\le Cr^2$ down to $r=0$; hence exchange leaves the plasma gap unchanged to first order, and we obtain a closed formula for the stiffness correction. Numerics for a $C^9$ smoothed Fermi ball support the analysis: self-energy and vertex terms cancel within $1.2\%$ on the computed range, and exchange softens the dispersion most strongly near $0.7\,κ_0$.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that in the time-dependent Hartree-Fock equation with Coulomb interactions, the purely imaginary plasmon poles persist when exchange coupling η is added, remaining simple, purely imaginary, and real-analytic in η. The first-order shift includes static self-energy and dynamic vertex corrections that nearly cancel (Ward-type identity), leaving the plasma gap unchanged to first order. Numerical results on a smoothed Fermi ball confirm the analysis.
AI.motivation: Existing nonlinear Hartree-Fock theory requires a short-range direct interaction and smooth small exchange kernel, which excludes the physically important Coulomb setting. The authors aim to extend the persistence of plasmon poles (established by Nguyen and You for the exchange-free case) to the physically realistic Coulomb exchange setting.
AI.method: The approach proves unconditional persistence of purely imaginary plasmon poles on compact bands away from the survival threshold κ₀, for small exchange coupling |η|. The proof establishes real-analytic dependence on η, derives a closed-form decomposition of the first-order shift into static self-energy and dynamic vertex corrections, and proves dispersive decay (t^{-3/2}) and Strichartz estimates for the plasmon channel. A first-order Ward-type cancellation is established for the shift, and numerics verify the analysis.
AI.result: The poles persist and remain simple and purely imaginary under Coulomb exchange. The first-order shift satisfies |τ_X(r)| ≤ Cr² via Ward-type cancellation, so the plasma gap is unchanged to first order. Numerics for a C⁹ smoothed Fermi ball show self-energy and vertex terms cancel within 1.2%, and exchange softens dispersion most near 0.7κ₀.
AI.conclusion: The paper rigorously extends the theory of plasmon poles to include physical Coulomb exchange in Hartree-Fock dynamics, demonstrating persistence, analyticity, and Ward-type cancellations, with explicit closed-form eigenfunctions and dispersive estimates. The numerical results corroborate the analytical findings.

title: Structure-Preserving Detailed-Balance Master-Equation Discretizations for Fokker--Planck Equations
summary: We develop a variational--Markov construction of detailed-balance master-equation discretizations for Fokker--Planck equations directly from their energy--dissipation laws. Rather than discretizing the differential operator, we represent mass transfer between neighboring grid points by two directional jump rates. On each edge, the discrete energy--dissipation law determines the net flux, while detailed balance fixes the rate ratio; a local reconstruction of edge quantities from neighboring grid-point values then uniquely determines both rates. A logarithmic-mean reconstruction recovers the classical Scharfetter--Gummel/Wang--Peskin--Elston rates, while alternative reconstructions yield other reversible schemes. The resulting semi-discrete systems conserve mass, preserve nonnegativity, satisfy detailed balance, and dissipate a discrete free energy. The same edgewise construction extends to state-dependent and degenerate mobilities, nonlocal interaction energies and higher-dimensional problems. The corresponding implicit and semi-implicit fully discrete schemes are linear, mass-conservative, positivity-preserving, and energy-stable, with a time-step restriction required only for nonlocal interaction energies whose kernel is not negative semidefinite. Numerical experiments confirm the expected spatial convergence rates of all detailed-balance schemes and verify their equilibrium accuracy, positivity preservation, and free-energy decay with discontinuous potentials, saturation, nonlocal interactions, and two-dimensional problems.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a variational-Markov framework for constructing detailed-balance master-equation discretizations of Fokker-Planck equations directly from energy-dissipation laws, producing schemes that conserve mass, preserve positivity, satisfy detailed balance, and dissipate discrete free energy.
AI.motivation: Traditional discretizations of Fokker-Planck equations focus on discretizing the differential operator directly, which may not preserve the underlying physical structure such as detailed balance, nonnegativity, and energy dissipation.
AI.method: The authors represent mass transfer between grid points via two directional jump rates, where the discrete energy-dissipation law determines net flux and detailed balance fixes the rate ratio. A local reconstruction of edge quantities determines both rates uniquely. This edgewise construction extends beyond the classical logarithmic-mean (Scharfetter-Gummel/Wang-Peskin-Elston) to other reversible schemes, and supports state-dependent/degenerate mobilities, nonlocal interactions, and higher dimensions.
AI.result: The resulting semi-discrete and fully discrete schemes are linear, mass-conservative, positivity-preserving, and energy-stable (with a time-step restriction only needed for nonlocal kernels not negative semidefinite). Numerical experiments confirm spatial convergence rates, equilibrium accuracy, positivity preservation, and free-energy decay across various test cases including discontinuous potentials, saturation, nonlocal interactions, and 2D problems.
AI.conclusion: The variational-Markov construction provides a principled, structure-preserving discretization framework for Fokker-Planck equations that unifies and extends classical schemes while guaranteeing key physical properties by construction.

title: Energy identity for Intrinsic Stationary Biharmonic Mappings into Homogeneous Spaces in Supercritical Dimensions
summary: In this paper, we consider energy identity for intrinsic stationary biharmonic maps into homogeneous spaces in supercritical dimensions, extending the corresponding result of Hornung-Moser [Anal. PDE. 2012] in critical dimension. The proof follows a similar strategy as that of Lin-Rivière [Duke Math. J. 2002]. A key ingredient is a conservation law for intrinsic biharmonic maps into homogeneous spaces, which allow us to derive higher regularity of the map.

AI.tldr: This paper proves the energy identity for intrinsic stationary biharmonic maps into homogeneous spaces in supercritical dimensions, extending prior work by Hornung-Moser from the critical dimension case. The proof adapts Lin-Rivière's strategy and relies on a key conservation law for intrinsic biharmonic maps into homogeneous spaces.
AI.motivation: To extend the energy identity result for intrinsic stationary biharmonic maps from the critical dimension (established by Hornung-Moser) to supercritical dimensions, where the analysis is more challenging and requires additional structure.
AI.method: The proof follows the strategy of Lin-Rivière. A key ingredient is deriving a conservation law for intrinsic biharmonic maps into homogeneous spaces, which enables establishing higher regularity of the map—this regularity is essential for proving the energy identity in the supercritical setting.
AI.result: The energy identity is established for intrinsic stationary biharmonic maps into homogeneous spaces in supercritical dimensions.
AI.conclusion: The energy identity holds for intrinsic stationary biharmonic maps into homogeneous spaces beyond the critical dimension, generalizing the earlier critical-dimensional result by Hornung-Moser.

title: Checkerboard Shells: A Position-Only Thin-Shell Discretization with Scale-Compatible Completion
summary: Checkerboard edge-midpoint geometry provides an exact planar Varignon parallelogram for every spatial quadrilateral, allowing a local tangent frame and normal to be recovered directly from nodal positions even when the raw quadrilateral is warped. Building on this property, we develop a position-only thin-shell discretization with no independent director, rotation, or strain variables. The connected edge-midpoint surface is taken as the physical midsurface: the first fundamental form is evaluated on planar B faces, while a W-centered second fundamental form is constructed from variations of neighboring B-face normals, so membrane and bending share the same geometric carrier. A variational-kernel analysis shows that smooth second-order consistency does not eliminate lattice-scale blind modes. After quotienting out the raw checkerboard gauge, the B metric has one physical membrane blind direction and the symmetric W curvature has two curvature blind directions. We introduce a quotient-minimal membrane compatibility coordinate $X_M$ and an objective reference-relative curvature coordinate $X_W^{rel}$, placed consistently in the $O(t)$ membrane and $O(t^3)$ bending sectors. The formulation admits an explicit midpoint quotient, complete flat blind-mode classification, rigid-motion objectivity, reference-state consistency, and an $O(h^2)$ near-isometry approximation result for aligned generalized cylinders. Numerical tests show second-order curvature convergence, targeted removal of the membrane defect, and a sub-percent, refinement-decaying influence of $X_W^{rel}$. Linear and nonlinear shell benchmarks further demonstrate flat bending, curved-shell membrane-bending coupling, thickness sensitivity, large rotation, nonlinear pinching, and localized ovalization within a single position-only framework.

AI.tldr: A position-only thin-shell discretization based on checkerboard edge-midpoint geometry, using B-face planar metrics and W-centered curvatures, with explicit handling of blind mode defects via quotient-minimal coordinates.
AI.motivation: To develop a thin-shell discretization that requires only nodal positions (no independent directors, rotations, or strain variables) while achieving accurate membrane and bending behavior even for warped quadrilaterals, and to systematically understand and eliminate lattice-scale blind (zero-energy) modes.
AI.method: Uses checkerboard edge-midpoint geometry to define an exact planar Varignon parallelogram for each spatial quadrilateral, enabling a local tangent frame and normal from positions alone. The edge-midpoint surface serves as the physical midsurface: first fundamental form on planar B faces, and a W-centered second fundamental form from neighboring B-face normal variations. A variational-kernel analysis classifies blind modes; quotient-minimal coordinates X_M (membrane) and X_W^rel (curvature) are introduced to resolve them.
AI.result: Second-order curvature convergence, targeted removal of the membrane defect, sub-percent refinement-decaying influence of X_W^rel, and O(h^2) near-isometry for aligned generalized cylinders. Benchmarks show flat bending, membrane-bending coupling, thickness sensitivity, large rotation, pinching, and ovalization within a single position-only framework.
AI.conclusion: The checkerboard edge-midpoint formulation yields a complete position-only thin-shell framework with explicit blind-mode classification, rigid-motion objectivity, and reference-state consistency, validated across linear and nonlinear shell benchmarks.

title: Existence of Periodic Solutions to Steady Viscous Burgers Equation with a General Force
summary: In this paper, we will construct periodic solutions to the viscous steady Burgers equation with an external force $f(x)$, based on the following formal expansion $u^\varepsilon(x)=u_0(x)+\varepsilon u_1(x)+\cdots+\varepsilon^n u_n(x)+\cdots$, where $\varepsilon \ge 0$ represents the viscosity and $u_0(x)$ is a solution to non-viscous steady Burgers equation with the external force $f(x)$. We will focus on the solutions which are uniformly bounded with respect to the viscosity. In our previous work, starting from $u_0=-(2+\cos x)$, the authors constructed the periodic solutions to the viscous steady Burgers equation with the external force $f=u_0(x)u_{0x}=-2\sin x-\sin x\cos x$. In this paper, we will extend the main result obtained in our previous work and construct the solutions starting from general $u_0$ and $f$ satisfying the non-viscous steady Burgers equation $u_0(x)u_{0x}=f$. It will be shown that there exists a $\varepsilon_0>0$, which depends on $n$, such that for any $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0$, the viscous steady Burgers equation with the external force $f$ has a periodic solution $u^\varepsilon(x) \in C^2([0,2π])$, satisfying $|u^\varepsilon(x)-u_0(x)-\varepsilon u_1(x)-\cdots-\varepsilon^n u_n(x)| \leq C\varepsilon^{n+1}$, where $C>0$ is a constant which depends on $n$, but is independent of $\varepsilon$. Compared with Jauslin-Kreiss-Moser's result, we present a new approach to construct periodic solutions to the viscous steady Burgers with a general external force. The constructed solutions will tend to the ones of the non-viscous Burgers equation with a sharper convergence rate (up to higher order) when the viscosity vanishes.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs periodic solutions to the viscous steady Burgers equation with a general external force using a formal asymptotic expansion in the viscosity parameter ε, proving the existence of solutions that are uniformly bounded up to arbitrary order n with convergence rate ε^(n+1).
AI.motivation: The authors aim to extend their previous work (which used a specific starting solution u0 = -(2+cos x)) to general solutions u0 of the non-viscous steady Burgers equation, and to improve upon existing results (notably Jauslin-Kreiss-Moser) by providing a new approach with sharper convergence rates.
AI.method: The method is a formal asymptotic expansion u^ε(x) = u0(x) + εu1(x) + ... + ε^n u_n(x) + ... where u0 satisfies the inviscid Burgers equation. The authors construct periodic solutions to the viscous equation with general external force f, establishing existence of solutions with error bounded by C·ε^(n+1).
AI.result: It is shown that there exists ε0 > 0 (depending on n) such that for any 0 < ε < ε0, the viscous steady Burgers equation with external force f has a C² periodic solution on [0,2π] satisfying the stated error bound, where the constant C depends on n but is independent of ε.
AI.conclusion: The authors present a new approach to constructing periodic solutions to the viscous steady Burgers equation with a general external force, achieving sharper (higher-order) convergence rates to the inviscid solutions as viscosity vanishes, compared to previous results.

title: Mesh-Uniform Power Stability of Two-Relaxation-Time Vector Lattice Boltzmann Schemes with Reversible Boundaries
summary: We consider the collision-transport operator for vector-valued two-relaxation-time lattice Boltzmann schemes linearized about a uniform rest state. Assume that the equilibrium blocks are positive definite and that the link-even and link-odd relaxation parameters satisfy s_+ + s_- = 2 and 0 < s_- < 2. If the homogeneous transport is unitary in the equilibrium metric and reversible under velocity exchange, then the powers of the amplification operator are bounded uniformly with respect to the number and arrangement of lattice nodes. The admissible transports include periodic transport, vector halfway bounce-back, coordinate-aligned specular reflection, tangential orthogonal involutions, and compatible multi-channel scattering. The proof reduces the population equation to a two-step macroscopic recurrence generated by a contraction. An inclusion of the numerical range in an ellipse, combined with the Crouzeix-Palencia theorem, yields a dimension-independent estimate for the companion operator and hence the population bound. For a three-coefficient off-midpoint boundary interpolation, we give an exact rational D2N5 example whose finite-domain amplification matrix has a real eigenvalue larger than one, although the interpolation coefficients and bulk parameters are admissible. Thus coefficient convexity alone does not ensure stability for this boundary family.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the stability of vector-valued two-relaxation-time lattice Boltzmann schemes by studying the collision-transport operator. Under conditions of positive-definite equilibrium blocks, relaxation parameters satisfying s_+ + s_- = 2 with 0 < s_- < 2, and unitary/reversible homogeneous transport, the authors prove that powers of the amplification operator are bounded uniformly independent of lattice node count and arrangement. They reduce the population equation to a two-step macroscopic recurrence, use numerical range ellipse inclusion with the Crouzeix-Palencia theorem to obtain dimension-independent estimates, and demonstrate via a counterexample that convexity of interpolation coefficients does not guarantee stability for a three-coefficient off-midpoint boundary scheme.
AI.motivation: The work aims to establish rigorous stability conditions for vector-valued two-relaxation-time lattice Boltzmann (TRT) schemes with various boundary conditions, including periodic, bounce-back, specular reflection, and scattering boundaries. A key motivation is to characterize when stability is guaranteed independent of lattice geometry, and to test whether coefficient convexity alone suffices for stability in higher-order boundary interpolation schemes.
AI.method: The proof reduces the vector-valued population equation to a two-step macroscopic recurrence generated by a contraction. Stability is established by showing the numerical range of the companion operator lies in an ellipse, then applying the Crouzeix-Palencia theorem for a dimension-independent bound. Counterexamples are constructed analytically, including a rational D2N5 example with admissible parameters but an unstable eigenvalue.
