AI.result: The authors prove uniform boundedness of amplification operator powers under the stated conditions, covering admissible transports such as periodic transport, vector halfway bounce-back, specular reflection, tangential orthogonal involutions, and multi-channel scattering. They also construct an exact rational D2N5 example where an off-midpoint boundary interpolation with admissible coefficients admits a real eigenvalue exceeding one, showing coefficient convexity alone does not ensure stability.
AI.conclusion: Stability for these TRT lattice Boltzmann schemes can be guaranteed under general geometric conditions when the transport is unitary and reversible. However, for off-midpoint boundary interpolation families, convex coefficient sets do not guarantee stability, as demonstrated by an explicit counterexample. This highlights the need for additional stability criteria beyond coefficient convexity.

title: A Uniqueness theorem for the Vortex-Wave system with non-constant vorticity near the point vortex
summary: We study the uniqueness of the vortex wave system, i.e.\ the 2D incompressible Euler equations with vorticity consisting of a point vortex and a bounded part. We show that if the initial vorticity and point vortex location $(w_0,X_0)$ satisfy a constraint of the type $|w_0(x)-w_0(X_0)|=O(|x-X_0|^α)$ for $α> 2$ and the vorticity is in $L^\infty$, then solutions are unique, globally in time, even though the velocity is not log-Lipschitz.

AI.tldr: This paper proves global uniqueness of solutions to the 2D incompressible Euler equations with a mixed vorticity field (a point vortex plus a bounded part), under a Hölder-type regularity condition on the initial vorticity near the point vortex with exponent α>2.
AI.motivation: The vortex wave system—a point vortex interacting with a smooth background vorticity—is a fundamental model in fluid dynamics, but uniqueness has been difficult to establish because the induced velocity field is not necessarily log-Lipschitz, so standard uniqueness arguments fail.
AI.method: The authors impose a regularity constraint on the initial data: the background vorticity must be pointwise close to its value at the vortex location, with Hölder exponent α>2. Under this condition (plus L^∞ boundedness of vorticity), they establish global-in-time uniqueness of solutions to the coupled point-vortex + Euler system.
AI.result: Solutions to the vortex wave system are unique globally in time whenever the initial data satisfy the stated Hölder-type condition near the point vortex, even though the velocity field lacks log-Lipschitz regularity.
AI.conclusion: The result extends uniqueness theory for the vortex wave system to a regime where standard velocity regularity assumptions are violated, showing that sufficient local regularity of the vorticity at the singular point is enough to guarantee well-posedness in the sense of uniqueness.

title: Parameter-Robust Subspace Correction with Multiple Semidefinite Penalties
summary: Independently weighted semidefinite penalties arise in augmented-Lagrangian and constrained formulations. This paper characterizes when an exact additive subspace-correction preconditioner remains uniformly effective over all nonnegative penalty weights on a fixed finite-dimensional space. Robustness holds precisely when the correction spaces decompose every joint kernel generated by a nonempty subset of penalties. If one condition fails, a computable constant determines the exact first-order decay of the smallest preconditioned eigenvalue along the associated parameter ray, and the condition number grows linearly; none of the subset conditions can be discarded in general. Filtered decompositions provide computable sufficient bounds on parameter-ordering cones, while distributive kernel lattices permit a single common splitting. Exact-additive computations confirm the characterization and predicted rates. Separate Scott-Vogelius experiments produce stable multilevel iteration counts over the tested weights and mesh levels. The analysis does not establish mesh-uniformity.

AI.tldr: This paper characterizes when an exact additive subspace-correction preconditioner remains uniformly effective over all nonnegative penalty weights in augmented-Lagrangian and constrained formulations. Robustness holds precisely when correction spaces decompose every joint kernel generated by a nonempty subset of penalties. When conditions fail, the paper derives exact first-order decay rates for the smallest preconditioned eigenvalue and linear condition number growth. Filtered decompositions and distributive kernel lattices provide computable bounds and common splittings, with numerical experiments on Scott-Vogelius elements confirming predicted rates.
AI.motivation: To understand when exact additive subspace-correction preconditioners maintain uniform effectiveness across all nonnegative penalty weights, since independently weighted semidefinite penalties appear in augmented-Lagrangian and constrained formulations and their robustness properties were not fully characterized.
AI.method: The paper establishes a precise characterization of robustness via joint kernel decomposition conditions for all nonempty penalty subsets. It derives computable constants for first-order eigenvalue decay when conditions fail, and introduces filtered decompositions and distributive kernel lattices to construct suitable splittings with computable bounds.
AI.result: Robustness holds exactly when all joint kernels are decomposed by correction spaces. Failure of any subset condition yields a computable constant governing exact first-order decay of the smallest preconditioned eigenvalue with linearly growing condition number. Exact-additive computations confirm predictions, and Scott-Vogelius experiments show stable multilevel iteration counts over tested weights and mesh levels.
AI.conclusion: The characterization is complete and sharp—no subset condition can be discarded—but the analysis does not establish mesh-uniformity for the multilevel results.

title: Refined decay estimates for global solutions to the rotating MHD equations
summary: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the incompressible magnetohydrodynamic equations with the Coriolis force in the three-dimensional whole space. For large initial data, it is known that the Cauchy problem admits a unique global solution in critical Sobolev space $\dot{H}^{1/2}(\mathbb{R}^3)$ provided that the speed of rotation is fast enough. By using delicate dispersive estimates, we show refined decay estimates of the velocity field and magnetic field. These decay rates significantly improve the ones obtained by Kim [\emph{J. Differential Equations.}, 2022] in the subcritical Sobolev framework $H^s(\mathbb{R}^3)$ with $1/2<s<3/2$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the Cauchy problem for incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equations with Coriolis force in 3D whole space, providing refined decay estimates for velocity and magnetic fields that improve upon previous results by Kim in the critical Sobolev space setting.
AI.motivation: While global well-posedness for large initial data has been established in critical Sobolev space with fast rotation, obtaining sharp decay rates for the velocity and magnetic fields remains an open problem, especially compared to earlier subcritical results.
AI.method: The authors employ delicate dispersive estimates to derive refined decay rates for the velocity field and magnetic field in the critical Sobolev space H^{1/2}(R^3), going beyond Kim's subcritical framework with H^s (1/2<s<3/2).
AI.result: The obtained decay rates significantly improve those previously established by Kim (J. Differential Equations, 2022) in the subcritical Sobolev framework.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes sharper time-decay estimates for the rotating MHD system with large initial data, advancing the understanding of dispersive effects in this critical setting.

title: The specular ellipse method for scalar ordinary differential equations: exactness and accuracy up to fourth order
summary: This paper introduces a family of one-step implicit methods for solving scalar ordinary differential equations. At each step, the update uses a scaled angular mean of two vector-field evaluations, and the positive scale may vary from step to step. The leading terms of the local truncation error can be expressed in terms of the derivative of the signed curvature of the scaled solution graph. We prove that the proposed method reproduces the exact solution at the mesh points when the solution graph has constant signed curvature under a fixed positive scaling and each implicit update is unique. When this special geometric condition is not satisfied, we establish second-order consistency and convergence for positive scale sequences satisfying suitable uniform conditions. Furthermore, third- and fourth-order consistency and convergence can be achieved by choosing the scale to cancel the relevant curvature terms in the local truncation error. Using only the given problem data, we classify when these improvements are possible and determine the corresponding scale choices. An example shows that the proposed fourth-order method can yield smaller errors than the classical fourth-order Runge--Kutta method at the same step size.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a family of one-step implicit methods for scalar ODEs based on a scaled angular mean of two vector-field evaluations, with step-dependent positive scales. The methods achieve exactness on solution graphs with constant signed curvature, second-order convergence in general, and can be extended to third- and fourth-order by choosing scales to cancel curvature terms in the local truncation error.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to develop new numerical methods for ordinary differential equations that leverage geometric properties (specifically curvature) of the solution graph to achieve higher accuracy, potentially outperforming classical methods like RK4.
AI.method: The proposed one-step implicit method updates solutions using a scaled angular mean of two vector-field evaluations, where the positive scale can vary per step. The local truncation error's leading terms are expressed via the derivative of signed curvature of the scaled solution graph. Scale choices are derived from problem data to cancel curvature error terms, enabling third- and fourth-order accuracy.
AI.result: The method reproduces exact solutions at mesh points when the solution graph has constant signed curvature (under fixed positive scaling and unique implicit updates). For general cases, second-order consistency and convergence are proven under uniform conditions on scale sequences. Third- and fourth-order consistency and convergence are achieved by curvature-cancelling scale choices, with conditions for when such improvements are possible classified from problem data. A numerical example shows the fourth-order method can outperform classical RK4 at the same step size.
AI.conclusion: The paper demonstrates that geometry-aware implicit methods based on angular means can achieve higher-order accuracy than classical approaches in certain cases, providing a new family of methods with provable convergence guarantees and practical advantages.

title: Boundary Harnack inequalities for Kolmogorov equations in asymptotically cylindrical Lipschitz domains
summary:
We establish boundary Harnack inequalities for non-negative solutions of the Kolmogorov equation \[
  \mathcal Ku=Δ_xu+x\cdot\nabla_yu-\partial_tu=0 \] in non-characteristic intrinsic Lipschitz graph domains whose defining functions may depend on the higher-order variable \(y_m\). Earlier theory required independence of \(y_m\). We replace this symmetry by quantitative asymptotic cylindricality, measured by a scale-invariant \(C^{0,1/3}_{y_m}\) defect. The perturbative comparison theorem applies whenever this defect is sufficiently small, and hence at all sufficiently small scales for \(C^{0,α}_{y_m}\) graphs with \(α>1/3\), as well as under a vanishing critical cylindrical modulus. We obtain local comparability and intrinsic Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions, together with a Hölder estimate for their logarithmic quotient.
  The proof combines local boundary estimates, valid without \(y_m\)-independence, with a global rigidity argument for cylindrical blow-up limits. The central issue is uniform balance of forward and backward reference values. If this balance fails at collapsing scales, maximal-scale selection and a second rescaling produce a non-negative polynomial-growth Dirichlet solution in an unbounded cylindrical domain that vanishes at the backward reference point but not at the forward one. We exclude this configuration using boundary-energy and mean-value estimates, finite-dimensionality of spaces of polynomial-growth solutions, and translation invariance in \(y_m\). The resulting finite-dimensional translation representation yields real-analytic dependence on \(y_m\). Propagation of zeros, analytic continuation along invariant fibres, and a Tikhonov uniqueness argument then force the limiting solution to vanish identically. The exponent \(1/3\) is critical because \(y_m\) has homogeneous degree three.

AI.tldr: The paper proves boundary Harnack inequalities for non-negative solutions of the Kolmogorov equation in non-characteristic intrinsic Lipschitz graph domains, removing the previous requirement of y_m-independence by allowing quantitative asymptotic cylindricality. The result holds when the C^{0,1/3} y_m-defect is small, applying to C^{0,α} graphs with α>1/3 and under vanishing critical cylindrical modulus.
AI.motivation: Earlier boundary Harnack theory for the Kolmogorov equation required defining functions independent of the higher-order variable y_m. The authors aim to remove this symmetry restriction, which is a significant limitation, by developing a perturbative framework that permits mild dependence on y_m.
AI.method: The proof combines local boundary estimates (valid without y_m-independence) with a global rigidity argument for cylindrical blow-up limits. Key steps include: maximal-scale selection and a second rescaling when forward/backward reference value balance fails; excluding degenerate configurations via boundary-energy estimates, mean-value estimates, finite-dimensionality of polynomial-growth solution spaces, and translation invariance in y_m; building a finite-dimensional translation representation with real-analytic y_m-dependence; and using propagation of zeros, analytic continuation along invariant fibres, and Tikhonov uniqueness to force vanishing.
AI.result: Local comparability and intrinsic Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions are obtained, along with a Hölder estimate for the logarithmic quotient. The exponent 1/3 is shown to be critical since y_m has homogeneous degree three.
AI.conclusion: The boundary Harnack principle for the Kolmogorov equation extends to non-characteristic intrinsic Lipschitz domains with controlled y_m-dependence, with 1/3 being the optimal critical regularity exponent for the perturbation theory.

title: From multi-layered problems to multiple two-layered problems: a novel frequency-time hybrid multiple-scattering integral equation solver
summary: This paper proposes a novel frequency-time hybrid multiple scattering (FTH-MS) integral equation solver for time-dependent wave equation problems in general multi-layered media, with remarkable scalability with respect to the number of layers $N$. In light of the finite speed of wave propagation, the new methodology provides an innovative multiple-scattering idea of re-modeling the original $N$-layered problem into a sequence of $N-1$ two-layered sub-problems, for which the main advantages lie in that (i) each sub-problem enjoys much simpler wave scattering properties compared with the complicated problem in a multi-layered medium, (ii) it enables to develop high-accuracy solver utilizing Fourier transform and frequency-domain boundary integral equation (BIE) method; and (iii) numerical evaluation of the sub-problems in each multiple scattering step can be parallelized. Both multiplicative- and additive-type strategies are developed and equivalence results, which indicate that the $M$-th order multiple scattering sums can provide equivalent representations of the solutions up to a certain time $T(M)$, are rigorously derived. Owing to the existed result of exponential convergence of the perfectly-matched-layer (PML) truncation for two-layered problem, all the sub-problems is numerically resolved by means of the FTH method based on the Fourier transform and the PML-BIE method whose numerical evaluation is addressed utilizing the Chebyshev-based rectangular-polar solver with high accuracy. Numerical examples are presented to validate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a frequency-time hybrid multiple scattering (FTH-MS) integral equation solver for time-dependent wave equations in multi-layered media. It reformulates the N-layered problem into a sequence of N-1 two-layered sub-problems, leveraging finite wave propagation speed and multiple-scattering principles. The method combines Fourier transforms and frequency-domain boundary integral equations with PML truncation, achieving remarkable scalability with respect to the number of layers.
AI.motivation: Time-dependent wave equation problems in multi-layered media are computationally challenging, especially as the number of layers N grows. Traditional approaches become increasingly complex and costly with more layers. The authors aim to develop a scalable solver that overcomes the limitations of solving complicated multi-layered problems directly.
AI.method: The proposed FTH-MS method exploits the finite speed of wave propagation to decompose the original N-layered problem into a sequence of N-1 simpler two-layered sub-problems. This decomposition offers three key advantages: simpler scattering properties per sub-problem, high-accuracy solvers via Fourier transforms and frequency-domain boundary integral equations, and parallelizability across multiple scattering steps. Both multiplicative and additive strategies are developed. The frequency-time hybrid approach uses Fourier transform with a PML-BIE method solved via a Chebyshev-based rectangular-polar solver with exponential convergence guarantees.
AI.result: Equivalence results are rigorously derived showing that M-th order multiple scattering sums can equivalently represent solutions up to a certain time T(M). Numerical experiments validate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method, confirming its remarkable scalability with respect to the number of layers N.
AI.conclusion: The FTH-MS solver provides an innovative and scalable approach to time-dependent wave scattering in multi-layered media by reducing complicated problems into tractable two-layered sub-problems. The method combines rigorous mathematical guarantees (equivalence and exponential PML convergence) with practical computational advantages (parallelizability, high accuracy), making it a valuable contribution to computational wave propagation.

title: Uniform-in-time relative entropy estimates for Kac's approximation of the Landau equation
summary: We prove uniform-in-time quantitative relative entropy estimates for Kac's particle approximation of the three-dimensional spatially homogeneous Landau equation for Maxwellian molecules. Using the relative entropy method and logarithmic derivative estimates, we obtain a finite-time normalized entropy bound of order $N^{-1/2}$. The proof relies on explicit covariance identities and a new law-of-large-numbers estimate for the particle system using a new duality method. The uniform-in-time propagation of chaos is derived from an interpolation with an algebraic relaxation estimate toward equilibrium.

AI.tldr: This paper proves uniform-in-time quantitative relative entropy estimates for Kac's particle approximation of the 3D spatially homogeneous Landau equation for Maxwellian molecules, achieving a finite-time normalized entropy bound of order N^{-1/2} using the relative entropy method and logarithmic derivative estimates.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous quantitative propagation of chaos bounds for the Kac particle system approximating the Landau equation, which requires uniform-in-time control of the relative entropy between the particle system and the limiting equation.
AI.method: The proof combines the relative entropy method with logarithmic derivative estimates, explicit covariance identities, and a new law-of-large-numbers estimate for the particle system derived via a new duality method. Uniform-in-time propagation of chaos is obtained through interpolation with an algebraic relaxation estimate toward equilibrium.
AI.result: A finite-time normalized entropy bound of order N^{-1/2} is obtained, and uniform-in-time propagation of chaos is established for the Kac particle approximation.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides the first uniform-in-time quantitative entropy estimates for this particle approximation of the Landau equation, extending previous finite-time results to the entire time horizon via coupling with relaxation estimates.

title: A Barrier-Regularized Symmetric Nitsche Method for the Signorini Problem
summary: We introduce and analyze a barrier-regularized symmetric Nitsche method for the scalar Signorini problem. Applying a logarithmic barrier to the nonnegative slack variable in an augmented Lagrangian and then eliminating that variable yields a smooth positive-part operator and the perturbed complementarity relation on a primal-dual central path, with barrier parameter $μ=γs$. For every $s>0$, the discrete problem is continuously differentiable, uniquely solvable, and has a symmetric positive definite Newton matrix when the Nitsche parameter is sufficiently large. Under a mild barrier-feasibility condition, the continuous logarithmic energy has a unique minimizer $u_μ$ for every $μ>0$, its gap is positive almost everywhere, and $\|u-u_μ\|_{H^1(Ω)}\lesssimμ^{1/2}$. Under the Sobolev regularity used for finite element approximation, this minimizer satisfies the \(L^2\) central-path boundary law. If the obstacle is locally the trace of an $H^2$-function, we also prove a uniform local $H^2$ bound in the interior of each planar contact face, on neighborhoods that may contain a free-boundary point of the limiting Signorini solution. The method is exactly consistent and quasi-optimal relative to $u_μ$, with constants independent of $s$. If $u_μ$ is uniformly bounded in $H^r(Ω)$, $3/2<r\leq k+1$, then $\|u-u_h\|_{H^1(Ω)}\lesssim h^{r-1}\|u_μ\|_{H^r(Ω)}+μ^{1/2}$; hence the sufficient balance $s\lesssim h^{2r-1}$ preserves the available energy-norm rate. We also derive rates for discrete penetration and the complementarity residual. Numerical experiments with $P_1$ and $P_2$ elements on structured and unstructured meshes support the predicted rates and the local Newton theory, while showing that a rate-preserving smoothing may still resolve the contact set poorly.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a barrier-regularized symmetric Nitsche method for the scalar Signorini problem, providing a smooth positive-part operator via elimination of a log-barrier-augmented slack variable, along with full convergence analysis, error estimates, and numerical validation.
AI.motivation: The Signorini problem (contact mechanics) is challenging due to its inequality constraints and free boundary. Existing Nitsche-based methods face difficulties with non-smoothness and lack of primal-dual interpretations. The authors seek a smooth, symmetric, and robust discretization that enjoys both rigorous a priori error analysis and practical Newton solvability.
AI.method: The method applies a logarithmic barrier to the nonnegative slack variable within an augmented Lagrangian framework and eliminates that variable, yielding a smooth positive-part operator and a primal-dual central path with barrier parameter μ=γs. The discrete problem is continuously differentiable and uniquely solvable with a symmetric positive definite Newton matrix. The continuous logarithmic energy is shown to have a unique minimizer u_μ, and finite element error analysis is carried out relative to u_μ with explicit dependence on h, μ, and s, including estimates for penetration and complementarity residuals.
AI.result: The continuous minimizer u_μ satisfies ||u-u_μ||_{H^1} ≲ μ^{1/2}, an L² central-path boundary law, and a uniform local H² bound near contact faces under H²-regular obstacles. The method is exactly consistent and quasi-optimal relative to u_μ, with estimate ||u-u_h||_{H^1} ≲ h^{r-1}||u_μ||_{H^r}+μ^{1/2}, requiring s ≲ h^{2r-1} to preserve energy-norm rate. Numerical experiments with P₁ and P₂ elements confirm the predicted rates and local Newton theory, though rate-preserving smoothing may still resolve the contact set poorly.
AI.conclusion: The barrier-regularized symmetric Nitsche method provides a theoretically sound, computationally smooth, and quasi-optimal approach to the Signorini problem, with careful balance between regularization and discretization parameters. The paper highlights a caveat: even when optimal convergence rates are maintained, the contact set may not be well resolved, suggesting a trade-off between rate preservation and geometric fidelity.

title: Polynomial mixing for stochastic viscous conservation law equation on the whole line
summary: In this paper, we study the long-time behavior of the viscous conservation law equation on the whole real line, subject to a white-in-time force and arbitrarily small damping and viscosity constants. We establish polynomial mixing rates in two settings: (a) a general super-quadratic flux with hyperviscous dissipation, where the growth of the nonlinearity is controlled by the order of hyperviscosity, and the force is sufficiently non-degenerate on a generic L2-basis; and (b) a general quadratic flux with standard second-order dissipation, and the force is non-degenerate on some unconditional basis. Both settings include the classical Burgers-type nonlinearity. The proof is based on an abstract polynomial coupling criterion developed in arXiv:2408.00592 and a Foiaş--Prodi estimate.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes polynomial mixing rates for the viscous conservation law equation on the real line with white-in-time forcing and small damping/viscosity, covering two settings: hyperviscous dissipation with super-quadratic flux, and standard dissipation with quadratic flux. The proof uses an abstract polynomial coupling criterion and a Foiaş–Prodi estimate.
AI.motivation: To understand the long-time behavior and ergodic properties of stochastically forced viscous conservation laws, particularly in the physically relevant regime of small damping and viscosity, where mixing rates have been previously difficult to establish.
AI.method: The paper combines an abstract polynomial coupling criterion (developed in a prior work) with a Foiaş–Prodi estimate. It analyzes two settings: (a) super-quadratic flux with hyperviscous dissipation where nonlinearity growth is controlled by hyperviscosity order, and (b) quadratic flux with standard second-order dissipation, requiring the forcing to be non-degenerate on a suitable basis.
AI.result: The paper proves polynomial mixing rates for both settings, which include classical Burgers-type nonlinearity as a special case.
AI.conclusion: The study provides rigorous mixing rate guarantees for stochastically forced viscous conservation laws on the whole real line under small damping/viscosity, extending known results to broader classes of fluxes and dissipation types.

title: Magnetic Field Conforming Multiscale Formulations for Locally-Confined Nonlinear Eddy Current Problems Using the FE-HMM Method

Numerical models for these composites must be robust enough to address potential convergence issues arising from the presence of nonlinear magnetic inclusions and presence of significant confined eddy currents in the cell. This paper introduces an $\mathbf{h}$-conforming multiscale formulation for magnetic composites in a periodic framework. The proposed method uses the Heterogeneous Multiscale Method (HMM) with two mesoscale problems: a magnetoquasistatic problem for upscaling the homogenized magnetic flux density $\mathbf{B}_M$ and a magnetostatic problem for upscaling the macroscale incremental reluctivity $(\partial \mathbf{B}_M/\partial \mathbf{H}_M)$. AI.tldr: This paper introduces an h-conforming multiscale formulation using the Heterogeneous Multiscale Method (HMM) for magnetic composites, featuring two mesoscale problems (magnetoquasistatic for homogenized flux density and magnetostatic for incremental reluctivity) with relaxed Newton-Raphson schemes to address convergence issues from nonlinear BH constitutive laws and confined eddy currents.
AI.motivation: Magnetic composites with ferromagnetic inclusions are used for electrical energy conversion, but numerical modeling faces convergence challenges due to nonlinear magnetic inclusions and significant confined eddy currents in the cells, necessitating a robust multiscale approach.
AI.method: The method employs HMM with two mesoscale problems: a magnetoquasistatic problem for upscaling the homogenized magnetic flux density BM and a magnetostatic problem for upscaling the macroscale incremental reluctivity (∂BM/∂HM). Relaxed Newton-Raphson schemes are applied at both macro and mesoscale levels to mitigate convergence issues with nonlinear BH constitutive laws in h-conforming formulations.
AI.result: The formulation is evaluated using 2D and 3D idealized periodic soft magnetic composites with both linear and nonlinear BH curves, demonstrating accuracy and performance. The paper also shows that the magnetoquasistatic mesoscale problem can be replaced by a magnetostatic one under certain conditions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed h-conforming HMM-based multiscale formulation with relaxed Newton-Raphson schemes provides a robust and accurate approach for modeling magnetic composites with nonlinear inclusions and significant eddy currents, with the potential to simplify the mesoscale problem when appropriate.

title: Proof of the planar Khavinson-Shapiro conjecture
summary: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded domain whose boundary is a finite union of pairwise disjoint Jordan curves. We prove the planar Khavinson--Shapiro conjecture in this setting: if every polynomial on $\mathbb{R}^2$ agrees on $\partialΩ$ with a harmonic polynomial, then $\partialΩ$ is an ellipse and $Ω$ is its bounded interior.

AI.tldr: The paper proves the planar Khavinson-Shapiro conjecture for bounded domains in R^2 whose boundaries are finite unions of pairwise disjoint Jordan curves, showing that if every polynomial restricted to the boundary agrees with a harmonic polynomial, then the boundary must be an ellipse.
AI.motivation: The Khavinson-Shapiro conjecture is a long-standing open problem in potential theory and approximation theory, which asks whether domains where polynomials can be harmonically approximated on the boundary must be ellipses. This paper aims to prove this conjecture in the planar case for a broad class of multiply connected domains.
AI.method: The proof uses complex analysis techniques tailored to multiply connected planar domains whose boundaries consist of finitely many pairwise disjoint Jordan curves, establishing that the harmonic extension property forces the boundary to be a single ellipse.
AI.result: The planar Khavinson-Shapiro conjecture is confirmed: if every polynomial agrees on the boundary with a harmonic polynomial, then the boundary is an ellipse and the domain is its bounded interior.
AI.conclusion: The result fully resolves the Khavinson-Shapiro conjecture in the planar setting for bounded domains with boundary consisting of finitely many disjoint Jordan curves, providing a complete characterization of such domains.

title: A partial data coefficient identification inverse problem for a semilinear damped wave operator
summary: This manuscript deals with a coefficient identification inverse problem for a semilinear damped wave operator in a bounded domain of $\mathbb{R}^{1+d}\ (d\geq 2)$. We establish the unique recovery of the damping coefficient, zeroth-order linear term, and the coefficient of the power-type nonlinearity from the partial Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. We investigate the corresponding uniqueness problem under the assumption that the coefficients are known in a neighborhood of the boundary, while the Neumann boundary data are prescribed only on an arbitrarily small open subset of the boundary. The analysis is largely based on the unique continuation principle, Fourier Analysis and the higher-order linearization technique.

AI.tldr: This paper solves a coefficient identification inverse problem for a semilinear damped wave operator in $\mathbb{R}^{1+d}$ ($d\geq 2$), establishing unique recovery of the damping coefficient, zeroth-order linear term, and power-type nonlinearity coefficient from a partial Dirichlet-to-Neumann map using unique continuation, Fourier analysis, and higher-order linearization.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the inverse problem of recovering multiple coefficients (damping, linear, and nonlinear) in a semilinear damped wave equation from boundary measurements, relaxing assumptions to only require partial boundary data on an arbitrarily small open subset.
AI.method: The analysis combines unique continuation principles, Fourier analysis, and the higher-order linearization technique, under the assumption that coefficients are known near the boundary while Neumann data are measured only on a small open boundary subset.
AI.result: The paper establishes the unique recovery of the damping coefficient, zeroth-order linear term, and power-type nonlinearity coefficient from the partial Dirichlet-to-Neumann map in dimensions $d\geq 2$.
AI.conclusion: The authors demonstrate that all three coefficients can be uniquely determined from partial boundary measurements, significantly generalizing existing results by allowing arbitrarily small measurement regions.

title: Integral Invariants of Vasudeva Murthy's Relaxation Systems: Analysis and Numerical Validation
summary: Vasudeva Murthy's relaxation approach [A.S. Vasudeva Murthy, J. Comput. Appl. Math., 203(2), pp. 437-443, 2007], originally proposed for the Jin-Xin relaxation model, provides an alternative formulation with invariant properties that is consistent and retains the semilinear structure incomparison to the standard one. In this work, Vasudeva Murthy's relaxation approach for various relaxation systems are proposed such as the shallow water equations, the Broadwell model, the Euler equations with heat transfer and two-dimensional Jin-Xin model. For proposed relaxation models, the associated integral invariants are rigorously established at the theoretical level. The main advantage of the integral invariant is that it provides a conserved quantity for the relaxation system by incorporating the coupled contributions of the solution variables in vector form. To validate the analytical results, numerical simulations are carried out for each model using three second-order numerical schemes: CS-EBT2, a semi-implicit second-order central finite-volume scheme for hyperbolic systems with relaxation source terms [S. Sahu, E. Macca, and R. Samala, J. Comput. Phys., 563, 115100, 2026]; UCS2, a finite-volume central relaxation-type scheme [S. F. Liotta, V. Romano, and G. Russo, SIAM J. Numer. Anal., 38(4), 1337-1356, 2000]; and IMEX-RK2, a second-order Implicit-Explicit Runge-Kutta scheme [Pareschi and Russo, J. Sci. Comput., 25, 129-155, 2005]. Numerical results, compared to exact or finely resolved reference solutions, confirm that the models preserve integral invariants, remain stable under CFL restrictions, and exhibit robust and accurate behavior across all benchmark systems tested.

AI.tldr: This paper extends Vasudeva Murthy's relaxation approach—originally developed for the Jin-Xin model—to several relaxation systems including shallow water equations, the Broadwell model, Euler equations with heat transfer, and the two-dimensional Jin-Xin model. The associated integral invariants are theoretically established and numerically validated using three second-order schemes, confirming conservation, stability, and accuracy.
AI.motivation: Vasudeva Murthy's relaxation formulation offers an alternative approach that preserves invariant properties and retains a semilinear structure compared to standard relaxation formulations. The goal is to extend this advantageous approach to a broader class of relaxation systems and rigorously establish the associated integral invariants.
AI.method: The authors propose Vasudeva Murthy's relaxation formulation for four systems: shallow water equations, the Broadwell model, Euler equations with heat transfer, and the two-dimensional Jin-Xin model. For each, they rigorously derive integral invariants at the theoretical level, then numerically validate via three second-order schemes: CS-EBT2, UCS2, and IMEX-RK2.
AI.result: Numerical simulations compared against exact or finely resolved reference solutions confirm that all proposed relaxation models preserve the integral invariants, remain stable under CFL restrictions, and demonstrate robust and accurate behavior across all benchmark systems.
AI.conclusion: The extended Vasudeva Murthy relaxation framework is verified as a reliable and accurate alternative for a wide range of hyperbolic relaxation systems, with integral invariants serving as conserved vector quantities that couple solution variables and are preserved numerically.

title: Failure of a BM-type inequality for the Gaussian torsional rigidity
summary: Let $u$ be the torsion function for the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator on a bounded domain $Ω\subset \R^n$, i.e., the solution of $Δu - x \cdot \nabla u=-1$ in $Ω$ with $u=0$ on $\partialΩ$. Let $\Tg(Ω)=\int_Ωu\,dγ$ be the Gaussian torsional rigidity. We prove that the Brunn--Minkowski-type inequality $\Tg((1-t)Ω_0+tΩ_1)^α\le (1-t)\Tg(Ω_0)^α+t\Tg(Ω_1)^α$ fails for every exponent $α>0$ and in every dimension $n\ge2$, for a pair of convex bodies centrally symmetric with respect to the origin, which may be taken smooth with positive curvature. This answers Conjecture~1.4 and Question~(Q) of Marín Sola and Salerno in the negative. The mechanism is a first-order lower bound for $\Tg$ at a ball $Ω_0$ under Minkowski perturbations. When the perturbing body $Ω_1$ has small torsion and large mean width, $\Tg((1-t) Ω_0 + t Ω_1)$ increases to first order. Since the Minkowski combination has larger torsion than both endpoints, no exponent can repair the inequality.

AI.tldr: The paper disproves a conjectured Brunn-Minkowski-type inequality for Gaussian torsional rigidity of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator, showing it fails for all exponents and in all dimensions n≥2, even for smooth centrally symmetric convex bodies.
AI.motivation: To settle a conjecture and open question by Marín Sola and Salerno regarding whether Gaussian torsional rigidity satisfies a Brunn-Minkowski-type inequality.
AI.method: The proof uses a first-order lower bound on Gaussian torsional rigidity at a ball under Minkowski perturbations. By choosing a perturbing body with small torsion but large mean width, the Minkowski combination increases to first order, exceeding both endpoint values, making the inequality irreparable by any exponent.
AI.result: The Brunn-Minkowski-type inequality fails for every exponent α>0 and in every dimension n≥2, even for smooth convex bodies with positive curvature that are centrally symmetric.
AI.conclusion: The conjecture of Marín Sola and Salerno is settled in the negative; no exponent can salvage the Brunn-Minkowski-type inequality for Gaussian torsional rigidity.

title: Model reduction of port-Hamiltonian systems via neural networks
summary: In this paper, we consider structure-preserving model reduction of port-Hamiltonian (pH) systems which extend classical Hamiltonian systems with dissipation and an input-output port. These pH systems are often used in multi-physics systems, as the interconnection of one or more \pH systems results again in a pH system. If particularly the system matrices associated with the interconnection and/or dissipation of a pH system are state-dependent, then the evaluation of standard reduced-order models (ROMs) may depend on the dimension of the original full-order model, resulting in high computational costs. To circumvent these high costs, we propose to use structure-preserving neural networks. In particular, we perform two steps: (1) we use the generalized manifold Galerkin projection to project the pH system onto the reduced space; then (2) we train a neural network to learn the map from the reduced-order state to the reduced-order interconnection and dissipation system matrices. To ensure that the resulting ROM is again a pH system, the architecture of the neural network is chosen such that the skew-symmetry and positive semi-definiteness of the reduced-order systems matrices are maintained. In a numerical example, we consider a nonlinear mass-spring-damper system with state-dependent system matrices. The numerical results show that the proposed method achieves a significant computational speed-up compared to the original \ROM with comparable accuracy.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a structure-preserving model reduction approach for port-Hamiltonian (pH) systems with state-dependent interconnection and dissipation matrices. The method combines generalized manifold Galerkin projection with a specially designed neural network that learns the mapping from reduced states to reduced system matrices while preserving the skew-symmetry and positive semi-definiteness properties required for pH structure.
AI.motivation: Standard reduced-order models (ROMs) of port-Hamiltonian systems with state-dependent matrices suffer from computational costs that scale with the dimension of the original full-order model. This defeats the purpose of model reduction, motivating the need for structure-preserving ROMs whose evaluation cost is independent of the full-order dimension.
AI.method: The method consists of two steps: (1) applying generalized manifold Galerkin projection to project the pH system onto a reduced space; (2) training a neural network to learn the mapping from reduced-order states to the reduced interconnection and dissipation matrices. The neural network architecture is designed to enforce skew-symmetry and positive semi-definiteness of the learned matrices, ensuring the reduced model remains a valid pH system.
AI.result: Numerical experiments on a nonlinear mass-spring-damper system with state-dependent matrices show that the proposed method achieves significant computational speed-up compared to the original ROM while maintaining comparable accuracy.
AI.conclusion: The proposed neural network-based structure-preserving model reduction approach effectively eliminates the dimension-dependence of computational costs in pH system ROMs while preserving the port-Hamiltonian structure, offering both speed and accuracy.

title: On Cauchy Problems for Parabolic Equations with Rough Coefficients
summary: The presented work investigates the Cauchy problems for parabolic equations in both non-divergence and divergence forms with rough diffusion coefficients, which commonly arise in composite media, financial pricing, and viscous fluids. Under critical regularity settings, we establish the unique solvability in optimal fractional Sobolev spaces. The first key technical step lies in constructing an effective approximation scheme with truncated and mollified diffusion coefficients $a^ε(t,x)$, for which we rigorously prove the uniform preservation of high-frequency smallness. By incorporating this approximation scheme with paraproduct decomposition, Fefferman-Stein maximal inequalities, Coifman-Meyer bilinear estimates, and refined Sobolev embeddings, we close the uniform a priori estimates and then pass to the limit. Furthermore, we prove that the threshold $s < \frac{1}{2}$ is sharp by constructing explicit counterexamples. These theoretical results provide a rigorous mathematical framework in the study of Cauchy problems for parabolic equations with rough coefficients.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes unique solvability of Cauchy problems for parabolic equations (both non-divergence and divergence forms) with rough diffusion coefficients in optimal fractional Sobolev spaces, under critical regularity settings. The threshold s < 1/2 is proven sharp via counterexamples.
AI.motivation: Parabolic equations with rough diffusion coefficients arise in composite media, financial pricing, and viscous fluids, yet their well-posedness in optimal function spaces remains challenging and largely open.
AI.method: The authors construct an effective approximation scheme using truncated and mollified diffusion coefficients a^ε(t,x), proving uniform preservation of high-frequency smallness. This is combined with paraproduct decomposition, Fefferman-Stein maximal inequalities, Coifman-Meyer bilinear estimates, and refined Sobolev embeddings to close uniform a priori estimates and pass to the limit.
AI.result: Unique solvability in optimal fractional Sobolev spaces is established for both non-divergence and divergence forms. The sharpness of the regularity threshold s < 1/2 is demonstrated through explicit counterexamples.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a rigorous mathematical framework for studying Cauchy problems of parabolic equations with rough coefficients, establishing optimal solvability theory.

title: Random attractors and almost-sure stability under discretization of a stochastic autoparametric system
summary: For a stochastic autoparametric block-and-pendulum system, the long-time dynamics exhibit two fundamental features: the almost-sure stability of the single mode solution, characterized by its Lyapunov exponent, and the global asymptotic dynamics when this single mode solution loses stability. This naturally raises the question of whether these dynamical features are preserved under discretization, since such preservation is essential for the resulting discrete system to faithfully capture the qualitative behavior of the continuous system. To address this question, we first establish the existence of a random attractor for the continuous system subject to multiplicative stochastic excitation, providing a rigorous characterization of the global asymptotic dynamics. We then propose a numerical discretization that induces a discrete random dynamical system and prove the convergence of its random attractor to the continuous one as the step size tends to zero. In addition, we show that the numerical Lyapunov exponent of the single mode solution has the same sign as its continuous counterpart for sufficiently small step sizes, thus preserving the corresponding almost-sure stability or instability classification. These results demonstrate that the proposed discretization captures both the global asymptotic dynamics and the stability characteristics of the underlying stochastic autoparametric system.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a stochastic autoparametric block-and-pendulum system, establishing the existence of a random attractor for the continuous system, proving convergence of discrete random attractors to the continuous one as step size goes to zero, and showing that the numerical Lyapunov exponent preserves the sign (and thus stability classification) of the continuous system for sufficiently small step sizes.
AI.motivation: The long-time dynamics of the stochastic autoparametric system have two key features: almost-sure stability of the single mode solution (via Lyapunov exponent) and global asymptotic dynamics when that solution loses stability. The central question is whether these features are preserved under numerical discretization, which is essential for the discrete system to faithfully represent the continuous system's qualitative behavior.
AI.method: The authors (1) establish existence of a random attractor for the continuous system under multiplicative stochastic excitation, (2) propose a numerical discretization inducing a discrete random dynamical system, (3) prove convergence of the discrete random attractor to the continuous one as step size tends to zero, and (4) show the numerical Lyapunov exponent has the same sign as the continuous counterpart for sufficiently small step sizes.
AI.result: The discretization is shown to preserve both the global asymptotic dynamics (via random attractor convergence) and the almost-sure stability/instability classification (via sign preservation of the Lyapunov exponent) of the underlying continuous stochastic autoparametric system.
AI.conclusion: The proposed discretization faithfully captures both the global asymptotic dynamics and stability characteristics of the underlying stochastic autoparametric system, confirming that the key dynamical features of the continuous system are preserved under numerical approximation.

title: High frequency wave propagation for the viscoelastic wave equation with singular memory
summary:
We study high-frequency propagation for a viscoelastic wave equation with spatially dependent hereditary memory in relative-history form. The kernel may have the integrable singularity $\mathfrak m(s,x)=s^{p-1}m(s,x)$, $0<p<1$; the regular case $p=1$ is included. Using the half-amplitude propagation distance and corresponding travel time as units, the wavelength $h\ll1$ yields the memory factor $\varepsilon=h^{1-p}$. We construct exact solutions with full two-scale geometric-optics expansions in powers $h^{k+(1-p)\ell}$. Memory modifies the propagation geometry through the instantaneous modulus $σ+\varepsilon\int_0^\infty\mathfrak m(s,\cdot)\,d s$, while the kernel singularity contributes $C_p=Γ(p)e^{iπp/2}$ to the leading transport equation. For $0<p<1$, this produces fractional scales, frequency-dependent attenuation, and a dispersive phase correction; for $p=1$, the fractional hierarchy disappears, attenuation is frequency independent, and the transport phase correction vanishes.
  We also derive a local damped wave equation whose incoming high-frequency solutions approximate the hereditary solutions with $O(h)$ error in semiclassical $C^k$ norms. Exterior observations for all incident directions and $0<h\ll1$ uniquely recover $σ_{\mathfrak m}$ and the full temporal jet of $m$ at $s=0$, which determine the expansion modulo $O(h^\infty)$.
  Finally, a contraction-semigroup argument gives well-posedness and arbitrary finite-order Sobolev regularity for spatially dependent weakly singular kernels and prescribed full prehistory, with explicit compatibility conditions and estimates uniform in $\varepsilon$. These estimates justify the geometric-optics construction.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes high-frequency wave propagation in viscoelastic media with spatially dependent memory kernels that may have integrable singularities. Using two-scale geometric-optics expansions, the authors show how memory modifies propagation geometry, introduces fractional scales and frequency-dependent attenuation for singular kernels (0<p<1), derive a local damped wave approximation, prove unique recovery of material properties from exterior observations, and establish well-posedness with regularity for weakly singular kernels.
AI.motivation: To understand how spatially dependent hereditary memory with integrable singularities affects high-frequency wave propagation, and to develop rigorous mathematical tools (geometric optics, well-posedness, inverse problems) for such viscoelastic media.
AI.method: The authors construct exact solutions using full two-scale geometric-optics expansions in powers of h^{k+(1-p)l}, where h is wavelength. They derive a local damped wave equation approximation, use a contraction-semigroup argument for well-posedness, and employ exterior observation data for the inverse problem.
AI.result: Memory alters propagation geometry via the instantaneous modulus modified by a memory integral. The kernel singularity contributes Γ(p)e^{iπp/2} to leading transport. For 0<p<1: fractional scales, frequency-dependent attenuation, dispersive phase correction. For p=1: fractional hierarchy disappears, attenuation is frequency-independent, phase correction vanishes. The damped wave approximation has O(h) error; exterior observations uniquely recover σ and the temporal jet of m at s=0; well-posedness with explicit estimates uniform in ε is established.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a complete high-frequency asymptotic framework for viscoelastic waves with weakly singular memory kernels, including rigorous well-posedness, geometric-optics construction justification, and unique recovery results for inverse problems.

title: Nechvile-Transformed Spacecraft Dynamics and Propellant Computation in the 3-Body Problem
summary: The uncontrolled equations of motion in the Nechvile frame for the restricted three-body problem have been well-known since at least the 1960s. It would seem that adding an external force to these equations is quite trivial: simply add an external force per mass term to the acceleration equations. Here we show that the last statement is not true. In fact, we show that the additive generic external force must be multiplied by the inverse of $(1 + e \cosθ)^3$ where $e$ is the relative eccentricity of the primaries and $θ$ is the true anomaly of the rotating frame located at the barycenter. Furthermore, when this result is combined with the mass flow rate equation, it generates several surprising results due to the mismatch between the resulting quadratic term and the cubic term in the equations of motion. This leads to a corresponding modification of the rocket equation itself. A Birkhoff-theoretic solution to an illustrative cislunar space mission problem shows propellent savings of 80% with the use of the correct cost functional. The popular quadratic cost utilizes more than $2X$ the minimum propellant consumption.

AI.tldr: This paper reveals that adding an external force to the Nechvile frame equations for the restricted three-body problem is not as trivial as previously thought. The external force must be scaled by the inverse of (1 + e cos θ)³, which when combined with the mass flow rate equation, leads to a modified rocket equation and significantly different propellant consumption predictions.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to correct a widely held assumption that adding an external force to the well-known Nechvile frame equations is straightforward. They demonstrate that the naive approach is incorrect and has significant implications for spacecraft trajectory design and propellant consumption.
AI.method: The authors derive the correct scaling factor for the external force in the Nechvile frame, show how this interacts with the mass flow rate equation, and reformulate the rocket equation accordingly. They then apply a Birkhoff-theoretic solution to an illustrative cislunar space mission to compare the correct cost functional against the popular quadratic cost.
AI.result: The correct scaling factor for the external force is the inverse of (1 + e cos θ)³. The Birkhoff-theoretic solution to a cislunar mission shows 80% propellant savings with the correct cost functional, while the popular quadratic cost uses more than 2X the minimum propellant consumption.
AI.conclusion: The coupling between the external force and the geometric scaling factor in the Nechvile frame fundamentally changes the rocket equation and optimal propellant consumption predictions, with major practical implications for mission design.

title: Gradient Estimates Near the Natural Exponent for Very Weak Solutions to $A_p$-Weighted Quasilinear Elliptic Equations
summary:
We establish local Calderón--Zygmund estimates near the natural exponent for very weak solutions to matrix-weighted quasilinear equations\[ - \mathrm{div\,} A_{\mathbb{M}}(x,Du) =
- \mathrm{div\,} A_{\mathbb{M}}(x,\mathbf{f}), \qquad A_{\mathbb{M}}(x,ξ)=\mathbb{M}(x)A(x,\mathbb{M}(x)ξ), \] where $A$ has $p$-growth and strong monotonicity, and $\mathbb{M}$ is a measurable positive-definite matrix field. We assume that $\mathbb{M}$ has bounded condition number and that \(ω:=|\mathbb{M}|^p\in A_p\), without imposing uniform upper or lower bounds on $\mathbb{M}$.
  This extends the near-natural Calderón--Zygmund theory developed by Adimurthi--Phuc \cite{AP15} to the matrix-degenerate setting: There exists $δ_0>0$ such that every very weak solution $u \in W^{p-δ_{0}}_{ω, \mathrm{loc}}$ satisfies \[ \mathbf{f}\in L^γ_{ω,\mathrm{loc}} \Longrightarrow Du\in L^γ_{ω,\mathrm{loc}} \] for $p-δ_0\leγ\le p+δ_0$. The proof requires handling the lack of energy estimates below the natural exponent and the use of Lipschitz truncation in the weighted setting. We achieve this through comparison estimates, higher integrability, and weighted analysis techniques.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes local Calderón–Zygmund estimates near the natural exponent for very weak solutions of matrix-weighted quasilinear elliptic equations, extending prior work by Adimurthi–Phuc to matrix-degenerate settings where the matrix field M has bounded condition number with |M|^p in the Muckenhoupt class A_p.
AI.motivation: To extend the near-natural Calderón–Zygmund theory for quasilinear equations to matrix-weighted (degenerate) settings, where the weight is a matrix field rather than a scalar weight, and to handle very weak solutions below the natural exponent where standard energy estimates fail.
AI.method: The proof employs comparison estimates, higher integrability results, and weighted analysis techniques. To handle the lack of energy estimates below the natural exponent, Lipschitz truncation in the weighted setting is utilized, combined with the A_p condition on |M|^p and bounded condition number assumptions on M.
AI.result: There exists δ_0 > 0 such that for any very weak solution u ∈ W^{p-δ_0}_{ω,loc}, the implication f ∈ L^γ_{ω,loc} ⇒ Du ∈ L^γ_{ω,loc} holds for all p - δ_0 ≤ γ ≤ p + δ_0.
AI.conclusion: The near-natural Calderón–Zygmund theory is successfully generalized to the matrix-weighted degenerate setting without imposing uniform upper or lower bounds on the matrix field M, relying only on bounded condition number and the weighted A_p condition.

title: Selection, Representation, and Execution in Sparse Fourier Neural Operators
summary: Sparse representations are often expected to make models smaller and also reduce inference cost. For Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs), these objectives are not equivalent or do not always align: removing parts of the learned operator can leave the underlying transforms and dense computations unchanged, while changing the grid on which the model is evaluated can introduce overhead of its own. We therefore distinguish sparsity in the representation, in the stored parameters, in the theoretical operation count, and in measured runtime, and present an empirical study of several routes toward sparse FNOs that tests each transition between them separately. Coarsening the execution grid reduces the theoretical cost without reducing measured latency, and adding a correction term recovers accuracy at the cost of making the model slower. Even an 83\% parameter reduction remains slower than the dense baseline under ordinary execution. These results motivate a stricter definition of useful sparsity: the deployed operator must preserve solution accuracy and map its reduced support to a genuinely cheaper execution path.

AI.tldr: This paper examines sparse Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) and finds that different notions of sparsity—representation, parameters, theoretical operations, and measured runtime—do not align. Sparsifying parameters or coarsening execution grids often fails to reduce actual latency, motivating a stricter definition of "useful sparsity" that requires both accuracy preservation and genuinely cheaper execution.
AI.motivation: Sparse representations are commonly assumed to yield smaller and faster models, but for FNOs this assumption may not hold. Removing parts of the learned operator may leave underlying transforms and dense computations unchanged, so the goals of model compression and inference speedup are not equivalent and need empirical disentanglement.
AI.method: The authors distinguish four types of sparsity: sparsity in representation, stored parameters, theoretical operation count, and measured runtime. They empirically study multiple routes toward sparse FNOs, testing each transition between these sparsity types separately—including grid coarsening, parameter reduction, and adding correction terms to recover accuracy.
AI.result: Coarsening the execution grid reduces theoretical cost but not measured latency. Adding a correction term restores accuracy at the cost of slower runtime. Even an 83% parameter reduction remains slower than the dense baseline under ordinary execution.
AI.conclusion: The paper motivates a stricter definition of useful sparsity: a deployed sparse operator must preserve solution accuracy and map its reduced support to a genuinely cheaper execution path, not merely to fewer parameters or lower theoretical operation counts.

title: Łojasiewicz--Simon inequalities near bubbling configurations for the Yamabe functional on bounded domains
summary: We establish Łojasiewicz--Simon type gradient inequalities for the Yamabe functional on bounded smooth domains near configurations consisting of finitely many concentrating bubbles, with or without a regular component. A weighted decomposition separates the finite-dimensional spectral and bubble parameters from an infinite-dimensional coercive remainder. We obtain quantitative estimates for the parameters, the remainder, and the corresponding energy gaps, in both the regular-plus-bubbling and the pure-bubbling regimes. These inequalities quantify the deviation from such surfaces and are essential for studying the dynamics of related parabolic flows.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes Łojasiewicz-Simon type gradient inequalities for the Yamabe functional on bounded smooth domains near configurations of concentrating bubbles, with or without a regular component. Using a weighted decomposition separating finite-dimensional spectral/bubble parameters from an infinite-dimensional coercive remainder, the authors derive quantitative estimates for parameters, remainder, and energy gaps in both regular-plus-bubbling and pure-bubbling regimes.
AI.motivation: The Yamabe functional plays a central role in geometric analysis, and understanding its behavior near critical configurations (concentrating bubbles) is essential. Łojasiewicz-Simon inequalities are key tools for analyzing the dynamics of parabolic flows, yet such inequalities have not been established for the Yamabe functional in these multi-bubble regimes.
AI.method: The approach uses a weighted decomposition that separates the finite-dimensional spectral parameters and bubble parameters from an infinite-dimensional coercive remainder. This decomposition enables quantitative estimates for the parameters, the remainder, and the corresponding energy gaps, covering both configurations with a regular component and pure-bubbling configurations.
AI.result: The paper establishes Łojasiewicz-Simon type gradient inequalities for the Yamabe functional near multi-bubble configurations on bounded smooth domains, with quantitative estimates in both regular-plus-bubbling and pure-bubbling regimes.
AI.conclusion: These gradient inequalities quantify the deviation from concentrating bubble surfaces and are essential tools for studying the dynamics of related parabolic flows.

title: Spectra of Non-Self-Adjoint Almost Mathieu Matrices and the Scottish Flag Operator
summary: For $N\geq 3$ and a potential phase $\vartheta\in\mathbb{R}$, we study the non-self-adjoint almost Mathieu matrix obtained by multiplying the discrete Laplacian by a complex phase with angle $\varphi\in\mathbb{R}$, $A_N(\varphi,\vartheta)=e^{i\varphi}(S+S^{-1})/2+\operatorname{diag}(\cos(2πj/N+\vartheta))_{j\in\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}}$, where $S e_j=e_{j+1}$ is the periodic shift on $\mathbb{C}^N$. We derive a Chambers formula and isolate the part $Q_{N,\varphi}$ of the characteristic polynomial that depends only on $N$ and $\varphi$, but not on $\vartheta$ or on a change of boundary conditions for the shift operator. We then show, for every $N$, that the zeros of $Q_{N,\varphi}$ lie on the two perpendicular lines $e^{i\varphi/2}\mathbb{R}\cup e^{i(\varphi/2+π/2)}\mathbb{R}$. For even $N$, the same property holds for the matrices $A_N(\varphi,\vartheta)$ with $\vartheta\in 2π\mathbb{Z}/N$, and we compute their limiting eigenvalue measure explicitly. For $\varphi\in[-π,π]$, the eigenvalue distribution approximates elliptic-integral densities with masses $1-|\varphi|/π$ and $|\varphi|/π$, and maximal radii $2|\cos(\varphi/2)|$ and $2|\sin(\varphi/2)|$, respectively. At $\varphi=π/2$, the central polynomial $Q_{N,\varphi}$ factors into positive quartic factors. This proves that the Scottish flag matrix, after Trefethen and Chapman, has its spectrum on the two diagonal lines of the saltire.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the non-self-adjoint almost Mathieu matrix with a complex phase, derives a Chambers formula, and proves that the zeros of the phase-independent polynomial Q lie on two perpendicular lines. For even N, the full spectrum lies on these lines, with explicit limiting eigenvalue measures given by elliptic-integral densities. The Scottish flag matrix spectrum is confirmed to lie on the two diagonal lines of the saltire.
AI.motivation: To understand the spectral properties of non-self-adjoint almost Mathieu matrices with complex phase, which generalize classical almost Mathieu operators and have connections to the Scottish flag matrix problem posed by Trefethen and Chapman.
AI.method: The authors derive a Chambers formula for the characteristic polynomial, isolating a phase-independent part Q_{N,φ}. Through algebraic analysis of this polynomial, they prove its zeros lie on two perpendicular lines, and for even N, extend this to the full matrix spectrum. They compute the limiting eigenvalue distribution using elliptic integrals.
AI.result: For every N, zeros of Q lie on e^{iφ/2}R ∪ e^{i(φ/2+π/2)}R. For even N, the matrices A_N(φ,θ) with θ ∈ 2πZ/N have spectra on these lines. The limiting eigenvalue measure has masses 1-|φ|/π and |φ|/π with maximal radii 2|cos(φ/2)| and 2|sin(φ/2)|. At φ=π/2, Q factors into positive quartic factors, proving the Scottish flag matrix spectrum lies on the saltire's diagonal lines.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a complete characterization of the spectral location for non-self-adjoint almost Mathieu matrices with complex phase, explicitly computing limiting eigenvalue distributions and confirming the Scottish flag conjecture through rigorous factorization arguments.

title: Exact counting of spherical metrics with one conical singularity on rectangular tori
summary: We prove that for every integer $n\geq 2$ and $8π(n-1)<ρ<8πn$, the singular Liouville equation $Δu+\e^u=ρδ_0$ on a rectangular torus $E_{\mathrm{i}b}=\mathbb{C}/(\mathbb Z+\mathrm{i} b\mathbb Z)$ has exactly $n$ solutions, which are all axisymmetric. Together with previous results by Chen-Lin and Lin-Wang, this yields that \begin{itemize} \item $E_{\mathrm{i} b}$ admits no spherical metrics with a conical singularity of angle $2π\vartheta$ as long as $\vartheta$ is a positive odd integer. \item For every integer $n\geq 1$, $E_{\mathrm{i} b}$ admits exactly $n$ spherical metrics with a conical singularity of angle $2π\vartheta$ for each $\vartheta\in (2n-1, 2n+1)$. \end{itemize} The basic idea is to prove that the linearized equation has only trivial solutions in the space of axisymmetric functions. The previous method of analysing nodal domains via Bol's isoperimetric inequality only works for $ρ\leq 8π$. We develop a unified approach for all $ρ\in (0,+\infty)\setminus 8π\mathbb{N}_{\geq 1}$ by exploring the deep connection with the monodromy of the classical Lamé equation.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that the singular Liouville equation on a rectangular torus has exactly n solutions for 8π(n-1)<ρ<8πn, all axisymmetric, which yields precise counts of spherical metrics with conical singularities on rectangular tori.
AI.motivation: To determine the exact number of solutions to the singular Liouville equation on rectangular tori across all energy ranges, extending previous results that only worked for ρ≤8π via nodal domain analysis.
AI.method: Proves that the linearized equation has only trivial solutions in the space of axisymmetric functions, developing a unified approach for all ρ by connecting the problem to the monodromy of the classical Lamé equation.
AI.result: For every integer n≥2 and 8π(n-1)<ρ<8πn, the equation has exactly n solutions (all axisymmetric). This implies rectangular tori admit no spherical metrics with conical singularity angle 2πϑ for odd integer ϑ, and exactly n such metrics for ϑ∈(2n-1,2n+1).
AI.conclusion: The paper completes the classification of solutions to the singular Liouville equation on rectangular tori for all energy levels, using a new approach via Lamé equation monodromy that overcomes limitations of previous isoperimetric inequality methods.

title: Derivation of a linearly elastic elliptic membrane shell theory in the framework of magnetoelasticity
summary: Starting from a three-dimensional model of linearized magnetoelasticity, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of a thin shell as its thickness approaches zero. Our analysis focuses on a family of linearly elastic elliptic membrane shells. Using $Γ$-convergence, we rigorously derive a two-dimensional linear magnetoelastic shell model and establish its relationship to the original three-dimensional model in terms of the convergence of minimizers.

AI.tldr: The paper derives a two-dimensional linear magnetoelastic shell model from a three-dimensional model via Γ-convergence as the shell thickness approaches zero, and establishes convergence of minimizers between the models.
AI.motivation: To understand how thin magnetoelastic shells behave asymptotically as their thickness goes to zero, and to rigorously derive a lower-dimensional effective model from the full 3D formulation.
AI.method: The authors use Γ-convergence techniques to pass from a 3D linearized magnetoelasticity model to a 2D model for linearly elastic elliptic membrane shells as the thickness parameter tends to zero.
AI.result: A two-dimensional linear magnetoelastic shell model is rigorously derived, with a proven relationship to the original 3D model through the convergence of minimizers.
AI.conclusion: The asymptotic dimension reduction of thin magnetoelastic shells is rigorously justified, yielding a well-defined 2D effective model that faithfully captures the limiting behavior of the 3D system.

title: Grow-up rates of inhomogeneous semilinear heat equations in the critical dimension
summary:
This paper concerns the grow-up rate of solutions to a semilinear heat equation in the unit ball with the exponential nonlinearity and an inhomogeneous term $f$. When $f=0$, it is known that the large-time behavior of a solution changes at the critical dimension $N=10$, and the grow-up phenomenon occurs for the case $N\ge 10$. For the inhomogeneous case with $N\ge 10$, the present author and a coauthor showed in [12] that the grow-up phenomenon disappears once $f$ exceeds a threshold.
  In this paper, we provide a quantitative characterization of the disappearance of the grow-up phenomenon by obtaining the grow-up rate in the critical dimension. Our result shows that a qualitatively different type of grow-up behavior occurs in the critical dimension compared with the case $N\ge 11$ studied in [12]. The difference is caused by a change in the outer behavior of the solution. Even in the case $f=0$, our result is new in that it provides a rigorous justification of the formal computation by Galaktionov and King [10].

AI.tldr: This paper provides a quantitative characterization of the disappearance of grow-up phenomena in a semilinear heat equation with exponential nonlinearity and inhomogeneous term in the critical dimension N=10, showing qualitatively different grow-up behavior compared to N≥11 cases.
AI.motivation: To quantitatively characterize the disappearance of the grow-up phenomenon in the critical dimension N=10 for a semilinear heat equation with exponential nonlinearity and inhomogeneous term, building on prior work showing grow-up disappears when f exceeds a threshold.
AI.method: Analysis of the grow-up rate in the critical dimension, examining the outer behavior of the solution to distinguish qualitatively different grow-up behavior compared to the N≥11 case previously studied.
AI.result: The study reveals that qualitatively different types of grow-up behavior occur in the critical dimension compared with N≥11, caused by a change in the outer behavior of the solution. The result also rigorously justifies a formal computation by Galaktionov and King even in the f=0 case.
AI.conclusion: The critical dimension N=10 exhibits unique grow-up behavior distinct from higher dimensions, and the quantitative characterization proves the disappearance of grow-up phenomena when f exceeds a threshold, with new results even for the homogeneous case.

title: Finite speed of propagation and waiting time phenomena for stochastic porous media equations with nonlinear conservative noise
summary: Starting from localized energy estimates, we prove finite speed of propagation for kinetic solutions to stochastic porous media equations with nonlinear conservative noise, the existence and uniqueness of which has recently been established. In particular, we propose a novel iteration technique which allows us to obtain a Stampacchia-type inequality involving one single integral quantity, despite the possibly different scaling behaviors of the porous media and the noise term. This allows us to apply stochastic filtering arguments developed for the case of linear source-type noise. Using related ideas, we identify flatness conditions on initial data which guarantee locally the occurrence of a waiting time phenomenon, i.e., the onset of forward propagation of the solution's support is locally delayed. The condition for the latter matches the one for the deterministic porous media equation up to a logarithmic correction in the case of critical nonlinearity in the noise, but it requires more and more flatness of the initial data as the nonlinearity tends towards linear conservative noise. This is in line with the expected behavior: In the case of linear conservative noise, instantaneous forward motion is possible due to the effects of stochastic transport, no matter how flat the initial profile is.

AI.tldr: This paper proves finite speed of propagation for kinetic solutions to stochastic porous media equations with nonlinear conservative noise, using a novel iteration technique to obtain a Stampacchia-type inequality. It also identifies flatness conditions on initial data that guarantee a waiting time phenomenon locally, matching the deterministic case up to a logarithmic correction for critical noise nonlinearity.
AI.motivation: To establish finite speed of propagation for stochastic porous media equations with nonlinear conservative noise, generalizing prior results that only handled linear source-type noise. This requires overcoming the challenge of different scaling behaviors between the porous media term and the noise term.
AI.method: The authors develop a novel iteration technique to derive a Stampacchia-type inequality involving a single integral quantity, despite differing scaling behaviors of the porous media and noise terms. This enables the application of stochastic filtering arguments previously developed for linear source-type noise. They also use related ideas to identify flatness conditions on initial data for waiting time phenomena.
AI.result: Finite speed of propagation is established for kinetic solutions of stochastic porous media equations with nonlinear conservative noise. Flatness conditions on initial data are identified that guarantee local waiting time phenomena. The condition matches the deterministic case up to a logarithmic correction for critical noise nonlinearity, but requires increasingly flat initial data as noise approaches linearity—consistent with the expectation that linear conservative noise causes instantaneous forward motion regardless of initial flatness.
AI.conclusion: The finite speed of propagation holds for the stochastic porous media equation with nonlinear conservative noise, and the waiting time phenomenon persists under appropriate flatness conditions on the initial data, with the required flatness growing as the noise tends toward linear conservative noise.

title: Compactly Supported Solutions near a Nehari Critical Value
summary: We study non-negative solutions of the indefinite sublinear Dirichlet problem $$ \left \{\ \begin{array}{ll} -Δu=λu+m(x)|u|^{α-1}u&\quad\hbox{ in $Ω$},\\ u=0&\quad \hbox{ on $\partial Ω$}, \end{array} \right . $$ where $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$ is a smooth bounded domain, $0<α<1$, $m\in L^{\infty }(Ω)$ is a sign-changing or non-positive weight, and $λ\in \mathbb{R}$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies non-negative solutions of an indefinite sublinear Dirichlet problem with a sign-changing or non-positive weight function, examining how the parameter λ affects the existence and structure of solutions.
AI.motivation: To understand the existence and properties of non-negative solutions for a sublinear elliptic problem where the weight m(x) can change sign or be non-positive, extending results beyond the classical positive weight case.
AI.method: The paper analyzes the indefinite sublinear Dirichlet problem -Δu = λu + m(x)|u|^(α-1)u with 0<α<1, sign-changing or non-positive weight m, and parameter λ ∈ ℝ, on a smooth bounded domain.
AI.result: The abstract does not specify the exact results, but the study characterizes the existence and structure of non-negative solutions depending on the parameter λ and the sign properties of the weight m.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a complete or partial characterization of non-negative solutions for this indefinite sublinear problem, particularly addressing cases where the weight is sign-changing or non-positive which are more delicate than the standard positive weight setting.

title: The flexible part of intermittent Onsager theorem for the two-dimensional stochastic incompressible Euler equations
summary: This work is concerned with the flexible part of Onsager theorem for the two-dimensional stochastic incompressible Euler equations. We develop a stochastic and intermittent variant of the Newton--Nash iteration scheme, which incorporates new stochastic pressure, Reynolds stress and intermittency perturbations to formalize the stochastic and intermittent fluctuations. For any $γ\in \left[ {0,\frac{1}{3}} \right)$, we employ this iteration scheme to construct $γ$-Hölder-continuous martingale solutions for the two-dimensional stochastic incompressible Euler equations. These martingale solutions exhibit dissipative behavior and intermittency, thereby settling the flexible part of intermittent Onsager theorem for the two-dimensional stochastic incompressible Euler equations.
