AI.tldr: This paper proves the flexible part of the Onsager theorem for 2D stochastic incompressible Euler equations by constructing γ-Hölder-continuous martingale solutions for any γ ∈ [0, 1/3) using a stochastic and intermittent Newton-Nash iteration scheme that incorporates stochastic pressure, Reynolds stress, and intermittency perturbations.
AI.motivation: To settle the flexible (or "wild") part of the intermittent Onsager theorem for 2D stochastic incompressible Euler equations, i.e., to construct non-smooth dissipative solutions at Hölder regularity below the critical threshold of 1/3, accounting for stochastic and intermittent fluctuations.
AI.method: A stochastic and intermittent variant of the Newton-Nash iteration scheme is developed, which introduces new stochastic pressure, Reynolds stress, and intermittency perturbations to formalize stochastic and intermittent fluctuations. The scheme is used to construct γ-Hölder-continuous martingale solutions.
AI.result: For any γ ∈ [0, 1/3), γ-Hölder-continuous martingale solutions to the 2D stochastic incompressible Euler equations are constructed. These solutions exhibit dissipative behavior and intermittency, thereby settling the flexible part of the intermittent Onsager theorem for the 2D stochastic Euler equations.
AI.conclusion: The flexible part of the intermittent Onsager theorem for 2D stochastic incompressible Euler equations is resolved by constructing dissipative, intermittent martingale solutions at all Hölder exponents below the critical 1/3 threshold.

title: Endpoint Mapping Properties of Wave Operators for Two-Dimensional Schrödinger Operators
summary:
We establish sharp endpoint mapping properties for the wave operators $W_\pm(H,-Δ)$ of two-dimensional Schrödinger operators $H=-Δ+V$ with real-valued decaying potentials $V$. Together with the known non-endpoint $L^p$ theory, our results give a complete classification of the $L^p$ mapping properties of the two-dimensional wave operators, and reveal an unexpected reversal of the usual threshold paradigm at the endpoints $p=1$ and $p=\infty$.
  When zero is a regular point of $H$, the wave operators fail to be bounded on $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and on $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^2)$, but they satisfy the atural substitute estimates of Calderón--Zygmund type: $$ L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\longrightarrow L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^2),\ \ \ \mathcal{H}^1(\mathbb{R}^2)\longrightarrow L^1(\mathbb{R}^2),\ \ \ L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^2)\longrightarrow \mathrm{BMO}(\mathbb{R}^2). $$ When zero is instead a threshold singularity of the first kind---an s-wave resonance with no other threshold obstruction, the wave operators are bounded on both endpoint spaces $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ and $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^2)$. Thus, in dimension two, an s-wave resonance improves the endpoint behavior of the wave operators, in sharp contrast with dimensions $n\ge3$, where the only regular case is the favorable one.
  We also determine the endpoint behavior in the remaining zero-energy spectral configurations of $H$. A p-wave resonance obstructs both the $L^1$- and the $L^\infty$-boundedness of the wave operators, while in the zero-eigenvalue case we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for endpoint boundedness, expressed in terms of the presence of s- and p-wave resonances and of explicit second-order harmonic moment cancellations satisfied by the zero-energy eigenfunctions.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes sharp endpoint (L¹ and L∞) mapping properties for wave operators of two-dimensional Schrödinger operators with decaying potentials, completing the L^p classification. The authors show that at zero energy, an s-wave resonance actually improves endpoint behavior (bounded on L¹ and L∞), opposite to dimensions n≥3, while p-wave resonances obstruct both endpoints. For zero-eigenvalue cases, they give necessary and sufficient conditions involving s-/p-wave resonances and harmonic moment cancellations.
AI.motivation: To complete the classification of L^p mapping properties of two-dimensional wave operators by resolving the previously unknown endpoint behavior at p=1 and p=∞, and to understand how zero-energy spectral configurations affect these endpoint properties—particularly revealing a surprising contrast with higher dimensions.
AI.method: The authors analyze wave operators W±(H,−Δ) for 2D Schrödinger operators with real-valued decaying potentials, classifying results by the zero-energy spectral configuration: regular point, s-wave resonance, p-wave resonance, and zero eigenvalue. They prove sharp endpoint estimates using Calderón–Zygmund-type techniques and derive necessary and sufficient conditions via harmonic moment cancellations of zero-energy eigenfunctions.
AI.result: (1) Regular zero point: wave operators fail L¹ and L∞ boundedness but satisfy sharp substitute estimates (L¹→L^{1,∞}, H¹→L¹, L∞→BMO). (2) s-wave resonance (only obstruction): wave operators are bounded on both L¹ and L∞—an improvement over the regular case, reversing the threshold paradigm from dimensions n≥3. (3) p-wave resonance: obstructs both L¹ and L∞ boundedness. (4) Zero-eigenvalue case: necessary and sufficient conditions for endpoint boundedness are given, expressed via s-/p-wave resonances and explicit second-order harmonic moment cancellations.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a complete classification of L^p mapping properties of two-dimensional wave operators, demonstrating that in dimension two, an s-wave resonance at zero energy improves endpoint behavior—a sharp reversal of the situation in higher dimensions where only the regular case is favorable. This completes the endpoint theory and reveals the dimension-dependent role of threshold resonances.

title: Revisiting Fazly-Wei-Xu pointwise estimates for the fourth-order Hénon equation via Bernstein's technique
summary: In a remarkable work published in Analysis and PDE 8 (2015) 1541-1563, M. Fazly, J. Wei, and X. Xu establish the following pointwise estimate \[-Δu \geq \frac 2{n-4} \frac{|\nabla u|^2}u + \sqrt{\frac 2{p+1- \frac 8{n(n-4)}}} |x|^{\frac σ2} u^\frac{p+1}2 \quad \text{in } \mathbf R^n\] for any bounded, positive, $C^4$-solution $u$ to the the fourth-order Hénon equation \[Δ^2 u = |x|^σu^p \quad \text{in } \mathbf R^n\] with $n \geq 5$, $σ\geq 0 $ but implicitly near $0$, and $p>(n+4+2σ)/(n-4)$. Their argument relies on a sophisticated iteration argument in the fashion of the standard Moser proof. In this paper, we provide an alternative approach which relies on the Bernstein technique via the maximum principle. The heart of our argument is a suitable choice of an auxiliary function allowing us not only achieving the same pointwise estimate, which still holds even for $p = (n+4+2σ)/(n-4)$, but also relaxing the boundedness of solutions. In addition, the pointwise inequality actually holds for any $σ\geq 0$. This estimate leads to an interesting consequence of the existence of conformal metric of $\mathbf R^n$ having positive scalar and $Q$ curvatures. We also show that the coefficient $2/(n-4)$ is sharp, hence providing the first answer to the question in the op. cit. paper. Our proof appears to be simpler and constructive.

AI.tldr: This paper provides an alternative proof of a pointwise estimate for the fourth-order Hénon equation, using the Bernstein technique and maximum principle instead of the Moser iteration argument used by Fazly, Wei, and Xu. The new approach extends the result to σ ≥ 0 (not just near 0), includes the critical case p = (n+4+2σ)/(n-4), relaxes the boundedness assumption on solutions, and proves the sharpness of the coefficient 2/(n-4).
AI.motivation: The previous result by Fazly, Wei, and Xu established a pointwise estimate for solutions of the fourth-order Hénon equation in R^n, but their proof relied on a sophisticated iteration argument (Moser-type) with limitations: it only worked for σ implicitly near 0, required bounded solutions, and did not cover the critical exponent case. This paper aims to overcome these limitations with a simpler and more general approach.
AI.method: The authors employ the Bernstein technique combined with the maximum principle. The core innovation is a carefully chosen auxiliary function that enables them to derive the pointwise estimate without the need for iteration arguments. This auxiliary function allows them to handle all σ ≥ 0, include the critical exponent p = (n+4+2σ)/(n-4), and relax the boundedness assumption on solutions.
AI.result: The pointwise estimate is established for all σ ≥ 0 and for the critical case p = (n+4+2σ)/(n-4), with relaxed boundedness conditions. The coefficient 2/(n-4) is proven to be sharp, providing the first answer to the question posed in the original paper. The estimate also leads to the existence of conformal metrics on R^n with positive scalar and Q curvatures.
AI.conclusion: The authors provide a simpler and more constructive proof of a sharp pointwise estimate for the fourth-order Hénon equation, generalizing and strengthening the prior result while establishing optimality of the constant. This also yields applications to conformal geometry regarding scalar and Q curvatures.

title: Higher Regularity of Time-Periodic Solutions to Nonautonomous Hyperbolic Problems: Away from Resonances
summary: We study higher regularity and its relation to nonresonant behavior for time-periodic solutions of boundary value problems for one-dimensional linear and nonlinear nonautonomous first-order integro-differential strictly hyperbolic systems. The boundary conditions include integral operators and various types of boundary reflections. We prove that continuous and classical solutions have $C^k$-regularity, provided the coefficients are sufficiently smooth and a suitable number of nonresonance conditions is satisfied. In the linear case, these conditions involve the principal coefficients, the diagonal lower-order coefficients, and the boundary reflection coefficients. In the nonlinear case, they also depend on the nonlinearities and on the solution itself. For nonautonomous hyperbolic systems, higher regularity generally requires additional nonresonance conditions, whose number depends on the desired order of differentiability. These conditions are not only sufficient but, in general, also necessary, revealing a distinctive feature of nonautonomous hyperbolic PDEs. By contrast, in the autonomous case, a single nonresonance condition (if one is needed at all) suffices to obtain arbitrarily high regularity. We also identify a class of nonautonomous hyperbolic problems for which no nonresonance conditions are required. In this case, the higher regularity of solutions is determined solely by the regularity of the data. The main technical tool underlying the proofs is an abstract regularity principle formulated in the setting of vector spaces.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates higher regularity (C^k) of time-periodic solutions to one-dimensional nonautonomous first-order integro-differential strictly hyperbolic systems with boundary conditions involving integral operators and reflections. Higher regularity requires additional nonresonance conditions whose number grows with the desired differentiability order—these are generally necessary and sufficient. In contrast, autonomous systems need only one (or zero) nonresonance condition for arbitrarily high regularity. A class of nonautonomous problems requiring no nonresonance conditions is also identified.
AI.motivation: To understand how higher regularity of time-periodic solutions to nonautonomous hyperbolic integro-differential systems is tied to nonresonance conditions, and to characterize when such conditions are needed versus when regularity is solely determined by data smoothness.
AI.method: The proofs rely on an abstract regularity principle formulated in the setting of vector spaces, applied to both linear and nonlinear first-order integro-differential hyperbolic systems with general boundary conditions (integral operators and reflections).
AI.result: Continuous and classical solutions attain C^k-regularity given sufficiently smooth coefficients and suitable nonresonance conditions. In the linear case these involve principal coefficients, diagonal lower-order terms, and boundary reflection coefficients; in the nonlinear case they additionally depend on nonlinearities and the solution itself. Nonautonomous systems generally require multiple nonresonance conditions (increasing in number with desired regularity), which are also necessary in general. Autonomous systems require at most one such condition for arbitrary regularity. A class of nonautonomous problems needs no nonresonance conditions at all.
AI.conclusion: Higher regularity for nonautonomous hyperbolic systems is fundamentally tied to a hierarchy of nonresonance conditions (generally both sufficient and necessary), a distinctive feature compared to the autonomous case where a single condition suffices for arbitrary regularity. Some nonautonomous problems are regular regardless of resonance.

title: Endpoint Energy Atoms Force Local Pressure Concentration in Three-Dimensional Navier-Stokes Flow
summary: We prove that a point atom in an endpoint kinetic-energy measure of a three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes flow on the flat torus forces quantitative concentration of the actual pressure. At each restart time tau, a same-state constraint-response comparison evolves u(tau) by the pressure-free componentwise advection-diffusion equation driven by u, and subtracts the resulting passive field z_tau. Writing r_tau = u - z_tau and g_tau = Q z_tau, we obtain an exact relative pressure-work identity. If the atom has mass m, Nash smoothing makes z_tau terminally non-atomic while r_tau retains terminal atomic mass at least m; hence, after every fixed restart, the terminal limsup of the accumulated pressure work is at least m/2. Mesoscopic localization yields scale-explicit lower bounds for gauge-invariant L2 pressure oscillation and for the local L2 mass of the pressure gradient in shrinking terminal cylinders. Consequently, on every terminal neighborhood of the atomic point, the pressure modulo functions of time and its gradient fail to be square integrable. The relative pressure-work principle extends to constrained solenoidal Oseen evolutions: as tau approaches T*, the zero-initial responses vanish in weak-tail topologies, although every fixed restart retains the same lower bound. This identifies a necessary pressure-work mechanism, generated by the incompressibility constraint, that links endpoint atoms to local pressure concentration, without requiring a full regularity hypothesis.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that if a point atom exists in the endpoint kinetic-energy measure of a 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes flow on the flat torus, then the pressure must exhibit quantitative concentration near that point. The authors establish an exact relative pressure-work identity and derive scale-explicit lower bounds on pressure oscillations and gradient mass in shrinking terminal cylinders, showing pressure and its gradient fail to be square integrable near the atomic point.
AI.motivation: Understanding the role of pressure in the regularity theory of 3D Navier-Stokes equations is a central open problem. The authors aim to connect endpoint singularities (atoms in kinetic-energy measures) to concrete, quantitative pressure concentration, revealing a necessary mechanism generated by the incompressibility constraint that operates independently of full regularity assumptions.
AI.method: The method introduces a same-state constraint-response comparison: at each restart time tau, u(tau) is evolved by the pressure-free componentwise advection-diffusion equation, producing a passive field z_tau. The differences r_tau = u - z_tau and g_tau = Q z_tau allow an exact relative pressure-work identity. Nash smoothing shows z_tau becomes terminally non-atomic while r_tau retains terminal atomic mass at least m, leading to a limsup lower bound of m/2 on accumulated pressure work. Mesoscopic localization then yields scale-explicit bounds on pressure oscillations and gradient mass in shrinking cylinders. The principle is extended to constrained solenoidal Oseen evolutions.
AI.result: The paper proves quantitative pressure concentration forced by endpoint atoms: on every terminal neighborhood of the atomic point, the pressure modulo functions of time and its gradient fail to be square integrable. It establishes scale-explicit lower bounds for gauge-invariant L2 pressure oscillation and local L2 pressure gradient mass in shrinking terminal cylinders, with the accumulated pressure work limsup at least m/2 after every fixed restart.
AI.conclusion: The authors identify a necessary pressure-work mechanism linking endpoint atoms to local pressure concentration, generated solely by the incompressibility constraint, without requiring a full regularity hypothesis. This provides a new structural constraint on potential singularities in 3D Navier-Stokes flows.

title: Ultracontractivity of heat semigroups with non-local Robin boundary conditions via two-sided bounds for a positive eigenfunction
summary: We study heat semigroups on bounded Lipschitz domains $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^{d}$ with dimension $d>2$ under non-local Robin boundary conditions. The boundary operator $B \in \mathcal{L}( \mathrm{L}^{2}(\partialΩ))$ is allowed to destroy the positivity of the semigroup. We assume that there exists a positive operator $C \in \mathcal{L}(\mathrm{L}^{2}(\partialΩ))$ such that $$ |Bu| \leq C|u| \quad\text{for every }u\in \mathrm{L}^{2}(\partialΩ), \qquad C{\bf 1}\in \mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\partialΩ). $$ Under this assumption, we prove that the semigroup generated by the corresponding uniformly elliptic operator is ultracontractive. More precisely, its norm from $\mathrm{L}^{2}(Ω)$ to $\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(Ω)$ has short-time order $t^{-d/4}$. The main step is the construction of a positive eigenfunction $φ$ of a dominating elliptic operator such that $$ 0 \ < \ δ\ \leq \ φ\ \leq \ M $$ almost everywhere in $Ω$. The upper bound is obtained by power truncations and an iteration of Sobolev exponents. The lower bound follows by comparison with the Neumann semigroup. The two-sided estimate gives an $\mathrm{L}^{\infty}$-bound for the comparison semigroup. Nash's inequality and duality then yield ultracontractivity.

AI.tldr: This paper proves ultracontractivity for heat semigroups on bounded Lipschitz domains with non-local Robin boundary conditions, where the boundary operator may destroy positivity. Under a domination assumption by a positive operator, the semigroup generated by a uniformly elliptic operator is shown to have L²→L∞ norm with short-time order t^{-d/4}, for d>2.
AI.motivation: To extend ultracontractivity results to heat semigroups with non-local Robin boundary conditions where the boundary operator can destroy positivity, which is a more general and challenging setting than classical positive Robin boundary conditions.
AI.method: The proof constructs a positive eigenfunction φ of a dominating elliptic operator with two-sided bounds (0 < δ ≤ φ ≤ M). The upper bound uses power truncations and iteration of Sobolev exponents; the lower bound uses comparison with the Neumann semigroup. These bounds give an L∞-bound for the comparison semigroup, and ultracontractivity follows via Nash's inequality and duality.
AI.result: The heat semigroup generated by the uniformly elliptic operator is ultracontractive, with norm from L²(Ω) to L∞(Ω) having short-time order t^{-d/4} on bounded Lipschitz domains with d > 2.
AI.conclusion: Ultracontractivity holds even when the non-local Robin boundary operator destroys positivity, provided there exists a positive dominating operator with the stated properties. The key technical achievement is the construction of a bounded-from-below-and-above positive eigenfunction for the dominating elliptic operator.

title: Inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equation in Fourier-Lebesgue and modulation spaces
summary: The purpose of this work is to provide a broader framework for analyzing the inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equation (INLS) \[iu_t + u_{xx} \pm |x|^{-b}|u|^{α-1}u=0, \quad 1<α< 5-2b\; \text{and}\; 0< b\leq 1/4.\] Specifically, we establish low-regularity well-posedness in the Fourier-Lebesgue $\widehat{L}^{p}$ spaces for $4/3<p<8$. The analysis is carried out differently for the cases $p<2$ and $p>2$. Primarily, in both cases, we prove global well-posedness for arbitrarily large initial data via the data decomposition method adapted for the Fourier-Lebesgue spaces. Furthermore, we obtain analogous results for INLS in modulation spaces $M^{p,p'}$ for $4/3<p<2$.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes low-regularity well-posedness for the inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equation (INLS) in Fourier-Lebesgue spaces, achieving global well-posedness for arbitrarily large initial data, with analogous results in modulation spaces.
AI.motivation: To provide a broader framework for analyzing the inhomogeneous nonlinear Schrödinger equation, extending well-posedness results to low-regularity Fourier-Lebesgue spaces where standard approaches may fail.
AI.method: The analysis is carried out differently for the cases p<2 and p>2 in Fourier-Lebesgue spaces, using a data decomposition method adapted for these spaces. Similar results are obtained in modulation spaces M^{p,p'} for 4/3<p<2.
AI.result: Global well-posedness is proven for arbitrarily large initial data in Fourier-Lebesgue spaces for 4/3<p<8, with analogous results established in modulation spaces.
AI.conclusion: The paper extends the well-posedness theory for INLS to broader function spaces and demonstrates the effectiveness of the data decomposition method in Fourier-Lebesgue and modulation spaces.

title: Tumor boundary instability induced by pressure feedback
summary: We consider a Hele--Shaw-type tumor growth model obtained from the incompressible limit of a porous-medium equation. The limiting model preserves the patch structure of the tumor density and therefore admits a single free-boundary formulation. We investigate how a pressure-feedback parameter associated with the homeostatic pressure affects boundary stability. Using asymptotic analysis, we study boundary perturbations of finite-radius tumors and planar traveling fronts and derive the corresponding stability criteria. For planar fronts, the stability thresholds are further shown to be bifurcation points from which nonsymmetric traveling waves emerge. Our results indicate that pressure feedback can induce boundary instability in parameter regimes where the model without pressure feedback remains stable.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes boundary stability in a Hele-Shaw-type tumor growth model derived from the incompressible limit of a porous-medium equation. Using asymptotic analysis on finite-radius tumors and planar traveling fronts, the authors derive stability criteria and show that pressure feedback can induce boundary instability in regimes where the model without feedback remains stable.
AI.motivation: To understand how a pressure-feedback parameter (associated with homeostatic pressure) affects boundary stability in tumor growth models, and to identify parameter regimes where pressure feedback can destabilize otherwise stable tumor boundaries.
AI.method: The authors employ asymptotic analysis to study boundary perturbations of (1) finite-radius tumors and (2) planar traveling fronts. They derive stability criteria for both configurations and identify bifurcation points where nonsymmetric traveling waves emerge from planar fronts.
AI.result: Stability criteria are derived for both finite-radius tumors and planar traveling fronts. The stability thresholds for planar fronts are shown to be bifurcation points from which nonsymmetric traveling waves emerge. Pressure feedback is found to induce boundary instability in parameter regimes where the model without feedback remains stable.
AI.conclusion: Pressure feedback can destabilize tumor boundaries in regimes where the standard model (without feedback) is stable, highlighting the importance of accounting for homeostatic pressure effects in tumor growth modeling and stability analysis.

title: An Almgren-type formula for planar $p$-harmonic functions
comment: 23 Pages. This manuscript is more of a small observation than a research article with new findings and has been under submission for months. The author initially decided against posting it on arXiv, but recently did so after some encouragement from Kai Xu
summary:
For a nonconstant planar $p$-harmonic function $u$, with $1 < p < \infty$, and according to previous results, most notably Aronsson's fundamental analysis of the hodograph representation in a neighborhood of an isolated critical point, we introduce the flux-normalized frequency $$
  N_*(x_0,r) = \frac{r\displaystyle\int_{B_r(x_0)} |D u|^p\,dx} {\displaystyle\int_{\partial B_r(x_0)} |D u|^{p-2}(u-u(x_0))^2\,dS}. $$ This ratio constitutes the natural counterpart of Almgren's frequency function in the nonlinear setting, as it recovers precisely the degree of homogeneity for every homogeneous $p$-harmonic profile. We further establish the corresponding gauge-corrected version of Almgren-type monotonicity and reinterpret, in terms of the frequency function, the classical planar unique continuation property. In addition, we derive a quantitative pinching estimate for the flux-normalized frequency and identify the specific obstruction that prevents a straightforward extension of the method to higher dimensions.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a flux-normalized frequency function for planar p-harmonic functions that serves as the nonlinear counterpart to Almgren's frequency function, recovering exact homogeneity degrees and establishing Almgren-type monotonicity with quantitative pinching estimates.
AI.motivation: To develop a natural frequency function for p-harmonic functions in the planar case that can capture homogeneity and monotonicity properties analogous to those in the linear (p=2) setting, building on Aronsson's work on hodograph representations near isolated critical points.
AI.method: The authors introduce a flux-normalized frequency ratio N_*(x_0,r) that normalizes the integral of |Du|^p over balls by a weighted boundary integral involving (u-u(x_0))^2, drawing on the hodograph representation for planar p-harmonic functions to establish the gauge-corrected Almgren-type monotonicity and pinching estimates.
AI.result: The flux-normalized frequency exactly recovers the degree of homogeneity for homogeneous p-harmonic profiles, yields a gauge-corrected Almgren-type monotonicity, provides a reinterpretation of the planar unique continuation property, and produces a quantitative pinching estimate—while identifying obstructions preventing extension to higher dimensions.
AI.conclusion: The flux-normalized frequency function provides a correct nonlinear analog of Almgren's frequency for planar p-harmonic functions, enabling monotonicity and unique continuation analysis, though its extension to higher dimensions faces specific structural obstructions.

title: Conservation Laws with Discontinuous Flux: A First Application to Traffic Flow
summary: This work provides a traffic flow interpretation of the model recently introduced in \cite{ABS2025}. We adapt the conservation law with discontinuous gradient-dependent flux to a macroscopic traffic setting, assuming concave flux functions $f(u)$ and $g(u)$ defined on the density domain $[0,u_{\max}]$. To prevent violations of the maximal density constraint, we introduce modified Riemann Solvers tailored to this setting and generalize the existence theory for weak solutions developed in \cite{ABS2025}. Finally, we construct Riemann Solvers for a broader two-phase model incorporating a free-flow regime, in which $f(u)=g(u)$ on a subset of $[0,u_{\max}]$, and establish existence of weak solutions in this more general framework.

AI.tldr: This work reinterprets a previously introduced conservation law with discontinuous gradient-dependent flux in the context of macroscopic traffic flow, adapting it to concave flux functions on a bounded density domain. It introduces modified Riemann Solvers to enforce the maximal density constraint, extends the existence theory for weak solutions, and generalizes the framework to a two-phase model with a free-flow regime.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to bridge a theoretical model (conservation law with discontinuous gradient-dependent flux) to practical macroscopic traffic modeling, while ensuring physically meaningful constraints (e.g., maximal density) are respected. It seeks to broaden the applicability and theoretical foundations of the model.
AI.method: The authors adapt the conservation law to a traffic flow setting with concave flux functions f(u) and g(u) on [0, u_max]. They introduce modified Riemann Solvers to prevent violation of the maximal density constraint, generalize the existing weak solution existence theory, and construct Riemann Solvers for a broader two-phase model where f(u)=g(u) on a subset of the density domain.
AI.result: The paper establishes existence of weak solutions for the adapted traffic flow model with discontinuous gradient-dependent flux, including the broader two-phase model with a free-flow regime where f(u)=g(u) on a subset of the density domain.
AI.conclusion: The adapted model and modified Riemann Solvers provide a consistent macroscopic traffic flow interpretation of the original conservation law, with a generalized existence theory that accommodates both the standard setting and a broader two-phase model with free-flow regimes.

title: Necessity of Ladyzhenskaya \& Ural'tseva's sufficient conditions in nonuniform ellipticity
summary: The sufficient conditions of Ladyzhenskaya \& Ural'tseva \cite{lu70} for interior gradient estimates in nonuniformly elliptic problems are found to be also necessary. Specifically, nonparametric minimal surfaces exhibit the maximal nonuniformity rate compatible with the local Lipschitz regularity of solutions, and the classical theory of Finn \cite{fin54} and Bombieri \& De Giorgi \& Miranda \cite{bdm69} doesn't extend beyond Bernstein genre $2$.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that the sufficient conditions established by Ladyzhenskaya & Ural'tseva for interior gradient estimates in nonuniformly elliptic problems are also necessary. The authors show that nonparametric minimal surfaces represent the maximal nonuniformity rate for local Lipschitz regularity, and that the classical theory of Finn and Bombieri-De Giorgi-Miranda cannot be extended beyond Bernstein genre 2.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to close the gap between sufficient and necessary conditions for interior gradient estimates in nonuniformly elliptic problems, thereby determining the sharp boundary of applicability for the classical regularity theory.
AI.method: The authors analyze the structural conditions of Ladyzhenskaya & Ural'tseva for nonuniformly elliptic equations and demonstrate their necessity by constructing or identifying counterexamples that saturate the constraints, particularly using nonparametric minimal surfaces as extremal cases.
AI.result: The findings show that the Ladyzhenskaya-Ural'tseva conditions are both sufficient and necessary. Nonparametric minimal surfaces achieve the maximal allowed nonuniformity rate for local Lipschitz regularity, and the Finn and Bombieri-De Giorgi-Miranda theories are sharp, not extending beyond Bernstein genre 2.
AI.conclusion: The classical regularity theory for nonuniformly elliptic problems is optimal: the known sufficient conditions are necessary, and the existing results on minimal surfaces cannot be improved beyond Bernstein genre 2.

title: Entire monotone solutions of the anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation in dimension 5
summary: In this paper, we consider the anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation $-\operatorname{div} a(Du)+W'(u)=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, where $a(p):=DH(p)$ with $H(p)=\frac{1}{2}F(p)^2$ and $F$ a uniformly elliptic integrand, and $W(u)=\frac{1}{4}(1-u^2)^2$. Based on the Mooney-Yang anisotropic minimal graph, we prove that the anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation admits a stable solution for $N\geq4$ in the weak sense, whose level sets are not hyperplanes. As a byproduct, we also construct a smooth solution of the above anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation for $N\geq5$ that is monotone in one direction but is not one-dimensional.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs stable solutions to the anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation in R^N for N≥4 whose level sets are not hyperplanes, and monotone-but-not-one-dimensional smooth solutions for N≥5, using Mooney-Yang anisotropic minimal graphs.
AI.motivation: To extend the classical De Giorgi conjecture and related rigidity results for the isotropic Allen-Cahn equation to the anisotropic setting, demonstrating that low-dimensional rigidity fails in higher dimensions.
AI.method: The authors leverage the Mooney-Yang anisotropic minimal graph construction, which provides examples of stable (or strictly stable) minimal hypersurfaces that are not hyperplanes in R^N for N≥4. By using these minimal graphs as level sets via a profile function, they build solutions to the anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation with the required properties.
AI.result: For N≥4, stable solutions to the anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation exist in the weak sense with non-planar level sets. Additionally, for N≥5, smooth solutions that are monotone in one direction but not one-dimensional are constructed.
AI.conclusion: The anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation admits counterexamples to rigidity conjectures analogous to De Giorgi's in sufficiently high dimensions, showing the sharpness of dimension thresholds in the anisotropic setting.

title: On a pointwise estimate for a weighted rough singular integral operator in stratified Lie groups and applications
summary: In this article, we present a new pointwise estimate for a weighted rough singular integral operator in the setting of stratified Lie groups. This operator, $T_{Ω, \varpi}$, is based on a kernel $Ω$ and a weight $\varpi$, where the kernel satisfies a natural size condition and a cancellation property with respect to the weight $\varpi$. Moreover, we do not assume any kind of regularity on these objects. This weighted rough singular integral operator, applied to a function $f$, is estimated through a combination of information involving a weighted maximal function of the gradient of $f$ and a weighted Morrey space. We also deduce from this pointwise estimate some new weighted functional inequalities and, as an application, we obtain a uniqueness result for a rough version of the stationary Navier-Stokes equation over the Heisenberg group.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a new pointwise estimate for a weighted rough singular integral operator on stratified Lie groups, without assuming regularity on the kernel or weight. The estimate combines weighted maximal functions of the gradient with weighted Morrey spaces, yielding new weighted functional inequalities and a uniqueness result for a rough stationary Navier-Stokes equation on the Heisenberg group.
AI.motivation: To extend pointwise estimates for weighted rough singular integral operators to stratified Lie groups, removing regularity assumptions on the kernel and weight, and to derive applications including functional inequalities and uniqueness for Navier-Stokes equations.
AI.method: The authors construct a pointwise estimate for the operator $T_{\Omega,\varpi}$ using weighted maximal functions of the gradient of $f$ and weighted Morrey spaces, under only natural size and cancellation conditions on the kernel with respect to the weight.
AI.result: New weighted functional inequalities are deduced from the pointwise estimate, and a uniqueness result is obtained for a rough version of the stationary Navier-Stokes equation on the Heisenberg group.
AI.conclusion: The pointwise estimate provides a general framework for weighted rough singular integrals on stratified Lie groups, with meaningful applications to PDEs such as the stationary Navier-Stokes equation.

title: A block-Toeplitz approach to the spectrum of the Neumann-Poincaré operator on self-similar chains
summary: We characterise the spectrum of the Neumann-Poincaré operator acting on a mean-zero subspace of the Sobolev-Slobodeckij space $W^{s,p}(Γ)$, where $Γ$ is a non-Lipschitz domain, consisting of an infinite self-similar chain of disjoint smooth domains accumulating at a limit point. We exploit the discrete geometric scaling of the chain to obtain an exact block-Toeplitz representation of the Neumann-Poincaré operator, as well as the single- and double-layer operators. The corresponding operator-valued symbol depends entirely on the single scaling parameter $α=(d-1)/p-s$ and belongs to the Wiener algebra whenever $0<α<d$. This allows us to exploit block-Toeplitz operator theory to characterise the essential spectrum and Fredholm regions within this regime. In the energy space $H^{-1/2}_0(Γ)$, corresponding to $α= d/2$, we prove the spectrum is real and characterise any isolated eigenvalues outside the essential spectrum through an operator-valued Wiener-Hopf factorisation. Furthermore, we apply an operator-valued Szegő limit theorem to derive the asymptotic spectral distribution for large finite truncations and establish an eigenvalue counting formula based on the operator symbol. We illustrate these results through explicit analytical computations for a chain of concentric annuli and numerical approximations for a chain of disks.

AI.tldr: This paper characterizes the spectrum of the Neumann-Poincaré operator on a mean-zero subspace of the Sobolev-Slobodeckij space W^{s,p}(Γ), where Γ is a non-Lipschitz domain consisting of an infinite self-similar chain of disjoint smooth domains accumulating at a limit point. Using discrete geometric scaling, the authors obtain an exact block-Toeplitz representation of the operator, allowing them to characterize the essential spectrum and Fredholm regions, prove spectral properties in the energy space H^{-1/2}_0(Γ), and derive asymptotic spectral distributions via an operator-valued Szegő limit theorem.
AI.motivation: The Neumann-Poincaré operator is fundamental in potential theory and boundary integral equations, but its spectral behavior on non-Lipschitz domains (such as self-similar fractal-like chains) is largely unexplored. Understanding the spectrum on such domains is important for applications in scattering, electromagnetism, and elasticity where non-smooth boundaries naturally arise.
AI.method: The authors exploit the discrete geometric scaling of the infinite self-similar chain to obtain an exact block-Toeplitz representation of the Neumann-Poincaré, single-layer, and double-layer operators. The operator-valued symbol depends entirely on the scaling parameter α=(d-1)/p-s and belongs to the Wiener algebra for 0<α<d. They apply block-Toeplitz operator theory for essential spectrum/Fredholm characterization, operator-valued Wiener-Hopf factorization for isolated eigenvalues in the energy space, and an operator-valued Szegő limit theorem for asymptotic spectral distribution of finite truncations.
AI.result: The paper fully characterizes the essential spectrum and Fredholm regions for 0<α<d. In the energy space H^{-1/2}_0(Γ) (α=d/2), they prove the spectrum is real and characterize isolated eigenvalues outside the essential spectrum via Wiener-Hopf factorization. They establish an eigenvalue counting formula based on the operator symbol and illustrate results with explicit computations for a chain of concentric annuli and numerical approximations for a chain of disks.
AI.conclusion: The block-Toeplitz framework provides a complete spectral characterization of the Neumann-Poincaré operator on self-similar chain domains, demonstrating that the geometric scaling parameter α fully determines the spectral structure. The results extend spectral analysis of the Neumann-Poincaré operator to non-Lipschitz infinite self-similar geometries, with concrete computational tools for practical applications.

title: Revisiting Picard's proof of the Picard--Weber--Weck selection theorem
summary: Revisiting the rationale provided by Picard in the seminal paper [13], we provide an independent, self-contained proof of the Maxwell compactness property for weak Lipschitz domains in the Euclidean setting, detouring technical complications like the differential forms setting, Gaffney's inequality for smooth domains, Calderon's extension theorem or regularity theory for PDEs, or systems thereof, on smooth domains that are used in this context. As a by-product we provide an independent proof of the classical Gaffney estimate for cubes using only $L^2$-completeness of the Fourier bases.

AI.tldr: The paper provides an independent, self-contained proof of the Maxwell compactness property for weak Lipschitz domains in Euclidean space, avoiding technical machinery such as differential forms, Gaffney's inequality for smooth domains, Calderon's extension theorem, and PDE regularity theory. As a by-product, it offers a simple proof of the classical Gaffney estimate for cubes using only L²-completeness of Fourier bases.
AI.motivation: The authors revisit the seminal work by Picard and seek to provide a simpler, self-contained proof of the Maxwell compactness property for weak Lipschitz domains without relying on heavy technical tools commonly used in this context.
AI.method: The proof is built directly in the Euclidean setting, avoiding differential forms, smooth-domain approximations, extension theorems, and PDE regularity theory. The Gaffney estimate for cubes is derived using only L²-completeness of Fourier bases.
AI.result: An independent, self-contained proof of the Maxwell compactness property for weak Lipschitz domains is established, along with a new elementary proof of the Gaffney estimate for cubes.
AI.conclusion: The paper demonstrates that the Maxwell compactness property can be proven with significantly simpler tools than previously employed, making the result more accessible and independent of the classical technical framework.

title: Global smooth solutions to the inhomogeneous Landau-Fermi-Dirac equation
summary:
We consider the spatially inhomogeneous Landau-Fermi-Dirac equation with Coulomb potential, a quantum modification of the classical Landau equation for fermions. Mathematically, the Pauli exclusion principle manifests as an additional a priori $L^\infty$-bound for solutions. Using this bound, we propagate polynomial decay in velocity, yielding unconditional upper bounds on the local mass and energy densities, thereby ruling out the possibility of implosions in the hydrodynamic quantities. Combining this estimate with a modified mass spreading method that yields desaturation, we deduce the existence of global-in-time classical solutions for rough initial data with polynomial decay in velocity. This result stands in stark contrast to the theory for the classical Landau and Boltzmann equations, for which no comparable nonperturbative global existence result is known despite sustained effort.
  Our treatment is almost entirely self-contained, using only robust, generic estimates for linear kinetic equations. In particular, our proof of local existence, in contrast to prior works, more closely mirrors the theory for parabolic equations using weak solutions and simpler function spaces. It may provide a concise roadmap to organizing, adapting, and applying the various linear and nonlinear estimates to obtain well-posedness for kinetic equations.

AI.tldr: The paper proves global-in-time existence of classical solutions for the spatially inhomogeneous Landau-Fermi-Dirac equation with Coulomb potential for rough initial data with polynomial decay in velocity, exploiting the Pauli exclusion principle's inherent L∞ bound to rule out implosions and achieve desaturation.
AI.motivation: The classical Landau and Boltzmann equations lack comparable nonperturbative global existence results despite sustained effort. The quantum modification (Landau-Fermi-Dirac) offers a Pauli exclusion principle bound that may enable a breakthrough toward global well-posedness.
AI.method: The approach combines (1) propagation of polynomial decay in velocity using the a priori L∞ bound from Pauli exclusion to rule out implosions, and (2) a modified mass spreading method to achieve desaturation. The local existence proof uses weak solutions and simpler function spaces, more closely mirroring parabolic theory, relying only on robust generic estimates for linear kinetic equations.
AI.result: Global-in-time classical solutions are established for rough initial data with polynomial decay in velocity, with unconditional upper bounds on local mass and energy densities. This is a stark contrast to the classical Landau and Boltzmann equations, where no comparable result exists.
AI.conclusion: The treatment is almost entirely self-contained and may provide a concise roadmap for organizing, adapting, and applying linear and nonlinear estimates to obtain well-posedness results for kinetic equations more broadly.

title: Higher-order Approximate Symmetries
comment: Accepted to Ukrainian Mathematical Journal, W. Fushchych memorial issue
summary:
Fushchych and Shtelen defined approximate symmetry by expanding the solution of a perturbed differential equation in the small parameter, replacing the original equation by a triangular system for the expansion coefficients. We extend this construction to arbitrary order. A coefficient-map formulation yields the order-$p$ Fushchych--Shtelen (FS) system and establishes, under explicit hypotheses, a correspondence with the Baikov--Gazizov--Ibragimov (BGI) method.
  The two frameworks are compared for a perturbed cubic wave equation. Up to equivalences, we classify the nonlinearities admitting an FS dilation through second order. The classification consists of a generic power family and logarithmic branches at exceptional exponents. Among perturbations nontrivial at first order, vertical BGI continuations select a proper subfamily of one FS branch, and a second common branch arises when the perturbation first enters at second order; the two methods are related but not interchangeable. Joint reduction by the Lorentz algebra and the inherited FS dilation integrates all resulting FS normal forms; the explicit solutions of the 1989 Fushchych--Shtelen letter are recovered as the first-order members of this reduction. In the part common to both frameworks, the logarithmic corrections arise from the expansion of a power law with a perturbation-dependent exponent.
  Finally, periodic travelling waves are used to examine the long-scale validity of the FS expansion. The first correction is obtained by quadrature, the second-order secular structure is isolated, and phase renormalization produces bounded order-consistent approximations. For integer-power members of the generic family, the amplitude dependence of the corrected wavenumber agrees with the scaling weights obtained from the symmetry classification.

AI.tldr: This paper extends Fushchych-Shtelen (FS) approximate symmetry to arbitrary order, establishes its correspondence with the BGI method under explicit hypotheses, classifies nonlinearities admitting FS dilations for a perturbed cubic wave equation, and validates the framework via periodic travelling waves with phase renormalization.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to rigorously extend the FS approximate symmetry construction to arbitrary order and clarify its relationship with the competing BGI framework, which had only been partially understood. They also seek to classify admissible nonlinearities and test the practical validity of the expansion for physical applications.
AI.method: The method uses a coefficient-map formulation to derive the order-p FS system. The FS and BGI frameworks are compared via a perturbed cubic wave equation, with nonlinearities admitting FS dilations classified through second order. Joint reduction by the Lorentz algebra and inherited FS dilation integrates the normal forms. Periodic travelling waves, quadrature, and phase renormalization are used to assess long-scale validity.
AI.result: The classification yields a generic power family with logarithmic branches at exceptional exponents. The BGI and FS methods are related but not interchangeable: vertical BGI continuations select a proper subfamily of one FS branch, while a second common branch arises when perturbation enters at second order. Explicit 1989 FS solutions are recovered as first-order members. Phase renormalization yields bounded order-consistent approximations, and amplitude-dependent corrected wavenumbers match the symmetry-derived scaling weights for integer-power members.
AI.conclusion: The FS and BGI approximate symmetry methods are complementary but distinct frameworks; both are needed for a full picture. The FS approach is validated as practically useful through the travelling-wave analysis, with the logarithmic corrections traced to the expansion of a perturbation-dependent power-law exponent. The amplitude-wavenumber agreement confirms the physical relevance of the symmetry classification.

title: Stationary kinetic Krylov-Safonov estimates in space dimension one
summary: We prove interior Hölder regularity for solutions of the stationary kinetic Fokker-Planck equation in non-divergence form in space dimension one. The estimate is independent of any small-oscillation condition on the diffusion coefficient.

AI.tldr: The paper proves interior Hölder regularity for solutions of the stationary kinetic Fokker-Planck equation in non-divergence form in one spatial dimension, with an estimate that does not depend on any small-oscillation condition on the diffusion coefficient.

AI.method: The proof establishes interior Hölder regularity for the stationary kinetic Fokker-Planck equation in non-divergence form, specifically in one space dimension, with estimates independent of small-oscillation conditions on the diffusion coefficient.

title: Finite-energy spacetimes with torus symmetry. Cauchy stability of Einstein-Euler and Einstein-Navier-Stokes areal flows
comment: This paper includes some estimates from version 1 of arXiv:2605.31585 for completeness
summary: We establish finite-energy Cauchy stability for vacuum and matter spacetimes with $T^2$ symmetry on $T^3$, under general constitutive equations satisfying hyperbolicity and mild asymptotic conditions at vacuum and large mass-energy density. First, using the area of the symmetry orbits as a time function, we introduce the JKL formulation of Einstein areal flows}, a first-order evolution-constraint system coupling a wave-map structure for the geometry to hyperbolic matter balance laws and weighted transport equations for the twists and the momentum tangent to the symmetry orbits. Second, we also define two classes of hyperbolic Einstein-Navier-Stokes models, constructed from (as we call them) a Navier-Stokes potential and a relaxation rate map. The proposed particle-production model has divergence-free matter stress and non-negative particle-number production, while the proposed dissipated-energy model conserves particle number and dissipates fluid mass-energy, while an auxiliary stress restores the total stress-energy conservation required by the contracted Bianchi identity. For regular finite-energy (Einstein, Euler, Navier-Stokes) flows, we establish maximum and invariant-domain principles, geometric and energy monotonicity formulas, spacelike and timelike energy estimates, and total-variation estimates. Third, together, these estimates yield finite-energy Cauchy stability in the future expanding regime and, in the contracting regime, until the spacelike volume collapses. They are independent of the viscosity (or relaxation) mechanisms and cover vacuum, unbounded mass-energy density, and arbitrary finite rapidity. They also extend to weakly regular Einstein-Euler areal flows satisfying a reference mathematical entropy inequality.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes finite-energy Cauchy stability for spacetimes with T^2 symmetry on T^3 in both vacuum and matter cases, using the JKL formulation of Einstein areal flows and introducing hyperbolic Einstein-Navier-Stokes models, with stability results that are independent of viscosity and cover extreme physical regimes.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous finite-energy Cauchy stability results for Einstein areal flows with T^2 symmetry under general constitutive equations, covering both vacuum and matter spacetimes, and to develop a framework that handles realistic matter models including viscous (Navier-Stokes-like) effects while maintaining hyperbolicity.
AI.method: The paper introduces the JKL formulation of Einstein areal flows using orbit area as a time function, creating a first-order evolution-constraint system with wave-map structure, hyperbolic matter balance laws, and weighted transport equations. It also defines two hyperbolic Einstein-Navier-Stokes models via a Navier-Stokes potential and relaxation rate map, then derives estimates including maximum principles, invariant-domain principles, energy monotonicity formulas, and total-variation estimates.
AI.result: The paper establishes maximum and invariant-domain principles, geometric and energy monotonicity formulas, spacelike/timelike energy estimates, and total-variation estimates for regular finite-energy flows. These yield finite-energy Cauchy stability in the future expanding regime and in the contracting regime until spacelike volume collapse, independent of viscosity mechanisms, covering vacuum, unbounded mass-energy density, and arbitrary finite rapidity, with extensions to weakly regular Einstein-Euler flows.
AI.conclusion: Finite-energy Cauchy stability is achieved for T^2-symmetric spacetimes under very general matter models, demonstrating that the stability results are robust across different constitutive equations and remain valid even with unbounded energy density and in viscous regimes, with the framework also applicable to weakly regular Einstein-Euler flows satisfying a reference entropy inequality.

title: Exponential mixing for the stochastic Navier--Stokes equation with localized noise
summary: This paper studies the 2D Navier--Stokes equation on a bounded domain with Navier-slip boundary conditions, driven by spatially localized stationary forcing generated by a stochastic heat equation. We prove exponential mixing for the associated Navier--Stokes--heat system, and consequently exponential convergence of the velocity law under stationary forcing. The main difficulty is that the white noise is confined to a subdomain and reaches the velocity indirectly through the heat component. To address the degeneracy, the proof combines Malliavin calculus with PDE control theory. The key ingredient is a stabilization scheme that converts localized Navier--Stokes controls into time-regular controls compatible with the heat dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper proves exponential mixing for a 2D Navier-Stokes equation with Navier-slip boundary conditions driven by stationary stochastic forcing generated by a heat equation, where the noise is localized to a subdomain. The proof combines Malliavin calculus with PDE control theory via a stabilization scheme that converts localized controls into time-regular ones.
AI.motivation: To establish exponential mixing (and hence exponential convergence of the velocity law) for the 2D Navier-Stokes system under stationary stochastic forcing, despite the difficulty that white noise is confined to a subdomain and reaches the velocity only indirectly through the heat component—a degeneracy that complicates standard ergodic analysis.
