title: Clustering versus sorting: a mass-conserving reaction-diffusion model of planar polarity puncta
summary: Planar cell polarity is preceded by the clustering of polarity proteins into discrete, low-turnover membrane subdomains (puncta), yet the minimal interactions that nucleate puncta, set their number, and segregate opposite orientations remain unclear. We address these questions with a mass-conserving reaction-diffusion model in which two diffusible monomers bind reversibly across a cell-cell junction into trans-complexes of two orientations, with feedback entering only through concentration-dependent rates. Above a critical density, the uniform state undergoes a long-wavelength mass-redistribution instability rather than a finite-wavelength Turing bifurcation. The form of the feedback then selects between two morphologies: broad mesas fixed by a Maxwell construction under saturating feedback, and narrow mass-limited spikes under unbounded feedback. For spikes we obtain closed-form expressions exhibiting a clean separation of amplitude (mass and feedback), width (the complex diffusion length), and spacing (the monomer screening length). Within a fast-monomer reduction we prove, for any number and arrangement of puncta, that like-oriented arrays coarsen, so multiplicity is metastable and kinetically determined. The second monomer reservoir introduces a second screening length that rate-limits competition by the harmonic mean of the monomer diffusivities, and the spectrum of a punctum remains free of oscillatory ("blinking") instabilities throughout. Finally, sign-definite cross-modulation of turnover converts clustering into orientation sorting - the mutual exclusion of orientations along a single contact: mass redistribution sets puncta number, and the sign of the cross-coupling determines whether orientations segregate. Puncta number and orientation sorting are thus governed by mathematically separable ingredients.

AI.tldr: A mass-conserving reaction-diffusion model explains how planar cell polarity protein puncta nucleate, determine their number, and segregate orientations through long-wavelength instabilities and feedback-selected morphologies.
AI.motivation: To understand the minimal interactions that nucleate polarity protein puncta, set their number, and segregate opposite orientations in planar cell polarity, since these remain unclear.
AI.method: Mass-conserving reaction-diffusion model with two diffusible monomers binding reversibly across cell-cell junctions into trans-complexes of two orientations, with concentration-dependent feedback rates.
AI.result: Above critical density, a long-wavelength mass-redistribution instability occurs (not Turing). Feedback selects between broad mesas and narrow mass-limited spikes. For spikes, closed-form expressions separate amplitude, width, and spacing. Like-oriented arrays coarsen (multiplicity is metastable). A second monomer introduces a rate-limiting screening length. No oscillatory instabilities occur. Sign-definite cross-modulation converts clustering into orientation sorting.
AI.conclusion: Puncta number and orientation sorting are governed by mathematically separable ingredients: mass redistribution sets puncta number, while the sign of cross-coupling determines whether orientations segregate.

title: A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations
summary: We study the periodic fractional stochastic Burgers equation $(\partial_t+Λ^γ)u=\partial_x(u^2)+|\partial_x|^{1-α}ξ$, where $1<γ\leq 2$ and $ξ$ is space-time white noise. Under the condition $α>\max{(7-4γ)/2,(15-8γ)/6}$, we establish pathwise $L^1$, energy, and Besov estimates for a transformed remainder. The argument combines a response decomposition with a conservative Zvonkin transformation. For $1<γ<2$, this produces a compensated nonlocal diffusion operator whose coercivity is coupled to a cubic-increment estimate adapted from the modified Karman--Howarth--Monin argument.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the periodic fractional stochastic Burgers equation with space-time white noise, establishing pathwise L1, energy, and Besov estimates for a transformed remainder under specific conditions on the fractional Laplacian exponent γ and noise parameter α. The approach combines a response decomposition with a conservative Zvonkin transformation, and for 1<γ<2 introduces a compensated nonlocal diffusion operator with coercivity coupled to a cubic-increment estimate from the modified Karman-Howarth-Monin argument.
AI.motivation: To obtain existence, uniqueness, and regularity estimates for the fractional stochastic Burgers equation with space-time white noise, which is a challenging object due to the combination of nonlinearity, fractional dissipation, and rough noise forcing. The transformed remainder allows for pathwise control of the solution's regularity.
AI.method: The method combines a response decomposition with a conservative Zvonkin transformation to transform the equation into a form where a compensated nonlocal diffusion operator emerges. For 1<γ<2, coercivity of this operator is established via a cubic-increment estimate adapted from the modified Karman-Howarth-Monin argument, yielding pathwise L1, energy, and Besov estimates.
AI.result: Under the condition α > max((7-4γ)/2, (15-8γ)/6), the paper establishes pathwise L1, energy, and Besov estimates for the transformed remainder of the periodic fractional stochastic Burgers equation where 1<γ≤2.
AI.conclusion: The established estimates provide a rigorous framework for analyzing the periodic fractional stochastic Burgers equation with space-time white noise, with the condition on α characterizing the admissible parameter regime where the analysis holds.

title: Sharp monotonicity for closed three-manifolds with positive scalar curvature
summary: We prove two sharp monotonicity formulae for the natural Green's function of a closed three-manifold with positive scalar curvature, analogous to the Munteanu-Wang theorem for non-negative scalar curvature. We also show that both results may be interpreted as the monotonicity of a suitably defined "enclosed mass" of the sublevel sets of Green's function in the corresponding "conformal" blow-up of the manifold.

AI.tldr: The paper proves two sharp monotonicity formulae for the Green's function on closed 3-manifolds with positive scalar curvature, analogous to the Munteanu-Wang theorem, and interprets both results as monotonicity of an "enclosed mass" for sublevel sets in the conformal blow-up.
AI.motivation: To extend the Munteanu-Wang theorem (originally for non-negative scalar curvature) to the positive scalar curvature setting, and to provide a geometric/physical interpretation of these monotonicity results via an "enclosed mass" quantity.
AI.method: The paper establishes two sharp monotonicity formulae for the natural Green's function on closed 3-manifolds with positive scalar curvature, and interprets both via the "conformal" blow-up of the manifold where the monotonicity is expressed in terms of an "enclosed mass" of sublevel sets.
AI.result: Two sharp monotonicity formulae are proven for Green's functions on closed 3-manifolds with positive scalar curvature, generalizing the Munteanu-Wang theorem, along with a mass-theoretic interpretation in the conformal blow-up.
AI.conclusion: The results provide sharp monotonicity formulae in the positive scalar curvature case and give a mass-based interpretation of the sublevel sets of Green's function in the conformal blow-up, mirroring and extending the known non-negative scalar curvature results.

title: One-dimensional Feynman--Kac regularity under the Engelbert--Schmidt conditions
summary: Let $X$ be a time-homogeneous one-dimensional diffusion whose coefficients satisfy the Engelbert--Schmidt conditions, and let $q$ be a bounded potential. We show that the associated Feynman--Kac semigroup is smooth in time and $C^1$ in space, with a locally absolutely continuous first spatial derivative; the Kolmogorov equation holds almost everywhere. If the drift, second-order coefficient, and potential are continuous, the Feynman--Kac value is $C^{1,2}$ in the interior. Thus, in the time-homogeneous one-dimensional setting, continuity suffices for interior $C^{1,2}$ regularity. We identify the corresponding semigroups with the killed and reflected Feynman--Kac functionals, treat nonzero, time-independent Dirichlet data, and give examples showing the sharpness of the continuity assumptions and the failure of the corresponding statement in two dimensions.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes interior C^{1,2} regularity for Feynman–Kac semigroups associated with time-homogeneous one-dimensional diffusions under only continuity assumptions on the drift, diffusion coefficient, and potential, showing sharpness of these assumptions and failure in two dimensions.
AI.motivation: To determine the minimal regularity conditions under which Feynman–Kac semigroups possess classical differentiability properties (C^{1,2} in space-time) for one-dimensional diffusions, and to understand whether continuity alone suffices in this setting.
AI.method: The authors analyze time-homogeneous one-dimensional diffusions under Engelbert–Schmidt conditions, study the associated Feynman–Kac semigroup's regularity, and identify it with killed and reflected Feynman–Kac functionals. They handle nonzero time-independent Dirichlet data and construct counterexamples to test sharpness.
AI.result: The Feynman–Kac semigroup is shown to be smooth in time and C^1 in space with locally absolutely continuous first spatial derivative; the Kolmogorov equation holds almost everywhere. When coefficients are continuous, interior C^{1,2} regularity holds. Counterexamples demonstrate sharpness of continuity assumptions and failure of the analogous result in two dimensions.
AI.conclusion: In the time-homogeneous one-dimensional setting, continuity of coefficients suffices for interior C^{1,2} regularity of Feynman–Kac values, but this statement does not extend to higher dimensions.

title: The symmetric maximal surface equation
summary: We establish the existence of smooth solutions to the symmetric maximal surface equation with degenerate boundary conditions. Moreover, we prove that these solutions maximize the associated area functionals. This result serves as the Lorentzian analogue of minimal graphs in hyperbolic spaces together with their associated area minimizing problem.

AI.tldr: The paper proves the existence of smooth solutions to the symmetric maximal surface equation with degenerate boundary conditions, and shows these solutions maximize the associated area functionals, providing the Lorentzian analogue of minimal graphs in hyperbolic spaces.
AI.motivation: To establish existence and area-maximizing properties for solutions of the symmetric maximal surface equation with degenerate boundary conditions, completing the Lorentzian counterpart to the classical minimal surface problem in hyperbolic spaces.
AI.method: Analytical techniques are used to prove existence of smooth solutions to the symmetric maximal surface equation under degenerate boundary conditions, followed by a proof that these solutions maximize the associated area functionals.
AI.result: Smooth solutions exist for the symmetric maximal surface equation with degenerate boundary conditions, and these solutions achieve maximal area among admissible competitors.
AI.conclusion: The existence of smooth maximal surface solutions with degenerate boundary data is established, and their area-maximizing property is proven, thus serving as the Lorentzian analogue of minimal graphs in hyperbolic spaces.

title: Band edges of periodic Schrödinger operators are generically isolated and nondegenerate
summary: For periodic Schrödinger operators $H_V=-Δ+V$ with bounded real-valued potentials on $\mathbb R^d$ with $d\ge2$, we show that for generic potentials, each endpoint of every spectral gap is attained by a single Bloch band at only finitely many quasimomenta, and has a nondegenerate Hessian at every attaining point. This proves the Spectral Edge Conjecture for periodic Schrödinger operators.

AI.tldr: The paper proves the Spectral Edge Conjecture for periodic Schrödinger operators on R^d (d≥2), showing that for generic bounded real-valued potentials, each spectral gap endpoint is attained by a single Bloch band at finitely many quasimomenta with a nondegenerate Hessian at every attaining point.
AI.motivation: The Spectral Edge Conjecture addresses the structure of spectral edges (band edges) in periodic Schrödinger operators, which is fundamental to understanding the band structure of periodic media such as crystals. Understanding whether band extrema are simple, isolated, and have nondegenerate curvature is crucial for analyzing effective mass approximations, transport properties, and wave behavior in periodic potentials.
AI.method: The authors analyze periodic Schrödinger operators H_V = -Δ + V with bounded real-valued potentials on R^d for d≥2. They use a genericity argument to show that for generic potentials, the spectral edges have the desired properties—namely, that each edge is achieved by a unique Bloch band at finitely many quasimomenta, with nondegenerate Hessian at those points.
AI.result: The Spectral Edge Conjecture is proven for periodic Schrödinger operators: for generic potentials, every spectral gap endpoint is attained by a single Bloch band at only finitely many quasimomenta, and the Hessian at every attaining point is nondegenerate.
AI.conclusion: The Spectral Edge Conjecture holds for periodic Schrödinger operators in dimension d≥2. This confirms that generically, spectral edges behave well: they are simple band extrema occurring at isolated quasimomenta with nondegenerate curvature.

title: Failure of the Proposed Local Decay Formula for Local Arnold Multiplicities under Twisted Kähler--Ricci Flow
summary: Let $λ(u,x)$ be the local Arnold multiplicity of a quasi-plurisubharmonic function $u$. Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu asked whether every maximal weak solution $\varphi_t$ of the twisted Kähler--Ricci flow satisfies $λ(\varphi_t,x)=\max\{λ(\varphi_0,x)-t,0\}$. We give counterexamples on the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e=\mathbb P_{\mathbb P^1} (\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}\oplus\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-e))$, $e\ge2$. Let $S$ be its negative section and $F_1,\ldots,F_k$ be distinct fibres. If $a,b_i>0$, $\sum_i b_i>ea$, and the initial current is $a[S]+\sum_i b_i[F_i]$, then $λ(\varphi_t,x)=a-\min\{k/e,1\}t$ for $x\in S\setminus\bigcup_iF_i$ and $0<t<\min\{a,b_1,\ldots,b_k\}$. Thus the formula fails for $k<e$; the slower decay is forced by the Zariski negative part of the residual class. Under explicit SNC and positivity hypotheses, we also prove an exact surface formula for pure divisorial data. Consequences include nonlocality with fixed background data and explicit multiplier ideals. Products with smooth factors give counterexamples in every complex dimension $n\ge2$.

AI.tldr: The paper provides counterexamples to a conjecture by Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu about the decay of local Arnold multiplicity under the twisted Kähler--Ricci flow, using the negative section of Hirzebruch surfaces, and proves an exact formula for pure divisorial data under SNC assumptions.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses an open question from Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu about whether the local Arnold multiplicity λ(φ_t,x) of maximal weak solutions to the twisted Kähler--Ricci flow follows the simple decay formula max{λ(φ_0,x)-t, 0}. Understanding this behavior is important for the singularity analysis of degenerate complex Monge--Ampère flows.
AI.method: The authors construct explicit counterexamples on Hirzebruch surfaces F_e (e≥2) using current data a[S]+Σ b_i[F_i] where S is the negative section and F_i are distinct fibres. They analyze the local Arnold multiplicity at points on S away from the fibres, deriving the modified decay rate a - min{k/e, 1}t. They also prove an exact surface formula for pure divisorial data under explicit SNC (simple normal crossing) and positivity hypotheses.
AI.result: The conjectured formula λ(φ_t,x)=max{λ(φ_0,x)-t,0} fails for k<e fibres, where the decay is slower. The slower decay is forced by the Zariski negative part of the residual class. Consequences include nonlocality with fixed background data and explicit computation of multiplier ideals. Products with smooth factors extend counterexamples to all dimensions n≥2.
AI.conclusion: The paper refutes the Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu conjecture in general, showing that the local Arnold multiplicity decay under twisted Kähler--Ricci flow is more subtle than initially conjectured, with Zariski negative components playing a crucial role. For pure divisorial data with SNC hypotheses, an exact surface formula holds, providing a positive result within a restricted class.

title: On the discrete spectrum of Dirac operators with Lorentz-scalar $δ$-shell interactions supported on unbounded curves
summary: We consider the massive Dirac operator (with positive mass) in the plane with an attractive Lorentz-scalar $δ$-shell interaction of strength $τ\in(-\infty,0)\setminus\{-2\}$ supported on a $C^\infty$-smooth curve $Σ\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ being a local deformation of the broken line. This singular interaction is defined by imposing a suitable transmission condition on the curve $Σ$ in the operator domain. Such a Dirac operator is self-adjoint and has a gap in the essential spectrum, whose size is explicit and depends on the mass and the interaction strength. We show that the number of discrete eigenvalues in the gap is finite. Under the assumption that one of the domains bounded by $Σ$ is convex, we prove that the corresponding Dirac operator has a non-empty discrete spectrum, provided that $τ$ is either sufficiently small or sufficiently large in absolute value. The result holds for any perturbation of a broken line of any opening angle as described above, and this discrete spectrum is induced by the geometry, since for the same type of a singular interaction supported on the straight line the discrete spectrum is empty.

AI.tldr: The paper studies a massive Dirac operator in the plane with an attractive Lorentz-scalar δ-shell interaction on a smooth curve that is a local deformation of a broken line. It proves the discrete spectrum in the gap is finite and non-empty (when one bounded domain is convex and the interaction strength is either sufficiently small or large), with eigenvalues induced purely by geometry.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to understand how geometry affects the discrete spectrum of Dirac operators with singular interactions, specifically whether local deformations of a broken line (a non-straight configuration) can produce discrete eigenvalues in the spectral gap, in contrast to the straight line case where no such spectrum exists.
AI.method: The Dirac operator with an attractive Lorentz-scalar δ-shell interaction on a C∞-smooth curve (a local deformation of a broken line) is defined via a transmission condition. The self-adjointness and spectral gap are characterized, then the discrete spectrum is analyzed using geometric assumptions (convexity of a bounded domain) and perturbation arguments in the interaction strength τ.
AI.result: The number of discrete eigenvalues in the spectral gap is finite. When one of the domains bounded by Σ is convex, the discrete spectrum is non-empty for τ sufficiently small or sufficiently large in absolute value. This holds for any perturbation of a broken line of any opening angle, and the spectrum is geometry-induced since the straight-line case has empty discrete spectrum.
AI.conclusion: The geometry of the curve (a deformation of a broken line) is responsible for generating a non-empty discrete spectrum in the spectral gap of the Dirac operator, unlike the case of a straight line support, where no discrete spectrum exists.

title: Ancient cylindrical flows with fast or slow convergence
summary: In a recent breakthrough, Bamler-Lai proved the mean-convex neighborhood conjecture in all dimensions by showing that any nontrivial ancient asymptotically cylindrical mean curvature flow is -- up to splitting Euclidean factors -- either a translating bowl, or an ancient oval, or a translating oval-bowl. In this paper, we provide a short alternative argument for two of the three scenarios. Specifically, using more elementary/traditional methods, we show that if the convergence to the round cylinder is fast then the solution is a bowl times a Euclidean factor, and if the convergence is slow then the solution is an ancient oval. Moreover, the present paper also yields a new proof of the mean-convex neighborhood conjecture for neck-singularities that substantially simplifies and streamlines the approach from our prior work joint with Hershkovits (Acta '22) and Hershkovits-White (Inventiones '22).

AI.tldr: This paper provides a short alternative proof for two of the three scenarios in the mean-convex neighborhood conjecture for mean curvature flow. Using elementary/traditional methods, the authors show that fast convergence to the round cylinder implies a bowl solution times a Euclidean factor, while slow convergence implies an ancient oval, significantly simplifying prior approaches.
AI.motivation: Bamler-Lai recently proved the mean-convex neighborhood conjecture in all dimensions. The authors aim to provide a more elementary and streamlined alternative argument for two of the three classification scenarios, and to substantially simplify prior work on neck-singularities.
AI.method: The paper uses more elementary/traditional methods (as opposed to the sophisticated techniques in Bamler-Lai's approach) to analyze the speed of convergence to the round cylinder. Fast convergence is shown to yield a translating bowl times a Euclidean factor, while slow convergence yields an ancient oval.
AI.result: The authors successfully provide an alternative proof covering two of the three scenarios in the conjecture: fast convergence leads to bowl-type solutions, and slow convergence leads to ancient ovals. They also give a new, substantially simplified proof of the mean-convex neighborhood conjecture for neck-singularities, improving upon their earlier work with Hershkovits and Hershkovits-White.
AI.conclusion: The paper offers a simplified and more accessible route to parts of the mean-convex neighborhood conjecture, complementing Bamler-Lai's result with elementary arguments and streamlining prior joint work on neck-singularities.

title: Sharp constants for weak estimates of Riesz Potentials when $0<s<\min\{n,2\}$
summary: In this paper we prove the sharp weak estimate for the Riesz potentials for $0<s<\min\{n,2\}$ $$\|I_{s}(f)\|_{L^{\frac{n}{n-s},\infty}}\leq γ_{n,s} v_n^{\frac{n-s}{n}}\frac{Γ(s/2)Γ((n+2-s)/2)}{Γ(n/2)}\|f\|_{L^1}.$$ where $γ_{n,s}=2^{-s}π^{-\frac{n}{2}}\frac{Γ(\frac{n-s}{2})}{Γ(\frac{s}{2})}$. The isoperimetric inequality for the Riesz capacity plays a crucial role in our approach.

AI.tldr: The paper proves a sharp weak-type estimate for Riesz potentials I_s on L^1 functions for 0 < s < min{n,2}, with the optimal constant expressed explicitly in terms of gamma functions.
AI.motivation: To establish the best possible (sharp) weak-type L^1 to L^{n/(n-s),∞} bound for Riesz potentials, filling a gap where only non-sharp estimates were known.
AI.method: The proof relies crucially on the isoperimetric inequality for Riesz capacity, which provides the geometric control needed to obtain the sharp constant.
AI.result: A sharp weak-type estimate is proven with explicit constant γ_{n,s} v_n^{(n-s)/n} Γ(s/2)Γ((n+2-s)/2)/Γ(n/2), valid for 0 < s < min{n,2}.
AI.conclusion: The sharp constant for the weak-type estimate of Riesz potentials is identified, with Riesz capacity isoperimetry being the key tool.

title: Finiteness and rigidity of optimal destabilizing subvarieties for the J-equation
summary: We prove that when the J-equation does not admit a smooth solution, there is always only a finite number of obstructing optimally destabilizing curves and divisors on compact Kähler manifolds of any dimension. For threefolds, this establishes the unconditional finiteness of all optimally destabilizing subvarieties. We moreover characterize the union of these optimal subvarieties, proving that they are contained in the locus where a natural continuity path loses local smooth compactness. Finally, to address subvarieties that are neither curves nor divisors, we prove a rigidity criterion which prevents optimal cycles from moving in compact one-parameter families, with further consequences for their deformation and symmetry properties.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that when the J-equation has no smooth solution, only finitely many optimally destabilizing curves and divisors exist on compact Kähler manifolds, establishes unconditional finiteness for all optimally destabilizing subvarieties on threefolds, characterizes their union via the loss of local smooth compactness in a continuity path, and proves a rigidity criterion preventing optimal cycles from moving in compact one-parameter families.
AI.motivation: The J-equation relates to the existence of certain canonical metrics on Kähler manifolds. When solutions fail to exist, instability is witnessed by "optimally destabilizing" subvarieties. Understanding the finiteness and structure of these obstructions is fundamental to the theory of stability in Kähler geometry, and prior work left open general statements about how many such obstructions can exist and how they behave.
AI.method: The authors prove finiteness results for obstructing optimally destabilizing curves and divisors using analytic and algebraic techniques. For threefolds, they combine these to obtain unconditional finiteness for all optimally destabilizing subvarieties. They characterize the union of optimal subvarieties by relating it to the locus where a natural continuity path fails to have local smooth compactness. A rigidity criterion is established to show optimal cycles cannot move in compact one-parameter families, with implications for deformation and symmetry.
AI.result: The paper establishes: (1) finiteness of optimally destabilizing curves and divisors whenever the J-equation lacks a smooth solution on compact Kähler manifolds of any dimension; (2) unconditional finiteness of all optimally destabilizing subvarieties on threefolds; (3) a characterization of the union of optimal subvarieties via non-compactness of a continuity path; (4) a rigidity criterion preventing optimal cycles from moving in compact one-parameter families, with further deformation and symmetry consequences.
AI.conclusion: Optimal destabilizing obstructions to the J-equation are fundamentally finite in number (for curves and divisors in all dimensions, and for all subvarieties in threefolds), geometrically localized (contained in the non-compactness locus of the continuity path), and rigid (cannot deform). These results provide a sharp structural description of how and where the J-equation fails to admit smooth solutions, deepening our understanding of Kähler stability.
